Withdraw. Pull the limbs and head in toward the shell. Its AC becomes −3. The head opening stays unsealed, so it can still snap at targets in front.
sections.Defenses: Saving throws gain +2 normally and +4 while withdrawn, including against mental attacks. While withdrawn, the guardian also gets an unmodified save against effects that usually allow none.
sections.Senses and movement: Infravision 90 feet in or out of water. It can float or remain submerged indefinitely and breathe in both water and air. It has its own language and has been heard speaking to tortle shamans.
sections.Red Curse: Always has at least one Legacy, with a 25% chance of two or more. Blend, Phase, Sight, Stone Shape, and Cure are common choices. Needs cinnabryl and is worth 1,000 extra XP per Legacy.

name: Krolli
otherStatistics: Hill or mountain. Rare, active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–12. Treasure M, with A listed for the community. Any alignment. Appearing 1d20. No magic resistance. Height 7–8 feet, wingspan 17–20 feet. Elite morale 13–14.
description: A lightly built, winged reptilian warrior. Krolli settle in isolated eyries and sometimes travel to trade or take mercenary work.

sections.Actions:
Ground attacks. Make two claws for 1d8+1 each and a bite for 1d6+1.
Airborne attacks. Make two front claws for 1d8+1 each, one rear claw for 1d10, and a bite for 1d6+1. Krolli can use this sequence against targets on the ground.
Weapons. About 30% fight with weapons instead, and many carry shields.
sections.Flight and defenses: The table lists AC 3 (2). Wings are AC 7. Frontal attackers can target the wings only if taller than the krolli, and rear attackers always roll against wing AC. A krolli that has lost at least half its HP cannot fly. It carries up to 30 pounds in flight unencumbered and up to 45 pounds encumbered. Save vs. paralyzation every 15 minutes of unencumbered flight or every 5 minutes when encumbered. On failure it must land and rest 1 hour per 15 minutes already flown.
sections.Group encounters: An eyrie holds 3d20 adults, including one 7th-level fighter per 10 adults, and young with 1/2 HD equal to about one-tenth the adult count. The prose assigns 95% of krolli to fighters up to 7th level and 5% to likely priests of Ka. Krolli have acute senses and speak a dialect of Shazak, with Common rare among the lizard kin.
sections.Red Curse and XP: Krolli in cursed areas can acquire Legacies and use cinnabryl to avoid Affliction. The XP table gives 270 normally, 420 with a Legacy, and 650 for a leader.

ruleNotes: AC 2 is parenthetical in the table. The prose mentions shields without explicitly tying them to that number. The XP column prints an extra 650 with a Legacy without marking which tier it belongs to.

name: Snapper
otherStatistics: Ocean shores. Rare, organized in packs, active by day. Carnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure U. Lawful evil. Appearing 2d10. No magic resistance. Height 6–7 feet. Steady morale 11–12.
description: Heavy-shelled hunters that travel in shoreline packs and ride aggressive nikt’oo.

sections.Actions:
Natural weapons. Make two claw attacks for 1d6 damage each and a bite for 2d4.
Armed attacks. Use a weapon and a bite instead. Tridents, nets, and spears are favored.
sections.Senses and movement: Infravision 60 feet, or 120 feet underwater. Snappers have the swimming nonweapon proficiency and can hold their breath underwater for up to two hours. Their shell cannot close around them.
sections.Group encounters: The largest, toughest male leads each hunting pack until challenged. The printing gives leaders no separate stat line. Packs train their nikt’oo mounts for aggression.

name: Forest Ray
otherStatistics: Any forest. Rare, solitary, active at any time. Carnivore. Intelligence 0. Treasure J–N ×10, Q ×5, X. Neutral. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Wingspan 16–20 feet. Elite morale 13–14.
description: A mottled flying ray that lies buried under forest litter until prey comes close.

sections.Hit dice, THAC0 and XP: 8 HD has THAC0 13 and 3,000 XP. 9 HD has THAC0 11 and 4,000 XP. 10 HD has THAC0 11 and 5,000 XP. 11 HD has THAC0 9 and 6,000 XP. Add 1,000 XP if it has a Legacy.
sections.Actions:
Bite. One attack for 3d4 damage. Against a human-sized or smaller target, a hit that beats the required attack roll by more than 2 swallows the target. The swallowed target dies at the end of six rounds. It can attack the ray from inside using a dagger or short sword at −4 to hit against the ray’s normal AC.
Sting. Instead of biting, make one sting attack for 2d10 damage. The target must save vs. paralyzation or be stunned for 2d4 rounds.
sections.Traits: Buried ambush grants +2 to surprise opponents. Flies no higher than the treetops and can turn sideways to pass between trees. Changing its coloration takes several days.
sections.Red Curse: A Legacy occurs 25% of the time, usually from Region 4, such as Duplicate or Regenerate. The text also gives a 10% chance of a Region 3 Legacy. Forest rays need no cinnabryl.

ruleNotes: The swallow rule says the roll must exceed the required number by more than 2, but the example lets a 16 swallow when the target number is 14. This block uses the written threshold.

name: Saragón Lyra Bird
otherStatistics: Very rare, usually solitary, active by day. Insectivore. Intelligence 1. No treasure or magic resistance. Neutral. Appearing 1, or occasionally a mated pair. Unreliable morale 2–4.
description: An iridescent bird drawn to hosts carrying parasites such as cardinal ticks and Inheritor lice.

sections.Actions:
The bird has no physical attacks and flees danger.
Song, 3/day. While singing it can use charm person, charm monster, or charm plant. Those charmed defend the bird as best they can.
sections.Traits: Continual protection from evil in a 10-foot radius. The bird neither gains Legacies nor needs cinnabryl. When it feeds on a host’s parasites, reduce infestation by 1 percentage point per day. It leaves at 5% and will die after a full week without parasites.
sections.Encounter rewards: Award 65 XP for a significant encounter, such as hearing its song or hosting the bird. Killing it gives no XP. The text suggests an optional mild curse for killing one, such as −2 to combat rolls and saves or −4 to proficiency checks. A high-level druid may assign penance. Killing one through captivity is rumored to bring an irreversible curse such as permanent Affliction.

ruleNotes: The table says 4–5 feet long, while the description calls it hummingbird-sized. Tiny follows the printed size category. The printing gives a three-use limit without saying whether it applies to each spell. This entry uses a shared limit. The belief that its song forbids all violence is a legend.

name: Legacy Leech
otherStatistics: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, active at any time. Feeds on Legacies. Intelligence 19–20. No treasure. Chaotic evil. Appearing 1. Magic resistance 25%. True leech form is 7 feet long. Fearless morale 19–20.
description: A banished tanar’ri posing as a red steel weapon. It steals Legacies through the wielder until it can return home.

sections.Actions: Weapon form. The unattended leech moves and makes one attack each round using the damage of the weapon it resembles. Once held, it uses the wielder’s weapon abilities. It can appear as a +1 rapier, dagger, magical hook, or pistol. It may also let the wielder use an absorbed Legacy.
sections.Bond and theft:
An intelligent creature that takes hold of the weapon is bonded as tendrils enter its flesh, with no save. The leech vanishes into its host until it reappears in one of its weapon shapes. The host drops anything held in that hand.
To steal a Legacy it does not have, the leech makes the host plunge its blade into the heart of a just-killed creature. The host can refuse a demand with a Wisdom check, blocking the leech for an hour or until a new conflict. During theft the host may save vs. spell to expel the leech, at −1 per Legacy it has absorbed. A host dies immediately once the leech steals 15 Legacies while bonded to that same host.
sections.Traits: Starts with 1d4+1 acquired Legacies and never needs cinnabryl. Its weapon form radiates evil. A good priest’s grasp makes it wrench free at effective Strength 20. It will not choose a host with a heroic spirit. A paladin can still grasp it.
sections.Restored tanar’ri: At 20 absorbed Legacies, the leech can break its banishment. It spends two rounds attacking those present before it automatically gates home. In this form it makes two claws for 4d4 each, casts as a 9th-level wizard, and is immune to cold, fire, electricity, poison, and charm.

name: Eyeweed
otherStatistics: Aquatic, usually along coasts or in rivers. Rare, solitary, active at any time. Carnivore. Intelligence 1. No treasure or magic resistance. Neutral. Appearing 1. Body 10 feet across. Steady morale 11–12.
description: A fleshy mass disguised as algae or seaweed. Its feelers look like stalks with eyes until the mouths at their tips open.

sections.Actions: Feelers. Attack with 2d4 feelers, each dealing 1d3 damage on a hit. They can extend up to 100 feet to find and bite prey. Eyeweed hunts by touch and smell.
sections.Defenses: Each feeler takes 6 damage to sever. Damage to a feeler does not reduce the plant’s HP. Kill the central body to destroy the eyeweed. Lost feelers grow back in a week.

name: Vermeil Fungus
otherStatistics: Any terrain. Rare, multicellular, active at any time. Scavenger. Intelligence 0. No treasure or magic resistance. Neutral. Appearing 2d4. Height 4–7 feet. Steady morale 11–12.
description: Crimson fungi that feed on steel seed and the remains of Legacy users. They often grow alongside vermilia.

sections.Actions:
The fungus has no ordinary attacks.
Detonating cloud. Attacking or disturbing it releases a red cloud in a 30-foot radius. Every vulnerable creature in the radius is affected as if caught next to detonating smokepowder. The cloud has no printed damage or save.
sections.Cinnabryl depletion: Under the linked campaign rule, an affected Inheritor instantly loses seven days of cinnabryl protection. If less remains, deplete what is left and apply the remaining time to the Time of Loss and Change. The fungus supplies the 30-foot radius in place of the smokepowder rule’s normal close range. The fungus itself has no Legacies.
sections.Setting rule source: Savage Coast Campaign Book, Depletion of Cinnabryl, pp. 78–79.

name: Aurochs Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence High (13–14). Size Medium, 4 ft. long. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 25%.
description: A shaggy, horned servant that takes a bison-like shape or stands upright like a minotaur.

sections.Actions:
Horns. In natural form, make one attack for 1d6 damage. With a running start, charge for 2d6 instead. A charge hit allows a separate trample attack for 2d4 damage. A target hit by the trample loses its initiative that round if it has yet to attack.
Humanoid weapons. Fight as a 7th-level warrior with +2 damage. The servant arrives with a halberd or can use a halberd, battle axe, or lance supplied by its bearer, including a magical one. It retains the weapon held when it shifted to natural form for its next humanoid transformation.
sections.Traits:
Armored head. The head has AC 0.
Spell immunity. Mind-affecting spells have no effect.
sections.Bearer benefits: While telepathically linked, the bearer gains +2 damage with halberds, battle axes, and lances. Baron Calturix of Nemausa is the known bearer.

name: Bear Heraldic Servant
speed: 12 upright, 18 on all fours or in humanoid form
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence High (13–14). Size Medium, 6½ ft. tall. Morale Fearless (19–20). Magic resistance 20%.
description: A dark-furred bear that stands upright to fight. Its humanoid form keeps its claws and bear-like face.

sections.Actions:
Claws and bite. In either active form, make two claw attacks for 1d10 each and a bite for 2d8. In natural form, if either claw hits, the bear can make a separate hug attack for 2d8 more damage.
Hold person (3/day). Use the 2nd-level priest spell.
sections.Traits:
Exceptional Strength. Strength 18/00.
Spell defense. Immune to all charm and hold spells. If magic resistance fails against a sleep spell, the servant must travel back to its coat of arms and remain inactive for one turn.
sections.Bearer benefits: While carrying the coat of arms as a shield, the bearer gains Strength 18/00 unless the servant is active and more than a mile away. Other magical defenses apply under the shared rules. Hold person and the sleep vulnerability stay with the servant. The Count of Harstal is the known bearer.

name: Bee Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence Exceptional (15–16). Size Medium, 5 ft. long. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 35%.
description: A human-sized bumblebee with a heavy stinger. The humanoid form keeps its wings and compound eyes.

sections.Actions:
Sting. In natural form, make one attack for 2d6 damage, then resolve the poison.
Poison. Save vs. poison at −2. A success still deals another 2d6 damage. Failure deals another 5d4 damage and paralyzes for one round.
Humanoid attacks. The stinger is gone. The servant can deliver the poison by touch or attack with a dagger it knows how to use.
sections.Traits:
Infravision 90 ft. in either active form.
Fear aura. Extends 10 ft. and affects only opponents.
sections.Bearer benefits: While telepathically linked or personally carrying the arms with the servant inactive, use the poison touch three times per day for half damage and the fear aura once per day. Magus Rex of Herath is the known bearer.

ruleNotes: The bee’s profile gives the fear aura’s radius and targets but omits a save category and duration.

name: Black Swan Heraldic Servant
speed: 6, fly 18 (C). Humanoid flight uses fly with maneuverability A.
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence Exceptional (15–16). Size Medium, 5 ft. tall. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 40%.
description: A black swan with a gold bill. In humanoid form it looks like an elven woman in a feathered cloak.

sections.Actions:
Beak. Make one attack for 1d6 in natural form. The humanoid form carries a dagger.
Charm. Choose a target at will, once per target per day. Immortals are immune. The target saves vs. breath weapon with +1 for each 10% of magic resistance or fraction thereof. Total charm immunity grants +10 instead. A natural 1 fails regardless of modifiers. On failure, the target cannot harm the swan or its bearer.
Mental command. Use the 1st-level priest spell on a creature already charmed. A command that provokes a strong negative response allows a new save to break the charm.
sections.Traits:
Enchanted defense. A creature that resists the charm still needs a +1 or better weapon to hit the servant.
Both active forms can use charm and command.
sections.Bearer benefits: While in contact with the servant, the bearer gains the protection against weapons below +1 and can use fly three times per day. The Count of Enom is the known bearer.

ruleNotes: The profile gives no charm duration. Keep the charm and its stated escape save together when running the encounter.

name: Dolphin Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence Genius (17–18). Size Medium, 5 ft. long. Morale Fearless (19–20). Magic resistance 15%.
description: A dolphin servant that swims through air just above the ground. Its humanoid form keeps its gills and webbed hands and feet.

sections.Actions:
Ram. In natural form, make one attack for 2d4 damage.
Humanoid weapons. Use any weapon available to a wizard at the listed THAC0.
Spellcasting. Cast as an 8th-level wizard in either active form. In natural form, dolphin speech and flipper gestures supply verbal and somatic components, but spells with material components are unavailable. The humanoid form can carry materials and often has two minor magic items. The bearer can supply a spellbook, which the servant absorbs on returning to natural form.
sections.Traits:
Saving throws. Use the saves of an 8th-level wizard.
Air movement. A magical field supports the natural form a few feet above the ground, where it moves as if swimming.
Speech. The humanoid form can still communicate with dolphins.
sections.Bearer benefits: While in contact or personally carrying its arms, use the servant’s saving throws whenever they are better. While telepathically linked, the bearer can breathe water and cast any 1st-level spell known to the servant. The Baroness of Savaria is the known bearer.

ruleNotes: The printing leaves the spell selection to the referee. Prepare the available spells as for an 8th-level wizard.

name: Dragon Heraldic Servant
speed: 12, fly 30 (C) in natural form. Humanoid has no wings.
otherStatistics: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence High (13–14). Size Medium, 6 ft. tall. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 15%.
description: A six-foot green dragon. Its humanoid form keeps the scales, claws, and teeth and loses its wings and tail.

sections.Actions:
Claws and bite. In dragon form, make two claw attacks for 1d10 each and a bite for 3d6. Its tail can also strike a creature behind it for 2d6.
Fire breath (3/day). In either active form, breathe fire for 6d8 damage in place of physical attacks.
Humanoid weapons. Fight as an 8th-level fighter using two claws for 1d6 each and a bite for 2d6, or a two-handed sword. If desired, the servant arrives with a +1/+3 two-handed sword, which is absorbed when it returns to dragon form.
sections.Traits: The same AC and hit points apply in either active form. Only the natural form flies.
sections.Bearer benefits: While telepathically linked, the bearer gains two effective levels instead of one and is immune to fire-based attacks. The King of Robrenn is the known bearer.

ruleNotes: The servant’s fire breath lists damage and uses but gives no area or save details. The sword’s +1/+3 notation is retained as printed.

name: Griffon Heraldic Servant
speed: 12, fly 30 class C in natural form. Fly 15 class D with a rider. Humanoid form 16, fly 30 class C.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 25%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fearless morale 19–20.
description: A yellow-furred griffon with an eagle's head and wings. Its upright humanoid form is lighter and keeps its wings.

sections.Traits:
Keen senses. By sight and smell, it can usually identify creatures up to one mile away.
Enchanted defense. Only a magical weapon of +1 or better can harm it. Once fighting, it stays in the fight until it or its foe dies or its bearer calls it back.
sections.Actions:
Raking pass. The griffon usually opens with a flying pass to rake with its claws, then lands. Its usual attack routine is two claws for 1d4+1 each and one beak strike for 2d8.
Enlarge. Apply the wizard spell with double its usual duration. The enlarged griffon can carry a rider at full movement.
Whispering wind and gust of wind. Use each spell up to three times per day. The griffon has all three spell effects in either active form.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Margrave of Zvornik and the Duke of Pachester ride theirs for ceremonies. The duke's magical saddle and harness improve flight maneuverability to B or C depending on the circumstances. While in telepathic contact, only magical weapons can hit the bearer.

name: Phoenix Heraldic Servant
speed: 8, fly 48 class C in natural form. Humanoid form 18, fly 24 class B.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 20%. High intelligence 13–14. Fearless morale 19–20.
description: A five-foot bird with violet and red-orange plumage, ruby eyes, and a sapphire-blue beak. Its humanoid form still has feathers, claws and wings.

sections.Traits: Regeneration. Restore 3 HP per round using the troll regeneration rule, including after death. Fire-based attacks have no effect. If other damage kills the phoenix, it turns to ash. A limited wish or destruct spell cast within one turn can prevent its return. Otherwise it rises as a bird of living flame with whatever HP it has recovered. This rebirth does not use any of the five daily immolations.
sections.Actions:
Talons and beak. Two talon attacks deal 1d10 apiece and the beak deals 2d8. The bird uses only its beak while on the ground. The humanoid form can use all three attacks.
Immolation, five times per day. Give up all attacks to burn for one round in either form. Anyone within 10 feet takes 8d6 fire damage, halved by a successful save vs. breath weapon.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Priest-King of Eshu gains the benefits of two extra experience levels while in contact with the phoenix. If the phoenix is killed and prevented from returning, the bearer loses four experience levels permanently.

name: Ram Heraldic Servant
speed: 16 in either form. Rough or broken ground does not slow the servant.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 30%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fanatic morale 17–18.
description: A shaggy mountain ram with oversized horns. Its upright form keeps the horns, hooves and coat.

sections.Traits: The ram switches to humanoid form to fight unless its bearer directs otherwise. In that form it can use armor supplied by its bearer and absorb it when changing back. Both forms are immune to blunt weapons, magical or otherwise.
sections.Actions:
Head-butt, ram form. One strike for 1d8 damage, inferred from the stated double-damage running head-butt of 2d8.
Maces, humanoid form. The ram produces a double-headed mace in each hand and makes four attacks for 2d4 damage each. It reabsorbs the weapons on changing back.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Baron of Sedhuen gains immunity to blunt weapons while in contact with the ram or carrying the coat of arms with the inactive servant.

ruleNotes: The table lists four 2d4 attacks for the humanoid mace routine. The natural-form prose gives a charging head-butt for 2d8 and calls it double damage.

name: Sea Lion Heraldic Servant
speed: 8 out of water, swim 18 in natural form. Humanoid form 12, swim 8.
otherStatistics: Natural AC 3 on the scaled body, where most attacks land, and AC 5 on the head. Humanoid AC 5 before armor. Magic resistance 20%. High intelligence 13–14. Fanatic morale 17–18.
description: A lion-headed swimmer with a fish's tail. On land its tail can propel it a few feet above the ground. Its humanoid form still has gills and webbed rear feet.

sections.Traits: Its magical field supports movement out of water. The humanoid form can wear armor.
sections.Actions:
Claws and bite. Two claws deal 2d4 each and the bite deals 2d6. If both claws hit the same target in the round, the target loses its attack if it has yet to act. The bite against that mauled target gets +4 on the attack roll and deals double damage.
Roar, three times per day. Declare the roar in place of the bite before any attack rolls. Enemies within 20 yards save vs. spell or suffer the effects of fear.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Lord Governor of Da Presa can breathe water and gains the combat benefits of a potion of heroism while in contact with the servant or carrying the coat of arms with it inactive.

name: Unicorn Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Natural AC 2. In humanoid form the chain mail gives AC 3. Magic resistance 15%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fearless morale 19–20.
description: A white unicorn with golden strands in its mane and tail. Its humanoid form is a young knight in white chain mail.

sections.Traits: Sense true enemies within 240 yards. Both forms are immune to charm, hold and poison, and make other saves as an 11th-level wizard. The white mail vanishes if taken off. The servant must spend one full turn in natural form before the armor can reappear.
sections.Actions:
Hooves and horn, natural form. Make two hoof attacks at 1d6 damage each and a horn attack at 1d12. The horn attack gets +2 to hit. If the unicorn has 30 feet to build up speed, it can charge with only the horn for 3d12 damage. The horn's touch dispels magic as an 11th-level wizard.
Longsword, humanoid form. Make two attacks per round with a +2 longsword that dispels magic as the horn does.
sections.Bearer benefits: No bearer is named. Tradition says the servant is granted to a fair and just human or elven maiden. The bearer can sense true enemies and gains the servant's spell immunities while in contact with it.

name: Wyvern Heraldic Servant
speed: 6, fly 24 class D in natural form. Humanoid form 18 on land.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 20%. High intelligence 13–14. Champion morale 15–16.
description: A gray, two-legged reptile with broad wings and a stinging tail. Its humanoid form resembles a wingless lizardfolk.

sections.Traits: It cannot speak in either form. In natural form it uses hisses and growls, and both forms retain the telepathic link with its bearer.
sections.Actions:
Bite and sting, natural form. The bite deals 2d8 damage. On a sting hit the target must save vs. type F poison or die. A successful save still leaves 2d3 damage. The wyvern favors a gliding approach that gives its victim a −2 surprise penalty.
Claws, humanoid form. Two claw attacks deal 1d6 damage apiece.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Margrave of Slagovich can use poison three times per day as the reverse of the priest spell neutralize poison. This power works regardless of telepathic contact or whether the bearer carries the coat of arms.

name: Eagle Heraldic Servant
speed: 6, fly 48 class C in natural form. Humanoid form 18, fly 40 class B.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 30%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fanatic morale 17–18.
description: A six-foot eagle with gold-tipped brown feathers, a white head, and a wingspan of more than 15 feet. Its upright form keeps both wings and taloned feet.

sections.Traits:
Keen sight. Surprise is possible only at night or in the eagle's lair, with a 1 in 10 chance in those circumstances.
Majestic aura. Before each attack on the eagle in natural form, the attacker must save vs. spell at −2 or be unable to harm it with that attack. The aura does not protect the eagle from an opponent it is directly attacking.
sections.Actions:
Natural attacks. Two claws for 1d8 each and one beak strike for 2d6. A dive of more than 50 feet gives +4 to the attack roll and doubles claw damage.
Humanoid attacks. Use a long sword as a 5th-level fighter or claws for 1d6 each. A diving claw attack still deals double damage.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Emperor of Eusdria gains the effect of eyes of the eagle and can invoke majestic aura for one round three times per day. Both benefits require either telepathic contact or carrying the coat of arms with the inactive servant.

name: Horse Heraldic Servant
speed: 16, fly 16 class C. Flight only while ridden and commanded telepathically by its bearer.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 30%. High intelligence 13–14. Fanatic morale 17–18.
description: A small black or white horse that can carry a rider about five feet tall or shorter. Its humanoid form keeps a narrow mane running from brow to neck.

sections.Traits:
Regeneration. Restore 1 HP per round in either form. Damage from acid or fire must be healed by magic. Barding improves Armor Class and reshapes to fit the humanoid form.
Magical flight. The horse walks or gallops into the air when its mounted bearer commands it through their link.
sections.Actions:
Warhorse routine. Two forehooves for 1d8 each and a bite for 1d6. These attacks can accompany its rider's attacks. On a round with no frontal attack, it can kick an opponent directly behind it for 2d8.
Humanoid mace. The servant produces a double-headed mace and fights as a 5th-level warrior.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Duke of Cimarron and the Baron of Mohesia share the servant's regeneration during telepathic contact.

name: Lion Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 20%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Champion morale 15–16.
description: A dusky yellow lion whose humanoid form resembles a rakasta with long claws and a lion's face.

sections.Traits: Alert and stealthy. Surprised only on a roll of 1. Can move silently as a thief with a 75% chance. Its humanoid form can wear armor.
sections.Actions:
Claws and bite. Two front claws for 1d4+2 each and a bite for 1d10. In natural form, if both front claws hit in the same round, roll another attack, dealing 2d12 damage with the rear claws on a hit.
Roar, once per turn. Replace the bite with a magical roar. Each opponent within 10 yards saves vs. paralyzation or is stunned for 1d4 rounds. Both forms can roar.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Queen of Bellayne, Lord Governor of Leãoça, and Margrave of Hojah are known bearers. During telepathic contact, the bearer can gain the effects of a potion of super-heroism three times per day. If the bearer carries the coat of arms in battle and the servant is within one mile, troops and allies gain +2 morale.

name: Rooster Heraldic Servant
speed: 16, fly 12 class D in natural form. After flying for one round it must stay on the ground for one round. Humanoid form cannot fly, but jumps up to 6 feet high or 12 feet across.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 35%. Genius intelligence 17–18. Champion morale 15–16.
description: A five-foot rooster whose humanoid form has red hair, dark eyes, and taloned feet.

sections.Traits: Magical defenses. Both forms are immune to illusions and save against other magic as a 12th-level wizard. The humanoid cannot wear armor.
sections.Actions:
Beak, natural form. One strike for 2d6. The humanoid can instead wield a dagger at THAC0 15.
Crow. In either form, reproduce each of these wizard spells once per day without casting it: feather fall, deafness, dispel magic, shout, chaos, conjure animals, and power word stun. Use 12th level for effects that vary by caster level.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Count of Suerba gains immunity to illusions and the servant's special saves when they are better than the count's own.

name: Sea Horse Heraldic Servant
speed: 11, swim 21 in natural form. Humanoid form 16, swim 16.
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 30%. High intelligence 13–14. Champion morale 15–16. Infravision 120 ft.
description: A six-foot seahorse plated in brown or green scales. Its humanoid form keeps the armor, gills, and webbed hands and feet.

sections.Traits: Magical hover. Out of water, the natural form swims through the air a few feet above the ground.
sections.Actions:
Natural attacks. Head-butt for 1d4+1 and tail slap for 2d4. The humanoid form uses two fists for 1d4 each.
Fire shield (cold). In either form, generate the 4th-level wizard spell.
Polymorph self, three times per day. For up to one hour, become a man-sized nonmagical creature known to the servant or bearer, and use that creature's natural weapons.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Lord Governor of Tartaruga gains 120-foot infravision and can use fire shield (cold) at will while in contact with the servant.

name: Stag Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 35%. High intelligence 13–14. Champion morale 15–16.
description: A six-foot stag with antlers edged in sharpened glassteel. The muscular humanoid form has brown fur and a bony ridge where the antlers would sit.

sections.Traits: Missile protection. Both active forms always have protection from normal missiles. Physical armor costs the humanoid two sword attacks per round. Magical protection does not impose that cost.
sections.Actions:
Antlers, natural form. One strike for 4d6, doubled on a charge.
Glassteel swords, humanoid form. Two attacks with each of two +1 short swords at 1d6+2 each, including the servant's Strength bonus. The swords are part of the servant and cannot be removed.
sections.Bearer benefits: The Countess of Morguen gains protection from normal missiles and +1 damage while in contact with the servant or carrying the coat of arms with the servant inactive inside.

name: Talbot Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: Magic resistance 25%. High intelligence 13–14. Fanatic morale 17–18.
description: A white hound with a broad muzzle and long, floppy ears. Its humanoid form looks much like a white-haired lupin.

sections.Traits: Tracking. Its sharp hearing and sense of smell detect and track enemies in either form. The humanoid can use the skills and weapons of a 6th-level ranger. The bearer supplies the gear, which the servant absorbs when changing back.
sections.Actions:
Bite, natural form. One bite for 2d4. In humanoid form, attack with a ranger weapon provided by its bearer.
Invisibility. Turn invisible at will in either form. Ambushes made this way gain +3 to surprise.
sections.Bearer benefits: The King of Renardy, Duke of Ysembragne, Baron of Brégoigne, and Countess of Marmandy are known bearers. While in contact, the bearer gains the keen senses and can turn invisible three times per day. Telepathic contact or carrying the coat of arms with the inactive servant also grants the ranger bonuses against giant-class creatures.

ruleNotes: The entry names the ranger bonus against giant-class creatures without supplying its numeric value.

name: Tyger Heraldic Servant
otherStatistics: No magic resistance. High intelligence 13–14. Elite morale 13–14.
description: A nine-foot cat with unstriped orange fur and jade-green eyes. Its humanoid form keeps the fur and feline face.

sections.Traits: Evade. If the servant waits for its opponents to attack, it has a 20% chance to evade a non-area attack, including a spell. On success it takes no damage and can still attack that round. On failure it takes the damage and loses all its attacks that round. Both forms can evade.
sections.Actions:
Natural attacks. Two front claws for 1d4 each and a bite for 1d10. If both front claws hit, the servant can attempt rear claw attacks for 2d6 per claw.
Humanoid attacks. Make two strikes with each hand for 1d6 per hit. To disarm, the servant must have initiative, succeed on an attack roll, and pass the same 20% chance used for evasion.
sections.Bearer benefits: No bearer is known. A bearer could use the servant's evasion only while in telepathic contact with it.

name: Cayma
otherStatistics: Temperate to subtropical swamps or forests. Uncommon. Village of 10d6 adults and half as many noncombatants. Active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Neutral. No magic resistance. Height about 1 foot. Morale 8–10.
description: A foot-tall lizard kin ambusher. Caymas use hidden village entrances and prefer a quick strike followed by retreat.

sections.Actions:
Attack once for 1d3 damage or use a weapon. Bone daggers deal 1d2. A bok deals 1d6. Caymas use it two-handed as a pike and cannot throw it.
Ambush. A concealed cayma imposes a −2 penalty on the target’s surprise roll.
sections.Senses and skills: Infravision 90 feet. Hide in Shadows and Move Silently each succeed 40% of the time. Speaks a Shazak dialect. Knowing one lizard kin dialect gives basic comprehension of the other two. A few individuals speak Common.
sections.Village shaman: Each village has a shaman equivalent to a 5th- to 7th-level priest. The shaman has AC 6 and raises a party’s morale by one level. XP by Hit Dice, with Legacy value second. 5 HD 420 or 650 XP. 6 HD 650 or 975 XP. 7 HD 975 or 1,400 XP.
sections.Red Curse: A cayma entering the cursed lands can acquire a Legacy and needs cinnabryl to prevent Affliction. A standard cayma with a Legacy is worth 120 XP.
sections.Cayma grenades:
A Wokan can supply ceramic grenades. On impact against a hard surface, roll 1d20. The grenade breaks and releases its cloud on 1–17.
Sleep. Within 1 foot of the impact, anyone whose head or breathing organ is in the cloud must save vs. breath weapon or sleep for 1d4 turns.
Choke. Same area and save as sleep. Failure leaves the victim unable to attack or defend for 1d6 rounds.
Fog. A 5-foot radius blocks ordinary vision and infravision for 1d6 rounds. Strong wind halves the duration.
Weapon details. Savage Coast Campaign Book, Part 2, pp. 136–137.

name: Gurrash
otherStatistics: Bayou. Rare. Village. Active at any time. Carnivore. Intelligence 5–7. Treasure M. Chaotic evil. Appearing 1d6. No magic resistance. Height about 8 feet. Morale 13–14.
description: A muscular Bayou reptilian with an alligator head. Its claws can drag a foe underwater and its tail keeps foes from closing behind it.

sections.Actions:
Claw and bite. Make two claw attacks for 1d4 each and one bite for 2d4, or replace the claw routine with a weapon. A gurrash can use a weapon and bite in the same round. Add +2 to weapon damage.
Tail slap. Against a foe behind it, add one attack for 1d8 damage to the round’s routine.
Drown. If both front claws hit one foe, drag it underwater. It drowns in 1d3 + 1 rounds. Resolve the hold as a wrestling maneuver.
sections.Berserk: When provoked or wounded, roll a 10% chance per melee round to go berserk. A berserk gurrash gains one attack and +1 to hit and damage. It can keep fighting to −7 HP.
sections.Village chief: Bite damage rises to 3d4. Strength 19 gives +3 to attack rolls and +7 to weapon damage.
sections.Languages and Red Curse: Speaks a Shazak dialect and can broadly understand the other two lizard kin dialects. Some gurrash mages know written Shazak. Common is rare. A gurrash entering the cursed lands can acquire Legacies and needs cinnabryl to ward off Affliction.

name: Nosferatu
otherStatistics: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, and active at any time. Drinks blood. Intelligence 8–18. Treasure F. Any alignment, usually evil. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 15–16. The XP listed is the minimum.
description: This blood-drinking undead keeps the skills and spells of its former life. It can pass for a living person in daylight, though it casts no shadow and has no reflection.

sections.Actions:
Bite or weapon. One bite deals 1d4 damage. It can instead use a weapon or cast a spell from its former class. Use the THAC0 of the equivalent class and level. Strength is at least 16.
Charm. A creature that meets its gaze saves at −2 or is affected as by charm person. The nosferatu can then use suggestion on that victim.
Change form. It can become gaseous at will and is immune to physical attacks in that form. At night it can become a large bat. By day it can become a raven. It can also use spider climb.
Summon animals. Call 1d100 rats or bats underground, or 3d6 wolves in the wilderness. They arrive in 2d6 rounds.
sections.Defenses and defeat:
Only +1 or better magical weapons can harm it. It regains 1 HP each round. Sleep, charm, hold, poison, and paralysis fail against it. Cold and electricity spells deal half damage. At 0 HP it turns gaseous and flees to its coffin. If it fails to reach the coffin within 12 turns, it dies. After eight hours inside, it regains corporeal form.
Garlic repels it. Clerical symbols and holy water are harmless to it. A cleric of opposing alignment or a cleric specialized in hunting undead can turn it. Immersion in running water for three consecutive rounds destroys it. A wooden stake through the heart stops it, but it resumes healing if the stake is removed. To destroy a staked nosferatu permanently, behead it and fill its mouth with earth consecrated to a good deity.
sections.Invitation and spawn: A resident must invite it into a private home. Charm or deception can secure the invitation. Once invited, it can come and go. If it chooses to create spawn, a drained human or humanoid rises after three days unless the body is burned or destroyed. The spawn obeys its creator until the creator dies.
sections.Former class: Keep the original class’s memories, abilities, skills, and restrictions. Set class level to at least 7 and at most 9 when it becomes a nosferatu. It can advance thereafter at triple the usual XP. Keep ability scores except that Strength is at least 16 and Constitution is no longer required. Warriors and clerics can wear armor without improving AC. Clerics retain spells from their original Immortal patron only if their alignment still matches.
sections.Hunger and Red Curse: It must drink at least 9 HP worth of mortal blood per week. After a week of fasting, its ability scores fall by 1 each day to a minimum of 9. An extra 1d4 HP worth of fresh blood restores lost scores. Nonhumanoid blood dulls the pain for one day without restoring scores. It never acquires Legacies and needs no cinnabryl.

name: Shazak
otherStatistics: Temperate to subtropical swamps and forests. Rare. Tribe. Active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K (A). Neutral. Appearing 3d6. No magic resistance. Height about 6 feet. Morale 13–14.
description: A woodland lizard kin who often defends settlements against raiders. Important tribal members and beast-riders ride trained giant bats called mobats.

sections.Actions: Claw and bite. Make two claw attacks for 1d2 each and one bite for 1d6, or fight with a weapon. Spears and swords are common choices.
sections.Leader and XP: The table lists a 6 HD leader worth 270 XP. A standard shazak with a Legacy is worth 120 XP.
sections.Languages and Red Curse: Speaks Shazak and can broadly understand the other two lizard kin dialects. Common is rare. A shazak entering the cursed lands can acquire Legacies and needs cinnabryl to prevent Affliction.

name: Skinwing
otherStatistics: Tropical or subtropical land. Rare. Flock. The table lists activity at any time and the ecology notes peak activity by day. Carnivore and scavenger. Intelligence 2–4. No treasure. Neutral with evil tendencies. Appearing 2d4. No magic resistance. Wingspan 12–21 feet. Morale 11–12, +1 if trained.
description: A leathery, batlike predator that rakes prey while flying past. Hunters sometimes train it as a short-distance mount.

sections.Actions:
Claw pass. Make two claw attacks for 1d4 each from above or behind, then fly out of reach. A flock normally concentrates these passes on one target. If both claws hit and the victim weighs less than half the skinwing’s carrying capacity, carry it aloft and deal 2d4 damage per round thereafter.
Bite. Deal 2d4 damage while landed or flying very slowly. Its AC is 7 while it uses this attack.
A skinwing carrying a rider cannot attack.
sections.Flight and loads: Carry up to 30 pounds per HD. It needs a drop-off to take off with a rider and must save vs. paralysis every half hour of mounted flight. Failure exhausts it and forces an immediate landing. Its flight ceiling is about 1,000 feet. At 50% or more damage it loses flight until fully healed.
sections.Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP:
4 HD. THAC0 17. XP 175, or 270 with a Legacy.
5 HD. THAC0 15. XP 270, or 420 with a Legacy.
6 HD. THAC0 15. XP 420, or 650 with a Legacy.
7 HD. THAC0 13. XP 650, or 975 with a Legacy.
sections.Red Curse: 25% have a Legacy from Region 3. Anti-Missile and Gaseous Form are typical. They do not require cinnabryl.

name: Tortle
otherStatistics: Forests and beaches. Uncommon. Tribe. Active by day. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Any alignment. Appearing 2d6. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 17–18.
description: A shelled coastal humanoid. In a group, the front line withdraws into its shells while the rear line shoots, then emerges when the volleys stop.

sections.Actions:
Claws or weapon. Make two claw attacks for 1d4 each or use a weapon. Some tortles have learned a bite that deals 1d6. Favored weapons include short bows, staves, long swords, and flails.
Shell withdrawal. Take no other action that round. While withdrawn, use AC 1 and add +4 to all saves, including saves against mental attacks. The tortle cannot move, attack, or see, but it can hear and smell. Gaze attacks and other effects that require the target to see fail against it while withdrawn.
sections.Senses and swimming: Infravision and underwater vision extend 60 feet. It has the Swimming nonweapon proficiency. Buoyancy keeps it afloat even in bogs, quicksand, and mud. It holds its breath for 10 turns. It speaks Tortle and usually Common or another local language.
sections.Red Curse: Tortles acquire Legacies and need cinnabryl to ward off Affliction.

name: Amber Lotus
otherStatistics: AC, HP and THAC0 apply to one plant. Common, neutral, active at any time. Average morale 8–10. No treasure or magic resistance. No Legacies.
description: A bed of water lilies near the Dream River can blanket the banks in sleep-inducing pollen. Batracines hide under the pads.

sections.Actions: The plants have no direct attack. Each person who contacts the pollen saves vs. poison at −2 or sleeps for at least 1d4+1 days. The victim stays asleep if the wind keeps carrying pollen over them. Batracines are immune.
sections.Running the encounter: A bed has 3d100+100 plants. Anyone approaching within 1 yard per plant is exposed. Wind can carry the pollen for miles and it clings to surfaces and creatures.
sections.Experience: Award 35 XP for surviving the encounter and 1,400 additional XP for destroying the bed.

name: Gargoñan Rose
otherStatistics: Rare, solitary, active by day in forest. Chaotic good. Intelligence 5–7. Steady morale 11–12. No treasure or magic resistance.
description: A sentient white rose bush senses visitors through scent and empathy. It gives up one flower a week to protect someone from the Red Curse.

sections.Actions: The bush has no normal attack. It uses its Legacies if someone uproots it or takes a second rose within a week. Its song can charm monsters within 1 mile and turn them against its foes.
sections.Defensive Legacies: Acid Touch deals 1d4 plus 1 per HD on a hit. Entangle creates tentacles 5 feet long per 3 HD, to a maximum of 25 feet, for 1 round per level. An entangled target needs a successful bend bars roll to escape. Poison adds 1d6 damage to a natural physical attack other than a bite and can also cause sleep, paralysis, damage or death depending on HD. A save vs. poison halves the effect. Weaken reaches 10 yards. On a failed save vs. spell, the target counts as Strength 5 and takes −2 to attacks and −1 per damage die for 1 round per level.
sections.Plucked rose: The flower protects as one ounce of cinnabryl. Its last petal drops at the end of day seven. The bearer cannot use Legacies while protected by the rose.
sections.Experience: Award 35 XP once for encountering the bush or using a rose. Destroying the bush earns no XP.
sections.Printed source: pp. 88–89, with Legacies on pp. 7–9

ruleNotes: The appendix gives the song a 1-mile radius without specifying a save, duration or use limit. Its generic Poison rule lists possible effects by HD without giving a full tier table.

name: Golem
description: Savage Coast builders use glassteel, red steel and cut stone to make guards and siege engines.

sections.Actions: Choose one printed form below. Use its listed attack routine and relevant defenses. These constructs have no Legacies or cinnabryl requirement.
sections.Aelder: Lesser golem. AC 3, 9 HD, 60 HP, THAC0 11, movement 18, 2,000 XP. Two piercing front-leg strikes for 2d6 each reach 10 feet. In icy burial grounds, ranged attacks beyond 20 feet are impossible and nonmelee attacks within 20 feet take −2. Immune to light or gaze effects. Can cast color spray, dancing lights and hypnotic pattern three times each per day. A spider aelder spins thick glassteel webs for cover or nearly invisible brittle strands that shatter to alert it. Ee’aar priests create and command them in pairs. Large, neutral, fearless 19–20. No magic resistance or treasure.
sections.Glassine Horror: Lesser golem. AC 2, 8 HD, 60 HP, THAC0 13, movement 9, fly 36, 4,000 XP. As an inactive sheet, it occupies 50–100 square feet across a window or doorway and is 1–6 inches thick. As a roughly 15-foot humanoid, it punches once for 2d10. Opponents within 10 feet save vs. spell or take −2 to attacks. It can use crystalbrittle, sunburst as a wand of illumination, and continual light in this form. It is immune to light and electricity spells while humanoid. In sand form it moves at 36, at most 5 feet above a surface. The 100-cubic-foot cloud deals 2d8 to a creature on a successful attack roll and blinds it for 2d4 turns on a failed save vs. spell. The cloud is immune to wind spells. It flees below 10% of starting HP and heals by resting or absorbing 50 gp in gems per HP. Usually alone or 1d6 under its creator’s command. Lawful neutral, average morale 8–10, treasure Q ×4. No magic resistance.
sections.Red Golem: Greater golem. AC 1, 18 HD, 90 HP, THAC0 3, movement 6, 14,000 XP. Two punches for 2d12 each. Both must target the same foe while that foe is still standing. It attacks the greatest threat first. Cinnabryl within 10 feet loses 1 ounce each round without triggering the Time of Loss and Change. It requires a +2 weapon to hit and takes half weapon damage from enchantments below +4. Magical electricity slows it for 1d3 rounds. Magical fire heals 1 HP per damage die. Other spells fail against it. It uses taunt after a strike with a nonmagical weapon or a spell it is immune to. It can alter its size and appearance with shapechange only on its master’s command. Large, neutral, fearless 19–20. No magic resistance or treasure.
sections.Hulean Juggernaut: Greater golem. AC 0, 30 HD, 150 HP, movement 9, 21,000 XP. Creatures in its path save vs. breath weapon to escape sideways or take 10d10 damage. Its wheelbase can crush multiple targets at once. A ram may break larger obstacles, and soldiers aboard can attack creatures that evade the wheels. It can stop, turn or reverse within one round. Immune to fire, sleep, charm, hold and nonmagical weapons. All its saves succeed on 4 or higher. It obeys only its creator’s simple verbal commands and may keep following the last order after the creator dies. Only the creator can authorize entry. Gargantuan, neutral, elite morale 13–14, treasure A and possible extras. No magic resistance.

name: Heroic Spirit
otherStatistics: Very rare, solitary. Retains its alignment from life. Fearless morale 20. No magic resistance, treasure, Legacies or cinnabryl requirement.
description: A dead hero takes a living host to finish a deed or disgrace the villain who stopped it.

sections.Actions: The spirit has no direct attack. When the host faces deadly peril, it awakens and automatically influences the host with suggestion to rush into battle. Use the effects of a potion of super-heroism regardless of the host’s class. The host must fight with conspicuous daring for one round per foe, with a minimum of 4 and a maximum of 15 rounds. Afterward the host chooses whether to keep fighting or withdraw with flair.
sections.Running the encounter: Outside combat the spirit mostly lies dormant and communicates through empathy alone. Its host keeps free will under ordinary conditions. A host who adopts the spirit’s flamboyant habits may gain Luck and reroll a failed saving throw or ability check. That benefit can persist while the spirit is dormant. It leaves after fulfilling its goal or moves on if the host gains a level first or dies.
sections.Exorcism and rivalry: The spirit cannot be attacked or turned directly, but exorcism can drive it out. A good spirit leaves if a host sincerely asks. It never chooses a host already carrying a Legacy Leech. Both spirits recognize one another when their hosts meet. If the spirit’s host refuses to attack the leech’s host, it attempts to seize control with magic jar, potentially forcing a fight to the death.
sections.Experience: Award the host 450 XP once, upon the spirit’s first activation. Helping it finish its deed earns a further 1,000 XP.
sections.Printed source: pp. 100–101, with Luck Legacy on p. 8
sections.Super-heroism: Use the host’s current level. Level 0: +6 effective combat levels and 5d10 bonus HP. Levels 1–3: +5 and 4d10 + 1. Levels 4–6: +4 and 3d10 + 2. Levels 7–9: +3 and 2d10 + 3. Levels 10–12: +2 and 1d10 + 4. A host of level 13 or higher gains no bonus. Deduct damage from the bonus HP first. The spirit’s encounter rules determine duration and allow any class. See Encyclopedia Magica, Volume III, p. 890.

name: Parasite
otherStatistics: Rare, one infestation. Mindless, no treasure or magic resistance. Parasites neither gain Legacies nor become Afflicted.
description: An infestation creates a problem to diagnose or survive, with a cure that can drive an adventure.

sections.Actions: Use one infestation procedure below. Parasites have no regular attacks. Award 15 XP for surviving a nonfatal infestation or 65 XP for surviving a potentially fatal one.
sections.Inheritor lice: Roll d100 for the degree of infestation. Increase the host’s cinnabryl use by the same percentage, doubling it at 100%. Up to three times per day the lice can trigger Displace and move their host 10 feet in a random direction to evade an incoming physical hit. They sometimes do so at random. Cinnabryl ointment removes them. Saragón lyra birds eat them.
sections.Powder moth: Use detect invisibility to see the moths. Roll d100 for the percentage of smokepowder spoiled. While the moths remain, anyone moving the keg saves vs. paralysis or sets it off. A full keg deals 10d6+10 damage within 10 feet and half damage out to 20 feet. Scale damage by the unspoiled fraction, then halve it on a successful save vs. breath weapon. Inheritors within 20 feet lose one week of cinnabryl protection per full 8 points of damage suffered.
sections.Jibarú pest: Choose a local pest. A moth’s powder makes victims believe they can fly, and the moth can supply medicine for the Fly Affliction. A brown leech drains several HP of blood per week while preventing the Strength Affliction. A green territorial wasp’s sting kills on a failed save vs. poison. Its nest supplies an ointment that cures vermilia.
sections.Lupin plague: Infested grapes or wine transmit the plague. The host saves vs. poison at −3 at the end of each day or dies. Medication or magical healing can end it.
sections.Cardinal tick: Roll d100 for the starting infestation and use that percentage as the chance a Legacy fails. Participants in melee against an infested carrier acquire a 5% infestation. Each attempted Legacy use increases infestation by 15 percentage points. Nonhumanoids cap at 50%. Other Red Curse effects still apply. Cinnabryl ointment removes the ticks. Scratching them off costs 1 HP per percentage point removed without rare Jibarú medicine. Saragón lyra birds eat them.
sections.Vermilia: Physical contact transmits the infection. Living creatures save vs. poison to avoid it. Undead catch it automatically. Damage starts at 1 on day one and doubles each day. Undead can avoid the day’s damage with a save vs. death magic at the end of that day, with a penalty equal to that day’s damage. All victims take an additional −1 on related saves per Legacy. Infection counts as a +2 weapon for damaging undead or magical creatures. Cure disease, heal or a remedy from vulturehound blood or a suitable Jibarú pest ends the infection. Fire cleanses infested remains.
sections.Printed source: pp. 84–86, with Displace Legacy on p. 7

ruleNotes: The book leaves the Jibarú moth’s duration and the leech’s exact HP loss to the DM.

name: Scarlet Pimpernel
otherStatistics: Rare beds, appearing 2d4, active by day. Neutral. Intelligence 2–4. Steady morale 11–12. No treasure or magic resistance.
description: These orchids feed on cinnabryl and grow on mineral deposits or the graves of Legacy users. A similar-looking plant makes harvesting them dangerous.

sections.Actions: The plants have no direct attack. Assign a regional Legacy to each bed, offensive or defensive. After the bed uses a Legacy three times in a day, choose a different random Legacy for its next use. The bed can keep using powers while any plant survives. It depletes an ounce of cinnabryl per week. If deprived of cinnabryl, the plants dry up and release spores.
sections.Eating the orchid: Fresh pimpernel boosts effects such as the range, duration or damage of Legacies by 10% for 1 turn. Dried pimpernel gives a 30% boost for 3 turns, but requires a save vs. poison at −3. Failure causes hallucinations for 1d6 turns, during which the eater cannot react to real events.
sections.Crimson delight: Someone who eats this lookalike fresh must save vs. poison or die. Dried crimson delight instead prevents Legacy use for 24 hours.

name: Shadow Symbiont
classification: Tiny item or Medium shadow creature
otherStatistics: Very rare, appearing 1d4. Neutral. Intelligence 11–12. No treasure or magic resistance. Immune to the Red Curse.
description: A black garment adapts to its wearer and trades powers for experience. If starved or threatened with death, it may take the wearer into the Plane of Shadows.

sections.Actions: On the Prime Material Plane, the worn form has AC 10, 1 HD, THAC0 19, no movement or attacks, steady morale 11–12 and an XP value of 120. No magical aura betrays it. On the Plane of Shadows it becomes a humanoid with AC 2, 8 HD, THAC0 13, movement 15, champion morale 15–16 and an XP value of 5,000. It attacks twice for 2d4 each. Each hit drains 10% of the experience needed for a level and 1 point of Strength or Constitution, chosen at equal odds.
sections.Mask: The wearer concentrates to gain immunity to mind-affecting magic, at 20 XP per use per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows the symbiont has that immunity itself.
sections.Cloak: Absorbs all magical HP damage from a hit that would reduce the wearer below 0 HP. Costs 10 XP per point absorbed per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows, subtract 8 points of damage from each attack against the symbiont.
sections.Gloves: Give the wearer the Luck Legacy for hand-related actions only, allowing a reroll of a failed save or ability check when applicable. Costs 20 XP per use per wearer level. In the Plane of Shadows, the symbiont itself has Luck.
sections.Boots: Allow the wearer to cast dimension door for 10 XP per use per wearer level. The boots can also guide the wearer toward opportunities to earn XP at no cost, without controlling decisions. In the Plane of Shadows they cast dimension door as an 8th-level mage once per round.
sections.Feeding and defense: Only spells and weapons of +1 or better can harm the symbiont. Any damage it suffers also harms the wearer. A lethal attempt makes it flee by plane shift with the wearer. A wearer who gains too little new XP to feed it saves vs. spell. Success makes it drain three times the missing XP before slipping away. On failure it takes the wearer to the Plane of Shadows and tries to devour them.
sections.Printed source: pp. 108–109, with Luck Legacy on p. 8

ruleNotes: The encounter gives each power’s XP cost and describes the consequences of shortfalls, without prescribing a separate feeding schedule.

name: Wallaran Spirit
otherStatistics: All three totems are solitary, very rare, and neutral or good, usually lawful. Intelligence 19–20. Special morale. No treasure, Legacies or cinnabryl requirement.
description: A Wallaran totem animal visits the deepest dreams to offer advice. It sometimes leaves a token the dreamer finds upon waking.

sections.Actions: A spirit can cast at will as an 18th-level mage, with no casting time or components. It prefers to turn attackers into harmless creatures with polymorph other. It can disappear when attacked or replace the dreamer’s weapons with harmless objects. It speaks directly to the dreaming mind.
sections.Kangaroo: Medium. Movement 18. Three attacks for 1d3, 1d3 and 2d4. Its followers are known for acting quickly by Wallaran standards.
sections.Koala: Small. Movement 6. One attack for 1d2. Its followers often provide food for the community.
sections.Kookaburra: Tiny. Movement 6 and fly 18, maneuverability A. One attack for 1 damage. Nocturnal. Its followers often guide interactions with outsiders or care for children.
sections.Running the encounter: Clashes occur only in the Dreamworld. Only magical weapons physically brought there can hit the spirit. A weapon that appears merely because its owner is dreaming has no effect. All three totems have 95% magic resistance.
sections.Experience: Award 1,000 XP for a peaceful encounter with the spirit. There is no XP for fighting it.

ruleNotes: The Kookaburra size figure in the table appears as 18 feet. Its description gives 18 inches and the table classifies it as Tiny.

name: Akikage
description: An assassin who died before completing a mission can rise as an akikage. It stalks its intended victim in silence, vanishes, then attacks from a new position.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +7. AC 14 (+3 Dex, +1 deflection), touch 14, flat-footed 11. Base attack +3, grapple +3. Space and reach 5 ft.
sections.Skills and feats: Hide +11, Intimidate +7, Jump +6, Listen +9, Search +7, Sense Motive +9, Spot +9, Tumble +5. Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative.
sections.Actions:
Incorporeal touch. Melee +6 for 2d6 cold. Full attack makes two touches at +6 each.
Freezing Strike (Su, 6/day, once per round). Spend a use before the touch attack. A miss spends the use. On a hit, apply the touch damage. A target susceptible to cold makes a DC 14 Fortitude save or is stunned for 1 round, even if it is immune to critical hits. A critical hit also requires a DC 14 Fortitude save against death in 1d3 rounds. Creatures immune to critical hits ignore this death effect.
Invisibility (Su). On its turn, become invisible as a free action at will. The invisibility ends when it attacks.
sections.Traits:
Sneak Attack (Ex). Add 2d6 against a flanked target or one denied its Dexterity bonus to AC. This requires a living target with vulnerable anatomy and no concealment. Immunity to critical hits also prevents the extra damage. The akikage can sneak attack other incorporeal creatures.
Incorporeal and undead traits. Turn resistance +1.
sections.Encounter: Any land or underground, solitary. No treasure. Usually lawful evil. Advancement 7–10 HD (Medium). Understands languages it knew in life and never speaks.

name: Animator
classification: Undead acquired template for a nonmagical object
description: An invisible spirit feeds on a ward’s fear, jealousy, or anger. It takes over an object the ward cares about and uses it to keep others away.
ruleNotes: Several sample ACs disagree with their modifiers or the template. The profiles retain the listed totals. The Huge sample gives neither touch nor flat-footed AC.
The Colossal damage line adds an extra letter to the dice expression. It is presented as 1d3+9, consistent with the other five samples.

sections.Actions:
Physical attacks use the inhabited object’s attacks, damage, and special attacks. A bodiless animator makes no physical attacks.
Spell-like abilities (caster level 9). At will: animate objects, crushing despair (DC 16), fear (DC 16), rage (DC 15), scare (DC 14), and telekinesis.
Powerful Charge (Ex). In samples with this ability, add 4 damage to a charge. The host needs its own means of movement, such as wheels or legs, or must be propelled by telekinesis.
Blindsight (Ex). In samples with this ability, detect foes within 120 ft. Beyond that range, treat the animator as blinded.
sections.Template: Animate a nonmagical base object using the animated object rules and change its type to Undead. Change its Hit Dice to d12s. Keep its speed, attacks, damage, saves, special attacks, qualities, and hardness. Add +2 deflection AC. Increase Strength by 2, with size adjustments as appropriate. Typical mental scores are Int 15, Wis 12, Cha 12. Base skills are Bluff +10, Hide +5, Intimidate +10, Listen +5, Search +7, Sense Motive +10, Spot +5. Apply size and Dexterity to Hide, and adjust skills for size and level as needed. Add Improved Initiative and Iron Will, plus Power Attack for more powerful animators.
sections.Ward and weaknesses:
Ward (Su). An animator feeds on negative emotions produced by its ward and need not follow the ward’s orders. At more than 60 ft. from the ward, or when the ward goes more than a day without these emotions, it loses 1 Cha per day. Normal recovery resumes after rejoining its ward or finding another.
Outside an object it is naturally invisible and incorporeal. Invisibility purge does not cancel the natural invisibility. It cannot possess a magical object or an object under a spell. A successful melee touch with dispel evil expels it. Neither expulsion nor ordinary destruction of the host harms it. Soul bind or trap the soul can imprison it indefinitely. Turn or rebuke it as an 8 HD undead. To destroy it, trap it magically in the object, such as in an antimagic field, then destroy the object while it remains trapped.
sections.Tiny scarf:
1/2 d12 (3 hp). Initiative +6. Speed 40 ft. AC 16 (+2 size, +2 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 14, flat-footed 14. Base attack +0, grapple −8. Attack and full attack are slam +1 melee (1d3). Space 2½ ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +0, Ref +0, Will +1. Str 10, Dex 14, Int 15, Wis 12, Cha 12. Bluff +5, Hide +6, Intimidate +5, Listen +5, Search +6, Sense Motive +5, Spot +5. Improved Initiative (bonus), Iron Will.
Constrict (Ex). A successful grapple check deals slam damage to targets of Small size or smaller. It can also constrict a Medium victim wearing the scarf around its neck when it strikes.
sections.Small candelabra:
1d12 (6 hp), CR 3. Initiative +5. Speed 40 ft. AC 13 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +1 deflection), touch 13, flat-footed 12. Base attack +0, grapple −4. Attack and full attack are slam +1 melee (1d3). Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +0, Will +2. Str 10, Dex 12, Int 15, Wis 14, Cha 12. Bluff +4, Hide +5, Intimidate +5, Listen +6, Search +6, Sense Motive +4, Spot +5. Improved Initiative (bonus), Iron Will.
Powerful charge. A Small host gets surprise against opponents who fail a DC 20 Spot check.
sections.Medium bed: 2d12 (12 hp). Initiative +6. Speed 40 ft., or 50 ft. with multiple legs. AC 14 (+2 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Base attack +1, grapple +1. Attack and full attack are slam +1 melee (1d3). Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +0, Will +3. Str 10, Dex 14, Int 16, Wis 13, Cha 15. Bluff +7, Hide +7, Intimidate +7, Listen +6, Search +8, Sense Motive +6, Spot +6. Improved Initiative (bonus), Iron Will. Blindsight and powerful charge.
sections.Large cart: 4d12 (24 hp). Initiative +6. Speed 40 ft., or 50 ft. on wheels where the ground permits. AC 14 (−1 size, +3 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 14, flat-footed 11. Base attack +2, grapple +9. Attack and full attack are slam +5 melee (1d3+3). Space and reach 10 ft. for long and tall hosts. Fort +1, Ref +1, Will +4. Str 16, Dex 12, Int 16, Wis 12, Cha 14. Bluff +9, Hide +8, Intimidate +9, Listen +6, Search +10, Sense Motive +8, Spot +6. Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative (bonus), Iron Will. Blindsight and powerful charge.
sections.Huge carriage: 8d12. Initiative +3. Speed 40 ft., or 60 ft. on wheels. AC 16 (−2 size, −1 Dex, +2 deflection listed). Base attack +8, grapple +16. Attack is slam +4 melee (1d3+4). Full attack is two slams at +4 each (1d3+4). Space 15 ft., reach 10 ft. for long hosts or 15 ft. for tall ones. Fort +2, Ref +2, Will +6. Str 18, Dex 9, Int 18, Wis 14, Cha 14. Bluff +13, Hide +15, Intimidate +13, Jump +14, Listen +13, Search +15, Sense Motive +13, Spot +15. Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative (bonus), Iron Will, Power Attack. Blindsight and powerful charge.
sections.Gargantuan cottage: 16d12 (96 hp). Initiative +2. Speed 10 ft. AC 6 (−4 size, −2 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 6, flat-footed 8. Base attack +16, grapple +32. Attack is slam +7 melee (1d3+7). Full attack is two slams at +7 each (1d3+7). Space 20 ft., reach 15 ft. for long hosts or 20 ft. for tall ones. Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +10. Str 24, Dex 7, Int 17, Wis 14, Cha 14. Bluff +21, Hide +17, Intimidate +21, Listen +17, Search +22, Sense Motive +21, Spot +21. Combat Reflexes, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Initiative (bonus), Improved Overrun, Iron Will, Power Attack. Blindsight and powerful charge.
sections.Colossal mansion: 32d12 (192 hp). Initiative +1. Speed 10 ft. AC 1 (−8 size, −3 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 1, flat-footed 0. Base attack +16, grapple +35. Attack and full attack are slam +2 melee (1d3+9). Space 30 ft., reach 20 ft. for long hosts or 30 ft. for tall ones. Fort +13, Ref +13, Will +17. Str 28, Dex 4, Int 16, Wis 14, Cha 15. Bluff +22, Hide +17, Intimidate +21, Listen +21, Search +23, Sense Motive +22, Spot +27. Awesome Blow, Combat Reflexes, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Feint, Improved Initiative (bonus), Improved Overrun, Improved Sunder, Improved Trip, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack. Blindsight and powerful charge.
sections.Encounter: Use the base object’s CR +1, with CR 3 listed for the Small sample. Every sample has no Constitution score and gains undead traits and Ward while retaining object hardness. Any land or underground, solitary, always chaotic evil, no treasure.

name: Arayashka
description: Snow wraiths appear during blizzards. They drain a traveler’s warmth before moving close enough to strike.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +4. AC 11 (−1 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 11, flat-footed 11. Base attack +2, grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft.
sections.Skills and feats: Hide +15, Listen +10, Spot +10. Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative.
sections.Actions:
Freezing Touch (Ex). Incorporeal touch +5 melee for 1d8 cold damage and 1 Strength damage. The target recovers 1 Strength per hour once the arayashka is driven off or destroyed.
Drain Heat (Ex). Choose one heat source within 30 ft. A small campfire goes out in 1d4 minutes. A creature makes a DC 25 Fortitude save or takes 1 nonlethal damage each round until the arayashka is driven away or the victim dies. At nonlethal damage equal to half its hit points or more, the victim becomes fatigued. A full attack uses the same single choice.
sections.Traits:
Create Spawn (Su). A humanoid slain by an arayashka and buried where snowfall can occur rises as one at the next snowstorm. It loses its former abilities.
Incorporeal and undead traits. Cold subtype.
sections.Encounter: Any land in blizzard conditions, solitary or gang of 2–6. Standard treasure. Always neutral evil. Advancement 6–10 HD (Medium).

name: Giant Assassin Bug
description: A nearly transparent insect waits for helpless prey. Its carapace turns opaque and red after it feeds.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +0. AC 12 (−1 size, +3 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 12. Base attack +6, grapple +13. Space 5 ft., reach 10 ft.
sections.Actions:
Sting. Melee +6 for 1d8+5 and poison. Its full attack is the same sting.
Poison (Ex). Injury, Fortitude DC 14. Initial effect paralyzes for 2d6 minutes. No secondary effect.
Blood Drain (Ex). After paralyzing a victim, deal 1d4 Constitution damage each subsequent round while the proboscis stays attached. Any damage to the bug breaks contact.
sections.Traits: Camouflage (Ex). +6 racial bonus to Hide checks. After draining blood, it loses camouflage for 2 hours per point of Constitution damage it dealt. Vermin traits.
sections.Encounter: Hills or underground, colony of 2–5. One-tenth coins, half goods and items. Always neutral. Advancement 5–10 HD (Large).

name: Backward Man
description: This creature makes a household think it is haunted before it attacks. Its backward gait leaves its eyes and mouth pointed at whoever follows.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +3. AC 16 (+3 Dex, +3 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 13. Base attack +3, grapple +5. Space 5 ft., reach 10 ft.
sections.Skills and feats: Hide +3, Intimidate +6, Listen +8, Move Silently +8, Open Locks +8, Sleight of Hand +8. Combat Reflexes, Improved Grab, Multiattack.
sections.Actions:
Tentacle. Melee +5 for 2d4+2. Full attack adds one melee +3 attack for 2d4+2 per extra tentacle sprouted before its turn.
Constrict (Ex). Deal 2d4+2 on a successful grapple check against a Medium or smaller creature.
Spell-like abilities (caster level 4). Ghost sound 3/day and invisibility 2/day.
sections.Traits:
Sprout Tentacles (Ex). Each piercing or slashing wound deals damage normally and grows an extra tentacle that can attack on the backward man’s next turn. Each of those attacks is at +3.
Fast Healing (Ex). Recover 2 HP per round while above 0 HP. At 0 HP it bursts into inert tentacles. The burst deals no damage, though a DC 18 Horror save may apply.
Spider Climb (Su). Climb sheer surfaces as with spider climb.
sections.Encounter: Temperate and cold forest or marsh, solitary or pack of 2–5. Standard treasure. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 5–8 HD (Medium), 9–12 HD (Large). Speaks the local domain language.

name: Bakhna Rakhna
description: These nocturnal raiders slip into kitchens using phase door. A group scatters if pursued, leaving a few of its number to distract or poison the pursuers.
ruleNotes: The stat block’s size and size modifiers are Small. The advancement line lists Tiny.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +7. AC 14 (+1 size, +3 Dex), touch 14, flat-footed 11. Base attack +0, grapple −5. Space and reach 5 ft.
sections.Skills and feats: Escape Artist +6, Hide +14, Jump +4, Listen +2, Move Silently +8, Search +2. Dodge (bonus), Improved Initiative (bonus), Mobility.
sections.Actions:
Poisoned arrow. Use an arrow as a dagger, melee +1 for 1d3−1 plus poison. Or fire it from a tiny bow, ranged +5 for 1d3 plus poison. Its full attack uses the same single choice.
Phase Door (Sp). Three uses per day, caster level 16.
sections.Traits:
Poison Blood (Ex). Injury, Fortitude DC 13. Initial and secondary damage each deal 1d6 Dexterity damage. The DC is Constitution based.
Light Sensitivity (Ex). Take −2 on attacks and skill checks in bright sunlight or within daylight. Spell resistance 16.
sections.Encounter: Forest, hill, or underground. Gang of 4–9 or tribe of 5–20. Half goods. Always neutral evil. Advancement 1–3 HD (printed as Tiny). Level adjustment +0, cohort.

name: Baobhan Sith
description: This black sprite hides behind its invisibility and waits for a fight to leave someone isolated or helpless.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +7. AC 17 (+2 size, +4 Dex, +1 natural), touch 16, flat-footed 13. Base attack +1, grapple −9. Space 2½ ft., reach 0 ft.
sections.Skills and feats: Bluff +7, Concentration +4, Disable Device +7, Escape Artist +8, Hide +12, Intimidate +6, Listen +6, Move Silently +8, Ride +8, Search +9, Sense Motive +6, Spot +6. Dodge (bonus), Flyby Attack (bonus), Point Blank Shot (bonus), Weapon Finesse.
sections.Actions:
Dagger or javelin. Dagger +6 melee for 1d4−2 or tiny javelin +6 ranged for 1d4. Its full attack uses the same single choice.
Infectious Laughter (Su, once per day). Everyone within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Will save. On a failure, apply Tasha’s hideous laughter for 1d3 rounds at caster level 8. A success grants immunity to any baobhan sith’s laughter for the rest of the day.
Spell-like abilities (caster level 8). Once per day each: confusion, dancing lights, detect law, detect thoughts, dispel magic, entangle, permanent image (visual and auditory effects only), and polymorph. Save DC 13 + spell level, Charisma based.
sections.Traits: Natural Invisibility (Su). Invisible even while attacking. Suppress or resume it as a free action. Spell resistance 16.
sections.Encounter: Temperate forest. Gang of 2–4, band of 6–11, or swarm of 20–80. No coins and half goods and items. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 2–3 HD (Tiny). Level adjustment +3, cohort.

name: Bastellus
description: A dream stalker hides among cast shadows until someone sleeps. It takes on a broad human shape and spreads dark tendrils over the sleeper's face as it feeds.
otherStatistics: Any land or underground. Solitary or pack of 2–5. Always chaotic evil. No treasure. Advancement 6–10 HD (Medium). No level adjustment. Understands its languages from life but cannot speak. It can communicate with any creature that has a language through a dream.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +3. AC +3 Dex and +3 deflection. Touch 16 and flat-footed 13, calculated from those bonuses. Base attack +2, grapple +2 as listed. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6.
sections.Skills and feats: Bluff +9, Hide +10 or +20 with multiple light sources, Intimidate +11, Listen +9, Sense Motive +8, Spot +12. Alertness (bonus), Blind-Fight, Skill Focus (Hide).
sections.Traits:
Undead traits, incorporeal subtype, and +4 turn resistance.
Hide in Plain Sight (Ex). It takes on the shape of a shadow cast by a creature or object. An observer can use Spot to notice an extra shadow. The bastellus gains a +10 circumstance bonus to Hide in a room with more than one light source. A dream invasion reveals its actual form, ending this benefit.
Light Blindness. Sunlight or comparably intense light such as daylight blinds it. It tries to smother the light with darkness.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +5 melee. In the waking world the touch deals no damage. A creature hit must make a DC 17 Will save against insanity or suffer confusion for 1d4 rounds.
Darkness (Sp). Twice per day as a 5th-level sorcerer.
Sleep (Sp). Every living creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or fall asleep, regardless of Hit Dice.
Dream Invasion (Su). Take on its actual form and touch a sleeping victim's forehead. Witnesses make a DC 15 Horror save. The sleeper makes a DC 18 Will save. Failure gives the bastellus control of the dream and the sleeper wakes with one negative level. On a success, the sleeper can fight back inside the dream. Both sides retain their normal abilities, and the sleeper also has their current gear, spells, and feats. Supplies and spells used in the dream remain available after waking. The bastellus's dream touch deals 1d6 Wisdom damage instead of causing insanity. At Wisdom 0, the sleeper loses and wakes with one negative level. If the sleeper wins, they wake at once and recover lost Wisdom. The bastellus is stunned for 10 minutes per level of the sleeper.
Create Spawn (Su). Someone who dies from a dream invasion returns as an independent bastellus after 1d4 days, without their former abilities.
sections.Tactics: It attacks the weakest or least guarded target, puts guards to sleep when needed, and flees when it can if cornered.

ruleNotes: The attack header lists Constitution drain, but the detailed rules supply no amount or trigger. Use the detailed insanity and dream invasion rules. The printed grapple bonus is retained, though standard incorporeal creatures cannot physically grapple corporeal opponents.
The book gives no duration or daily limit for Sleep. For a runnable table default, use five minutes, as for the 3.5 spell at 5th caster level, with the printed save, radius, and unlimited HD.

name: Carrion Bat
description: This cave bat leaves kills to attract the maggots and grave scarabs it eats. It strikes in flight and retreats until scavengers arrive.
otherStatistics: Any land or underground. Colony of 10–40. Always neutral. Standard treasure. Advancement 3–4 HD (Medium) or 5–7 HD (Large). No level adjustment.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +9. Touch AC 16, flat-footed 14. Base attack +2, grapple −3. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +2, Ref +9, Will +2.
sections.Skills and feats: Listen +11 and Spot +11, each including a +4 racial bonus that is lost whenever its blindsight is suppressed. Improved Initiative (bonus), Flyby Attack.
sections.Traits: Blindsight. The printing lists the sense without a range.
