The printed Fortitude save removes a negative level. The text gives no special timing for the removal save.
description: A painted porcelain tiger guards valuables. On command it fires an enervation ray or grows large enough to fight with claws and teeth.

sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Claw +1 melee for 1d2 − 1 damage or the enervation ray.
Enervation Ray (Su, 3/day). Attack at +7 ranged touch as enervation at caster level 8. A living creature hit gains one negative level. Use the printed DC 6 Fortitude save to remove that negative level.
Enlarge (Su, at will). Grow to a 9-ft.-long Large tiger with AC 14 and Strength 23. Use two claws +9 melee for 1d8 + 6 each and one bite +4 melee for 2d6 + 3.
sections.Traits: Construct traits and damage reduction 5/—. Immune to fire. Continuously uses see invisibility at caster level 8.
sections.Control: Once a month, the figurine and its master make opposed Will saves. A win frees the figurine, changes its moral alignment to evil, and sends it after its former master. Figurines understand their creator's language and cannot speak.
sections.Encounter details: Any land in Sri Raji. Solitary. Always neutral while controlled. No treasure. Advancement 7–10 HD (Tiny), 11–14 HD (Small).

name: Cerebral Vampire
otherStatistics: Adapted from the printed fledgling nosferatu. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.
description: This vampire drains a pinned victim’s mind and uses the same lunar powers as a nosferatu.

sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Intelligence Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple and drain 1d4 Intelligence each round the pin holds. At Intelligence 0 or less the victim becomes catatonic. Use this in place of Blood Drain. The source describes the persistent Domination save as a Blood Drain rider and gives no new rider for this replacement.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.
sections.Traits:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.
sections.Spawn: If a victim dies while its Intelligence is 0 or less from the drain, it rises under the creator’s control on the next full moon. A victim with 4 or fewer HD returns as spawn and one with 5 or more HD as a cerebral vampire. The creature regains its original Intelligence in undeath. Cerebral spawn also replace Blood Drain with Intelligence Drain. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.
sections.Repelling and slaying: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.
sections.Skills and feats: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. otherStatistics: Fledgling sample, 5th-level dwarf fighter. Initiative +6. Touch AC 11, flat-footed AC 28. BAB +5, grapple +11. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +5, Will +3.

sections.Actions:

Failure by 1–5 leaves the target shaken, 6–10 frightened, and 11 or more panicked. Fear lasts 5d6 rounds. Failure by 16 or more also prompts a Horror save at DC 7, the Fear DC minus 5. Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple. Each round the pin holds, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP.

sections.Repelling and slaying: Mirrors and presented holy symbols repel it. An unbroken line of metal shavings blocks it even through stone. otherStatistics: Warm forest of the Verdurous Lands. Solitary, group of 5–8, or pride of 5–20 with one 6-HD leader. Standard treasure. Usually lawful neutral.
description: Werejaguar packs stalk through jungle cover, wearing down prey before closing in.

sections.Actions:

Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A humanoid that contracts the curse shifts permanently to hybrid form 2d6 hours after the attack. It scarcely remembers its earlier life and keeps this form until cured or slain.
When the pack stalks someone in the jungle, the target can make a Spot check to notice the ambush. An unaware target is flat-footed when the pack attacks.
sections.Hybrid form:

ruleNotes: The strain description refers to transmitted attacks but does not identify which wounds carry the curse. Apply the usual qualifying-bite rule to its hybrid bite.

name: Wereleopard
classification: Medium humanoid (Human, Shapechanger) in hybrid form
otherStatistics: Warm forest, hills, or plains. Solitary, pair, or pride of 5–10. Standard treasure. Usually lawful evil. A pride may serve a paka.

sections.Actions:

Hobble (Ex). A bite critical halves the target’s speed for one day. A successful DC 15 Heal check or at least 1 HP of magical healing ends the penalty early.
Lightning Phobia (Ex). Witnessing a burst of electricity, including lightning bolt, requires a DC 13 Fear save. Use a Will save and the Ravenloft Fear rules.
Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A newly afflicted creature becomes hybrid at the next dawn. It reverts to humanoid form on full-moon nights and remembers what it did in either form. True wereleopards have only hybrid form.

description: Wereravens spy for allies of the Vistani and avoid a fight when they can. In the air, they go for the eyes.

sections.Actions: Eye Peck (Ex). On a bite critical, the wereraven blinds one eye. A creature left with one eye takes a −2 competence penalty on Dexterity-modified rolls. Losing the last eye blinds the target. Only heal or regenerate cures this injury. Dire raven and hybrid bites use the listed curse. Once an enemy is blinded, the wereraven may return to human form to fight with a weapon or let the foe go. It can speak in dire raven form.

Amphibious (Ex). The hybrid can stay out of salt water for one minute per point of Constitution. After that, apply the 3.5 drowning rules.
A wereray uses the bite when it wants to pass on the curse. Its tail slam cannot transmit the curse. Stingray and hybrid forms have DR 10/coral.

Amphibious, DR 10/coral and stingray empathy.

ruleNotes: The tail slam’s poison appears in the full-attack line and the trait, but not in the single-attack row. Apply it to any tail slam.

name: Cannibal Zombie
description: These hungry dead return to the same isolated house night after night, retreating at sunrise and trying again after dark.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative −1. AC 14 (−1 Dex, +5 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 15. Base attack +1, grapple +5. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +1, Ref +0, Will +3. Climb +8. Toughness.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Slam +5 melee for 1d8 + 4 damage.
Bending the Land (Su). While pursuing a chosen victim, the zombie can stay at a set distance no matter how fast or far the victim flees. If watched, it can fade from sight and appear ahead or to the side. It closes in if the victim stops and can give up the pursuit at any point.
Create Spawn (Su). Someone it kills soon rises with the same statistics. The new zombie hunts alongside the pack of its own accord.
Stitching (Ex). The zombie can repair an injury by eating the corresponding body part. Replacing a lost arm, for example, requires eating an arm. The repair takes 4 hours.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/slashing, undead traits. It takes only a single move or attack in a combat round. It can utter short phrases in its former language. Speak with dead lets it converse coherently for the spell’s duration.
sections.Encounter details: Any terrain, often in packs of 7–20. Always chaotic evil. No treasure. Its odor can give away its presence from 50 ft. away. When barred from prey, a pack may turn on one of its own.

ruleNotes: Use the printed flat-footed AC 15. The source gives no distance for Bending the Land or exact timing for Create Spawn. Set these when planning the encounter.

name: Desert Zombie
description: Senmet’s undead servants swim beneath the sands of Har’Akir, leaving shallow furrows when they travel near the surface.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +2. AC 15, touch 10, flat-footed 15. The listed armor component is +3 natural. Base attack +1, grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +1, Will +3. Swim (sand) +5. Improved Natural Armor.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Slam +2 melee for 1d8 + 1 damage. The prose gives the same damage for weapons or other attacks.
Grab from Beneath (Ex). From under the sand, make an attack against AC that includes the victim’s Dexterity bonus but excludes natural armor and worn armor. A hit grabs the victim. The victim can break free with an opposed Strength check. After 3 rounds of being pulled down, the victim is completely buried. They survive the first round underground and die at the end of the second unless freed.
Spell Use. A zombie that cast spells in life still casts them, using the sorcerer class regardless of its previous casting class.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/slashing, undead traits. Sandswim (Ex) lets it travel beneath the sand to set up a grab. The print supplies no separate sand movement speed. It understands simple commands and rarely speaks.
sections.Encounter details: Deserts of Har’Akir, commonly in packs of 6–10. Usually neutral evil. No treasure. The prose says it retains its former skills and abilities. The printed stat block presents an ordinary specimen.

ruleNotes: Preserve the listed AC and saves where the components and ability scores disagree. The grab gives a custom defense and escape check but prints no separate attack bonus. Use the printed slam bonus for the initial grab as a table default.

name: Mud Zombie
description: Azalin’s muddy undead rise from the marsh with damaged or missing limbs. They drag anyone caught in both claws into the mud coating their chests.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative −1. AC 12 (+2 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 12. Base attack +2, grapple +7. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +4. Listed skills are Combat Reflexes +4, Hide +4, Use Rope +4, Search +4. Toughness.
sections.Actions:
Attack. Claw +7 melee for 1d6 + 5 damage. Full attack. Two claws at +7, each for 1d6 + 5.
Disease (Ex). A claw injury calls for a DC 15 Fortitude save. Failure deals 1 Strength damage initially, then 1 Strength damage per day for 1d6 days.
Suffocate (Ex). Two claw hits against the same victim grab them. Starting next round, the victim may try a Strength check once per round, with DC equal to their own Strength score. On a failure they take 1d4 suffocation damage that round. A success frees them.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to thrusting weapons, and undead traits. Immersion or steady exposure to water for 1d4 rounds strips the mud from the skeleton and removes Suffocate. The book gives no substitute skeletal stat block.
sections.Encounter details: Wetlands of Darkon. Always neutral evil. No treasure. The combat prose has it attack last in the round.

ruleNotes: The stat line prints Charisma −10, puts Combat Reflexes +4 among the skills, and gives initiative −1 despite Dexterity 14. Combat Reflexes is a feat in 3.5. Use the printed attack-last procedure and keep the supplied AC, attack and save figures.

name: Sea Zombie
speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), cannot run, swim 60 ft.
description: Packs of drowned sailors lure ships onto the rocks, climb aboard at night, and overwhelm the survivors.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +7. AC 16 (+2 Dex, +2 leather armor, +2 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 14. Base attack +5, grapple +8. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +7, Ref +4, Will +1. Climb +4, Jump +4, Ride +2, Swim +4, Survival +2. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative, Weapon Focus (longsword).
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Slam +8 melee for 1d10 + 3, longsword +9 melee for 1d8 + 3, or shortbow +8 ranged for 1d6.
Disease/Poison (Ex). A creature wounded by the zombie makes an immediate DC 14 Fortitude save against its injury poison. Initial damage is 1d4 Constitution and secondary damage is another 1d4 Constitution. Use the normal secondary poison save.
Stench (Ex). A creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 15 Fortitude save. Failure leaves it nauseated and horrified, with a −1 penalty to attack rolls and AC for 2d4 rounds.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/slashing, spell resistance 10, +2 turn resistance, and undead traits. Electricity and cold deal double damage, and fire deals half damage. Its telepathy reaches other sea zombies within 100 ft.
sections.Encounter details: Shallow waters of Saragoss, the Sea of Sorrows, or Souragne. Packs of 6–10. Always chaotic evil. Standard treasure. They are active at any hour underwater, reach the surface at night, and rarely travel more than 100 ft. inland unless fog covers them.

ruleNotes: Use the printed AC despite the listed Dexterity component differing from the ability score. The stench calls its consequence horrified and supplies its duration and numeric penalties. No additional Horror save is specified.

name: Spectral Annis
description: This ghostly hag reaches through cover to sap her victims’ life and add them to her retinue of spectres.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +1. AC 12 (−1 size, +1 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 12, flat-footed 12. Base attack +7, grapple +18 as printed. Space and reach 10 ft. Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +6. Bluff +8, Diplomacy +2, Disguise +0 (+2 acting), Hide +13, Intimidate +10, Listen +18, Move Silently +8, Spot +18. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Great Fortitude.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +14 melee for 1d6 + 7 plus Chilling Touch.
Create Hag (Su). On the night of the new moon, a ceremony can turn a captive human woman into a living annis she commands.
Spell-like abilities. Disguise self and fog cloud, each 3/day at caster level 8.
sections.Traits: Incorporeal and undead traits, damage reduction 10/magic, darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 19, and sunlight powerlessness.
sections.Encounter details: Cold marshes. Solitary or in a covey of 3 mixed spectral hags, with any spectres they have created. Usually chaotic evil. No treasure. Speaks Common and one or two other local or racial languages.

ruleNotes: The stat line supplies a grapple modifier, but it does not grant an exception to the usual restriction on incorporeal creatures grappling corporeal opponents.

name: Spectral Green Hag
speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 40 ft. (perfect), swim 30 ft.
description: A false animal call draws prey into a marsh, where the hag cloaks her approach with spells before striking.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +1. AC 13 (+1 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 13, flat-footed 12. Base attack +9, grapple +13 as printed. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +7. Concentration +7, one Craft or Knowledge +7, Hide +17, Intimidate +8, Listen +19, Move Silently +8, Spot +19, Swim +12. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Casting, Great Fortitude.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +13 melee for 1d6 + 4 plus Chilling Touch.
Create Hag (Su). Under a full moon, a ceremony can turn a captive elf woman into a living green hag she commands.
Mimicry (Ex). Imitate nearly any animal sound she has heard.
Spell-like abilities. At will at caster level 9: dancing lights, disguise self, ghost sound (DC 12), invisibility, pass without trace, tongues, water breathing.
sections.Traits: Incorporeal and undead traits, damage reduction 10/magic, darkvision 90 ft., spell resistance 18, and sunlight powerlessness.
sections.Encounter details: Temperate marshes. Solitary or in a covey of 3 mixed spectral hags, with any spectres they have created. Usually chaotic evil. No treasure. Speaks Common and one or two other local or racial languages.

ruleNotes: The stat line supplies a grapple modifier, but it does not grant an exception to the usual restriction on incorporeal creatures grappling corporeal opponents.

name: Spectral Sea Hag
classification: Medium undead (aquatic, incorporeal, formerly monstrous humanoid)
speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 40 ft. (perfect), swim 40 ft.
description: The hag stays below the waterline until travelers come within reach, then rises to confront them directly.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +1. AC 13 (+1 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 13, flat-footed 12. Base attack +3, grapple +7 as printed. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +4. One Craft or Knowledge +3, Hide +12, Intimidate +8, Listen +14, Move Silently +8, Spot +14, Swim +12. Alertness, Toughness.
sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +7 melee for 1d6 + 7. Apply the separately listed Chilling Touch as described in the shared rules.
Create Hag (Su). During a lunar eclipse, a ceremony can turn a captive halfling, gnome, or dwarf woman into a living sea hag she commands.
Evil Eye (Su, 3/day). Target one creature within 10 ft. that is not immune to fear. On a failed DC 13 Will save it is dazed for 3 days, or until remove curse or dispel evil ends the effect. It must also make a DC 13 Fortitude save or die of fright. This death does not create a spectre.
Horrific Appearance (Su). A creature other than another hag that sees her makes a DC 13 Fortitude save or takes 2d6 Strength damage, to a minimum Strength of 0. At 0 Strength the creature is helpless. Whether it saves or suffers the effect, it is immune to this hag’s appearance for 24 hours.
sections.Traits: Incorporeal and undead traits, damage reduction 10/magic, spell resistance 14, and sunlight powerlessness.
sections.Encounter details: Temperate aquatic terrain, including swamps and the shores of lakes. Solitary or in a covey of 3 mixed spectral hags, with any spectres they have created. Usually chaotic evil. No treasure. Speaks Common and one or two other local or racial languages.

ruleNotes: The sample calls this creature a monstrous humanoid and prints Constitution 12, but gives undead traits and belongs to a template that changes type to undead and removes Constitution. Run it as undead, preserving the printed hit points, saves, touch damage and ability score for reference. Its attack line omits Chilling Touch, which appears in the special attacks list and shared template. The printed grapple number does not override incorporeal restrictions.

name: Zombie Golem
description: Azalin’s lumbering construct is stitched from several ruined zombies. Its smell reaches intruders well before its fists do.

sections.Combat statistics: Initiative −1. AC 17 (−1 size, −1 Dex, +9 natural). Derived touch AC 8 and flat-footed AC 17. Base attack +12, grapple +16. Printed space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +6, Ref +5, Will +6.
sections.Actions:
Attack. Slam +16 melee for 2d8 + 4 damage.
Standard Actions Only (Ex). Move or attack on a turn, or combine them as a charge. The chart separately lists a full attack of two slams at +16 for 2d8 + 4 each.
Stench (Ex). Coming within 30 ft. requires a DC 19 Fortitude save. Failure applies a −2 circumstance penalty to attacks, saves and skill checks for 1d6 + 4 minutes. Success grants immunity to this golem’s stench for one day.
sections.Traits: Construct traits, damage reduction 10/magic. Magic Immunity (Ex) blocks spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural effects, with the listed exceptions. Targeted dispel magic with a check of at least 16 shuts it down for a number of rounds equal to the check result minus 10. A result of 26 or higher destroys it. Detect magic shows a growing magical aura while it is down. True resurrection destroys it immediately. Animate dead restores it to full HP.
sections.Encounter details: Any land or underground. Solitary, always neutral, no treasure. Advancement 19–24 HD (Large) or 25–44 HD (Huge). A creator can command it within 60 ft. if it both sees and hears the creator. Otherwise it follows the last order and responds if attacked.

ruleNotes: The source shows a two-slam full attack but separately restricts it to standard actions. Use a single slam unless another effect explicitly allows a full attack. Space and reach remain as printed despite the Large size.

name: Changeling
description: An Arak construct made from a stolen mortal shadow. Its maker assigns it a single task, which it pursues to the exclusion of nearly everything else.

sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. One weapon attack at +2 for weapon damage. Noncombatants do not attack.
Powriekin. Favor poisoned daggers and darts. Sneak attack adds 2d6 as a 3rd-level rogue. Trained Hide and Move Silently with +10 racial bonuses.
Sheekin. Does not fight, even when attacked. Trained Perform with a +20 racial bonus.
Sithkin. Prefers a simple weapon such as a sickle. Can rebuke undead as a 7th-level evil cleric. Undead other than domain lords will not attack unless it attacks first. It never speaks and has a +10 racial bonus on Move Silently.
Tegkin. Uses simple weapons or shortbow or longbow. Trained Survival +10 racial, Hide, Move Silently and Spot +4 racial.
sections.Traits: Construct traits and darkvision 60 ft. Initiative +0, BAB/grapple +0/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +1, Ref +1, Will +1. It knows its former owner's languages and dissolves into shadow when killed. Racial skills count as trained despite having no skill points. Shadow Rift, solitary or pack of 2–12, no treasure. Its alignment follows its maker.
sections.Running the encounter: An Arak puts a mortal to sleep with faerie food and lights a magic candle. Over its five-hour burn the mortal cannot wake unless it is extinguished. The Arak uses black dust and a silver sickle to remove the shadow, then must deliver it to the Shadow Rift before the candle goes out. Success creates the changeling and leaves the mortal as an Intelligence-less, shadowless automaton that refuses to defend itself. Wish or miracle restores the mortal. Resurrection cast on the living changeling destroys it and restores the mortal.

ruleNotes: CR is 0 for a noncombatant and 1 for a combatant. The entry prints no separate touch or flat-footed AC, innate poison profile, or poison DC.

name: Dhampir
classification: Medium augmented monstrous humanoid, 8th-level human fighter example
description: The printed example is a fighter whose supernatural gifts falter in daylight and when he goes too long without humanoid blood.

sections.Actions:
Attack. Slam +13 melee for 1d6 + 5 or +1 rapier +14 melee for 1d6 + 8. Full attack uses slam +13 or rapier +14/+3, as printed. Slam counts as magic for overcoming damage reduction.
Domination (Su). Standard action. Meet a creature's gaze within 30 ft. and force a DC 17 Will save against dominate person at caster level 12. Mere eye contact does not trigger it.
Blood Drain (Ex). While pinning a living target, drain 1d4 Constitution damage each round the grapple is maintained.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to summon 4d8 dire rats, 10d10 bats or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve up to one hour.
sections.Traits:
DR 10/magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, and spider climb as the spell at CL 12. Fast healing 1 until reduced to −10 HP. Supernatural special attacks and qualities stop in natural daylight or after a week without humanoid blood.
Restless (Su). The printed fighter rises as a vampire 1d4 days after burial. Destroy the body as for a vampire to prevent it. A dhampir with fewer than 5 original Hit Dice instead rises as vampire spawn.
sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +8. AC from +4 Dex, +4 natural and +5 +1 chain shirt. Touch 14, flat-footed 19. BAB/grapple +8/+13, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +8, Ref +8, Will +4.
sections.Skills and feats: Bluff +9, Climb +15, Hide +10, Jump +13, Listen +10, Move Silently +12, Ride +12, Swim +15, Search +8, Sense Motive +8, Spot +10. Alertness, Athletic, Combat Reflexes, Combat Expertise, Dodge, Improved Critical (rapier), Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Mobility, Quick Draw, Spring Attack, Weapon Focus and Weapon Specialization (rapier), Whirlwind Attack.
sections.Encounter details: Solitary, any land. Dust of appearance, double standard treasure.

ruleNotes: The printed example uses d12s and gives the second rapier attack as +3. The general template describes increasing Hit Dice by one die size. Retained the sample’s listed dice and attacks.

name: Dread Fiend
classification: Medium outsider (augmented humanoid), transposed 6th-level human fighter example
description: A succubus has taken control of the printed fighter. It can imitate the host’s ordinary life until its wings and infernal features give it away.

sections.Actions:
Attack. +1 longsword +13 melee for 1d8 + 8, claw +11 melee for 1d4 + 5, or shortbow +11 ranged for 1d6/×3.
Full attack. +1 longsword +13 with bite +6 for 1d6 + 5, two claws +11 with bite +6, or shortbow +11.
Smite Good (Su, 1/day). Add 6 damage to a normal melee attack against a good foe.
Spell-like abilities. Charm person at will. Darkness 3/day. Desecrate and unholy blight 1/day each. CL 6, Charisma-based saves.
sections.Traits: DR 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft., immune to poison, acid/cold/electricity/fire resistance 10, SR 16. Dread fiends summoned into Ravenloft cannot return to their plane when the spell ends.
sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +7. AC +5 Dex, +1 natural, +4 chain shirt. Touch 15, flat-footed 15. BAB/grapple +6/+11, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +10, Ref +7, Will +2.
sections.Skills and feats: Climb +7, Craft (woodworking) +2, Handle Animal +2, Intimidate +7, Jump +7, Ride +8, Swim +7. Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative, Mounted Combat, Weapon Focus and Weapon Specialization (longsword). Solitary, always evil, double standard treasure.
sections.Applying the encounter template: A complete transposition replaces the host’s agency and changes the host to outsider. The host must be living, corporeal, nongood and Int 4+. Keep size, Hit Dice, BAB and saves. Add +1 natural armor, two claws and a bite, magical natural weapons, and flight at land speed (average) only if wings function. Smite adds HD damage (max +20). DR increases to 10/magic at 12 HD, SR is HD +10 (max 35). Modifiers Str +4, Dex +4, Con +2, Int +4, Cha +2. Increase CR by 1 at up to 4 HD, by 2 at 5–10 HD, or by 3 at 11+ HD.
sections.Template powers: If Int or Wis is at least 8, gain cumulative Charisma-based abilities at CL equal to HD. At 1 HD darkness 3/day; 3 desecrate; 5 unholy blight; 7 poison 3/day; 9 contagion; 11 blasphemy; 13 unholy aura 3/day and unhallow; 15 horrid wilting; 17 summon monster IX (fiends only); 19 destruction. Default is 1/day.
sections.Possessing fiend options: Balor grants see invisibility at will and fire that deals 2d6 per round to anyone touching it, with −4 Cha. Erinyes grants cause fear at will and +4 Cha. Pit fiend grants +2 Str and injury poison at Fortitude DC 27, initially 1d6 Con and then death. Succubus grants charm person at will and +4 Cha.
sections.Natural attack damage by size: Bite/claw: Fine 1/none; Diminutive 1d2/1; Tiny 1d3/1d2; Small 1d4/1d3; Medium 1d6/1d4; Large 1d8/1d6; Huge 2d6/1d8; Gargantuan 3d6/2d6; Colossal 4d6/3d6. The full attack can use two claws and a secondary bite, or a weapon and secondary bite plus a claw if it has a free hand.

ruleNotes: The book supplies Hit Dice but does not print a fixed HP total. Roll 6d10 + 24. The printed HP dice and initiative do not follow directly from the listed abilities and feats.

name: Elemental Lich
classification: Medium undead (augmented humanoid), 10th-level human wizard example
description: An elemental lich fights up close to channel Ravenloft’s fire, mist, grave earth and blood. Its phylactery lies hidden beneath a mist-shrouded grave.

sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Touch +5 melee (see powers below), dagger +5 melee for 1d4/19–20, or dart +3 ranged for 1d4/×2. The touch and other natural weapons count as magical.
Conjure Dread Elemental (Su). Each day it may call one 8 HD blood, grave, mist and pyre elemental. Each serves willingly.
Fear Aura (Su). A creature under 5 HD that looks at it within 60 ft. must make a DC 18 Will save against fear. Success gives immunity to this aura for 24 hours. Caster level equals the lich's level.
Touch of Blood (Su). A hit deals 1d8 + 5 HP damage. DC 18 Fortitude or permanent paralysis and 1d4 damage each round. Remove paralysis or curse removal ends paralysis. DC 20 Spot or DC 15 Heal reveals the paralyzed victim is alive.
Touch of the Grave (Su). DC 18 Fortitude. Success means 1d8 + 5 HP damage. Failure means death unless heal is cast on the victim within one round.
Touch of the Pyre (Su). Hit for 1d10 damage, then clothing and armor save or ignite. The magic fire deals 1d10 each round until dispelled or the victim is burned to ash, typically within 1d4 rounds.
Touch of Mist (Su). No HP damage. DC 18 Will or the victim becomes chaotic evil and serves the lich, which can contact it telepathically up to 10 miles away. Remove curse cast by someone of the victim’s former alignment frees it and restores that alignment.
sections.Traits: Sample DR 15/bludgeoning and magic. Immune to elemental attacks, electricity, involuntary polymorph, and mind-affecting effects. Undead traits and +3 turn resistance. It cannot control undead.
sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +6. AC +2 Dex, +5 natural, +3 bracers, +2 protection ring. Touch 17, flat-footed 10 as printed. BAB/grapple +5/+5, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +11.
sections.Spells prepared: DC 15 + spell level. 0: detect magic, flare, ray of frost, read magic. 1st: burning hands, chill touch, comprehend languages, expeditious retreat, magic missile, true strike. 2nd: continual flame, flaming sphere, fog cloud, gust of wind, whispering wind. 3rd: dispel magic, explosive runes, fireball, slow. 4th: fire trap, remove curse, wall of fire, wall of ice. 5th: cone of cold, passwall.
sections.Skills and feats: Concentration +15, Decipher Script +10, Hide +18, Knowledge (arcana) +15, Knowledge (engineering) +10, Listen +18, Move Silently +26, Spellcraft +15, Spot +12. Combat Casting, Craft Wondrous Item, Improved Initiative, Scribe Scroll, Still Spell, Toughness.
sections.Phylactery encounter: The lich buries its phylactery in a grave near the lair, where a rite calls mist over the site. Approaching creatures make a DC 18 Will save or wander away in confusion. Digging above it alerts the lich, which usually arrives in 1d10 rounds.
sections.Applying the encounter template: Use a humanoid able to create the phylactery. Type becomes undead; keep size, BAB, saves and skill points. HD becomes d12, natural AC becomes +5 or remains higher, and Int, Wis and Cha increase by 2. Add one touch per round and the listed powers. Add +8 racial on Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Sense Motive and Spot. CR increases by 2; save DC is 10 + half HD + Cha modifier. The sample carries +3 bracers, potions of invisibility and gaseous form, and a brooch of shielding.

ruleNotes: Roll 10d12 + 3 because the sample does not print a fixed HP total. Keep sample touch and flat-footed AC despite the printed breakdown. The sample’s DR includes magic, but the template lists only bludgeoning. Pyre does not specify the item save category.

name: Geist
classification: Medium undead (augmented humanoid, incorporeal), 2nd-level human commoner example
description: The common geist cannot manifest in the material world. Instead it shows witnesses a false image of itself or draws them into an impression of the past.

sections.Actions:
No weapon or natural attack.
Mind Games (Su). As a free action, show a self-image to living creatures within 30 ft. Use major image except the image is a phantasm. DC 10 Will to avoid perceiving it. The GM may call for a Horror save if the geist died a gruesome death.
Phantom Shift (Su). Target a living creature and replace its perception of the Material Plane with the area’s ethereal resonance. DC 10 Will negates. The geist often recreates the circumstances of its death.
sections.Traits: Incorporeal and undead traits. The geist cannot manifest and ignores damage from corporeal sources. Destroying it temporarily does not end the haunting; it returns until its unfinished business is laid to rest. A bound geist has +4 turn resistance and cowers rather than leaving its site if turned.
sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +2. AC +2 Dex, touch 12, flat-footed 10. Printed BAB/grapple +1/+1, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +2, Will +0.
sections.Skills and feats: Hide +10, Listen +10, Profession +7, Search +8, Spot +11. Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Profession). Solitary, gang of 2–4 or mob of 7–12, any alignment and no treasure.
sections.Applying the encounter template: Choose a base creature with Charisma at least 6 from aberration, animal, dragon, giant, humanoid, magical beast, monstrous humanoid or shapechanger. Its type becomes undead with the incorporeal subtype. Keep size, saves and applicable base statistics, but remove prior attacks and special abilities, Strength and Constitution. HD becomes d12; Charisma rises by 2; fly 30 ft. perfect or keep a higher fly speed. Natural armor applies only to ethereal encounters. Add +8 racial bonuses to Hide, Listen, Search and Spot. The listed common geist uses Mind Games and Phantom Shift. CR 1/2; ability DC equals 10 + half HD + Cha modifier.

ruleNotes: The printed sample lists a grapple modifier despite its incorporeal subtype. It has no physical attacks.

name: Living Tattoo
classification: Construct; Medium incorporeal Dark Man shown in header
description: A dream spirit bound to a living host. The six printed samples are companions of a 5th-level human fighter with 40 HP.

sections.Actions:
Dark Man. Medium. Initiative +2, AC 13 (touch 12, flat-footed 11), BAB/grapple +3/+3, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +5. Attack or full attack is incorporeal touch +3 melee for 1d6 Strength damage. It fights as a shadow without creating spawn. Dodge. Hide, Listen, Spot and Survival each +8; Stealth adds +10 enhancement to Hide in shadows. Cooperation lends the host Hide while merged.
Living Spear. Medium object, 30 HP, hardness 5 or DR 10/magic, whichever applies; they do not stack. It cannot move independently. Use host BAB, attack and saves. Weapon damage 1d8 + 1. Dexterity 14, Int 4, Wis 14; no Str, Con or Cha. Guile can poison three penetrating attacks per day. Swiftness makes separation a free action and places it in the host’s hand.
sections.Traits: All samples have 5d10 and 30 HP. Treat them as summoned creatures for XP; overcoming their host earns the award. All understand their host’s languages and have construct traits, DR 10/magic, Empathic Link, Merge and Life Bond. They cannot heal naturally or receive curing magic. A separated tattoo loses 1 HP per full 24 hours. A tattoo with an undead model cannot create spawn.
sections.Violet Panther: Medium. Initiative +4, speed 40 ft., climb 20 ft., AC 15 (touch 14, flat-footed 11), BAB/grapple +3/+6, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +3. Str 16, Dex 19, Int 4, Wis 14, Cha 6. Claw +6 for 1d3 + 3; full attack two claws plus bite +1 for 1d6 + 3. Pounce, improved grab and rake 2d4 + 1 as a leopard. Scent, Stealth and darkvision 60 ft. Balance +12, Climb +11, Hide +9, Listen +7, Move Silently +9, Spot +7. Dodge and Weapon Finesse. It attacks without orders and must be told to stop.
sections.Grandfather Raven: Tiny. Initiative +2, speed 10 ft., fly 40 ft. average, AC 14 (touch 14, flat-footed 12), BAB/grapple +3/−10, space 2½ ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +2. Str 1, Dex 15, Int 4, Wis 14, Cha 6. Claw +4 for 1d2 − 5, two claws at full attack (minimum 1 damage on a hit). Listen +6, Spot +6, Weapon Finesse. Counsel grants discern lies and Worldliness grants tongues, each 1/day at CL 8.
sections.Winged Snake: Small. Initiative +4, speed 40 ft., fly 100 ft. average, swim 40 ft., AC 15 (touch 11, flat-footed 15), BAB/grapple +3/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +6. Str 13, Dex 10, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 10. Claw +7 for 1d4; full attack two claws plus bite +2 for 1d6 + 1. Wyrmling green dragon breath: 20-ft. cone of acid for 2d6, DC 13 Reflex half. Guile applies to the bite. Electricity resistance 10, immune to acid, water breathing. Concentration +5, Diplomacy +5, Escape Artist +5, Listen +7, Search +5, Spot +7. Improved Initiative.
sections.Silver Wolf: Medium. Initiative +2, speed 50 ft., AC 14 (touch 12, flat-footed 12), space/reach 5 ft./5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +2. Str 13, Dex 15, Int 4, Wis 13, Cha 6. Bite +3 for 1d6 + 1 with wolf trip: a hit allows a free trip attempt without an initial touch attack, and failure allows no counter-trip. Scent; while merged the host may use the tattoo’s scent and Survival as listed. Hide +3, Listen +6, Move Silently +4, Spot +4, Survival +1. Weapon Finesse.
sections.Running the encounter: Empathic Link is telepathy while touched or in line of sight. Merge or separate at will as a standard action; merging requires touch. While merged, damage to the host does not damage the tattoo. Attacks must specifically target the tattoo to harm it. Death of the host releases the spirit. Once per round as a free action the host can pay any number of their own HP to restore that many tattoo HP. The host recovers that loss only by natural healing. If the tattoo is destroyed, the host must make a Fortitude save at DC 10 + half tattoo HD or die. The site cannot hold another magic tattoo.
sections.Model abilities: A host binds only one tattoo. The model must be no larger than the host and have fewer HD. Treat tattoo HD as the host’s level and HP as three-quarters of host HP rounded down. Keep model attacks and movement; objects cannot move on their own. Merged and object tattoos save as the host. Add two suitable powers: Caution, chosen energy resistance 10; Cooperation, one skill while merged; Counsel, discern lies 1/day; Excitement, +1d6 electricity on three attacks daily; Guile, three penetrating attacks daily poison at Fort DC 13 for initial 1d4 Str and secondary 1d4 Con; Mystery, blindness/deafness 1/day; Piety, prayer 1/day affecting tattoo and host; Stealth, +10 enhancement to Hide in shadows; Swiftness, free-action separation; Vigilance, darkvision 60 ft.; Worldliness, tongues 1/day. Use CL 8 for listed daily spell effects and DC 10 + tattoo Wis modifier + spell level.
sections.Bonding: An Abber shaman’s rite takes 1d8 + 8 hours and deals 2d4 nonlethal damage to the host each hour. Afterward DC 14 Wisdom attracts a spirit. Bonding costs 200 XP per model HD, or 1/25 the object’s market price in XP with a minimum of 100 XP.

ruleNotes: The header uses the Dark Man example. The six forms do not have independent printed CRs. The source omits independent speed and AC for Living Spear and BAB/grapple for Silver Wolf. Use host rolls for Spear where directed.

name: Vistani
description: The printed encounter presents an expert traveling with a caravan. He may try to drive attackers away with the evil eye.

sections.Actions:
Attack or full attack. Dagger +0 melee for 1d4, or light crossbow +0 ranged for 1d8.
Evil Eye (Ex). Standard-action gaze against one target; merely looking at the expert does not trigger it. The printed male example’s Will DC is 11. Select one of the following on a failed save:
Paralysis. Paralyzed for 1d4 + 1 rounds. If failure exceeds four, instead paralyzed for 2 rounds, then convulsions deal 1d8 each round for 3 rounds. Afterward DC 15 Fortitude or die; on success the victim is unconscious but easily awakened.
Fear. Fear spell effect for 1d4 + 1 rounds.
Domination. Dominate person effect for 1d4 + 1 rounds.
Suggestion. Suggestion spell effect for one day or until the task is complete.
sections.Traits: Initiative +0, touch AC 10, flat-footed 13, studded leather +3. BAB/grapple +0/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +0, Ref +0, Will +4. Speaks Patterna; many know domain languages. The source gives Evil Eye DC 10 + half HD + Cha for a male and 12 + half HD + Cha for a female encounter NPC.
sections.Skills and feats: Bluff +5, Diplomacy +5, Listen +6, Sense Motive +8, Spot +6, Survival +8, and four ranks in a Craft, Perform or Profession skill. Voice of Wrath and Skill Focus in the selected skill. The printed racial +2 on Sense Motive and Survival is represented in the sample values.
sections.Encounter details: Any land. Gang of 3–6 or a caravan of 20–40 plus 30% noncombatants, four 3rd-level guards, a 5th-level captain, and a 7th-level raunie. Usually neutral, standard treasure. Guards may try to capture enemies instead of killing them.

ruleNotes: The entry does not give a specific range for Evil Eye. Use the standard 3.5 gaze range as a table default if needed.

name: Blood Hound
publication: Blood Spawn: Creatures of Light and Shadow
classification: Medium beast. Neutral. Vos hounds are neutral evil.
description: A war dog marked by a divine bloodline. A blooded handler can send it after a missing heir or a rival scion.

sections.Actions: Bite. One attack for 2d4 damage. A Vos hound instead bites for 2d6. A trained hound generally pins the quarry first. It attacks if attacked, ordered to bite, or convinced its handler is threatened.
sections.Tracking scions: Automatically detect a blooded trail within 1 mile or one left in the area in the last five days if rain has not cleared it. At up to 5 miles, or for a blooded trail in that radius from the last two days, use 50%. Add 15 percentage points for a matching bloodline derivation, 15 for a named target whose personal effect the hound can scent, and 10 for a target with a great bloodline. When seeking any scion, exclude the hunting party and prefer a matching derivation in the area over a nearer nonmatching one. The chance to find a specified unblooded person within 1 mile is 50%.
sections.Handler bond: Only a blooded handler can bond with the hound. A breeder’s imprinting ritual binds it for life unless its handler mistreats it, dies, or transfers the bond by ritual. With a handler of the same bloodline derivation, its combat morale is 20. If it believes that handler is in danger, it fights to the death unless called off by them.
sections.Bloodline and Seeming: Tainted bloodline 1d3, with a Bloodmark. There is a 5% chance of one extra minor blood ability appropriate to the derivation. Choose from Courage, Detect Illusion, Detect Life, Direction Sense, Iron Will, Long Life, Poison Sense, or Resistance. Slight Perception only warns it that something is wrong with a creature disguised by the Seeming. It cannot determine what the disguise hides.

otherStatistics: Very rare in Cerilia, principally Anuire. Solitary, or pack for Vos hounds. Appearing 1d4, or 3d6 Vos hounds. Active any time. Omnivore. Semi-intelligence 2–4. Medium, 4–6 ft. long. Morale 11–12 or 20. No treasure or magic resistance. Perception slight, Seeming none.
ruleNotes: The page 14 combat prose gives the ordinary bite as 2d4 + 1. The stat table on p. 15 gives 2d4. Use 2d4 as the table default.

name: Minion of the Lost
publication: Blood Spawn: Creatures of Light and Shadow
classification: Shadow World minion. Size and alignment vary by form.
description: The Lost magically reshaped the peoples in their service. Choose one of the three printed minion forms for the encounter.

sections.Actions: Use the printed form below. Minions speak their ancestral language and usually know only the mission their master gave them. Each form appears in groups of 3–24, or 10–100 in its community. None has a bloodline or blood abilities.
sections.Halfling Spawn: AC 6, MV 6 or 12 in trees, HD 2, THAC0 19, XP 270. Small, 3 ft. 6 in. tall, neutral evil. Attack once by missile at +1 to hit, or make three melee attacks: two claws for 1d4 apiece and a tail strangle. After a successful tail hit, the victim takes 1d8 each round held and must save vs. paralyzation each round or fall unconscious for 1d4 turns. Opponents take −4 to surprise rolls. The spawn gains +2 on saves against poison, wands, staves, rods, and spells. Uncommon in Cerilian or Shadow World forests, active by day, omnivore, intelligence 8–10, treasure J (O, P), morale 8–10. Perception middling, Seeming lesser.
sections.Masetian Spawn: AC 8 (10), MV 12, HD 3, THAC0 18, XP 175. Medium, 6 ft. tall, lawful evil. Make one attack by weapon or bite for 1d6. It is surprised only on a 1 or 2, and opponents take −3 to surprise rolls. Thief-style chances: 50% move silently, 45% hide in shadows, 45% detect noise, 90% climb walls. Rare in the Shadow World, active by day, omnivore, intelligence 11–12, treasure K (M, P), morale 11–12. No magic resistance. Perception lesser, Seeming none.
sections.Orog Spawn: AC 3 on the armored torso and 5 on the lower body or unarmored torso. MV 12, HD 4+4, THAC0 17, XP 270. Huge, 7 ft. tall and 20 ft. long, chaotic evil. Makes one attack for weapon damage +2. Favored weapons are an axe, crossbow, heavy long sword, mace, or polearm. Bright sunlight blinds and nauseates it and gives −3 to attacks and saving throws. Rare in the Shadow World, active any time, carnivore, intelligence 5–7, treasure J (O), morale 13–14. No magic resistance. Perception slight, Seeming none.

ruleNotes: The Masetian Spawn AC is printed as 8 (10). The form’s prose does not explain the parenthetical value. No single AC, speed, Hit Dice, THAC0, or XP applies to all three forms.

name: Seemer
publication: Blood Spawn: Creatures of Light and Shadow
classification: Corporeal Shadow World creature. Any size. Chaotic evil.
description: A creature of the Seeming that takes the shape of what its visitors most dread. Several witnesses might see different creatures in the same place.

sections.Actions: The seemer senses psychic energy from 500 yards and takes a form before it is seen. It attacks intelligent creatures from outside the Shadow World. An observer must save vs. paralyzation or the seemer automatically gains surprise. It can project one person’s fear to the whole group or show each person a different fear.
sections.Form attacks: Use the apparent creature’s movement and attack routines with the seemer’s own AC, HD, and THAC0. Cap each damage roll at 2d6, or use the attack’s normal damage if lower. A spellcasting guise can mimic spell-like attacks other than abjuration or divination. Apparent effects such as poison, aging, and level drain persuade observers they are affected, then wear off after 2d4 hours.
sections.Defenses and contact: It takes damage normally despite its disguise. In sunlight it takes −2 to attacks and damage. Shadow World natives with greater Seeming or better can communicate. A creature with extraordinary Seeming has a 5% chance per 10 Seeming points to gain its brief cooperation.
sections.Perception and Seeming: Perception slight (1–5), Seeming extraordinary (41+). Compare a viewer’s Perception with the chosen Seeming score to see through the magical guise. Disbelief alone does not end the effect. See pp. 6–8 for the setting procedure.

otherStatistics: Rare in the Shadow World. Solitary or in small groups, appearing 1–10. Active any time. Feeds on psychic energy. High intelligence 13–14. Morale 13–14. No treasure, bloodline, blood abilities, or magic resistance.

name: The Dispossessed
publication: Blood Spawn: Creatures of Light and Shadow
classification: Medium disembodied spirit of a living creature. Alignment varies.
description: A spirit driven from its living body by possession. Bands of the dispossessed sometimes gather in an abandoned home and act out their former lives.

sections.Actions: Touch of despair. One attack for 1d4 damage plus despair. When the cumulative number of hits equals the target’s Constitution, its spirit leaves and becomes one of the dispossessed. The attacker immediately takes over the body. If the target survives, despair lingers for one day per hit. Each casting of remove fear shortens this by one day.
sections.Depression: On first sight of any dispossessed spirit, save vs. paralyzation. On failure, movement is halved and attacks and Dexterity-based tasks suffer −3 or −25% while any dispossessed spirit remains within 100 yards. After leaving that range, the penalty falls to −1 or −10% for 4d6 hours plus one hour for each four hours of exposure. A character conversing with one saves again each turn.
sections.Defenses and behavior: Requires a +1 or better weapon to hit. As spirits of still-living bodies, they do not respond to holy water, turning, or attacks specific to undead. They can speak and move small or medium objects psychically. Evil spirits seize chances to possess others. Any spirit has a 60% chance to mistake a character for its old body and focus on that character. Restoring it to its own body, or the death of that original body, puts it to rest. Taking a different body offers no lasting relief.
sections.Seeming: Perception none, Seeming slight. Observers with low Perception can mistake them for corporeal people.

otherStatistics: Uncommon in the Shadow World. Appears in bands of 1d20. Active any time. No diet. Average intelligence 8–10. Medium, about 6 ft. tall. Morale 15–16. No treasure, bloodline, blood abilities, or magic resistance.

name: Will o’Shadow
publication: Blood Spawn: Creatures of Light and Shadow
classification: Tiny to Small floating creature. Chaotic neutral.
description: A dancing light that reaches Cerilia just ahead of an opening Shadow World portal. It draws vitality from the living before the portal pulls it back.

sections.Actions: Life drain. One touch for 2d8 damage to a Cerilian creature. It feeds on that loss without adding the damage to its own HP. A non-Cerilian takes a 1d8 burn instead and provides no nourishment.
sections.Feeding near the portal: When Cerilian characters are within a quarter mile, there is a 50% chance the creature feeds on their life energy rather than the surroundings. Affected Cerilians save vs. poison or take 2d6 damage. When Cerilians are on the Shadow World side of a portal about to open and a will o’Shadow is present, make that save with a 1-point penalty. It is normally invisible on that side of the portal.
sections.Defenses and tactics: Mundane weapon blows deal normal damage. Detect invisibility and shadow magic are the only magic specifically noted as effective. Magical light makes the creature invisible until the light goes out. Its lesser Seeming can camouflage it with blur, color spray, dancing lights, or hypnotic pattern. It usually avoids direct combat, attacks to replace lost energy when provoked, and tries to flee at 5 HP or fewer.
sections.Portal clues: One to three lights can precede a portal by 1 minute to 3 hours. A larger light means it is closer to opening. Nearby vegetation may stay wilted for 1d4 days per round the portal was open. The lights communicate with one another through their movement.

otherStatistics: Rare in Cerilia and the Shadow World. Solitary, appearing 1d3. Active at night in Cerilia or any time in the Shadow World. Feeds on Cerilian life energy. High intelligence 13–14. Treasure Q. Size 1–4 ft. across. Morale 15–16. No bloodline, blood abilities, or Perception. Seeming lesser.

name: Aboleth
description: Aboleths live in deep waters and remember their kind’s ancient rule. They use telepathy to learn what intruders want and bargain for obedience.

sections.DM tactics:
Opening move. If the party approaches the water together, use Enslave on a visible creature within 30 feet. If they close to melee, use Multiattack.
Between turns. A charmed target gives the aboleth a choice between healing with Psychic Drain and spending one legendary action on Tail Swipe.
Player options. The shoreline matters. A character with reach can strike from 10 feet away to avoid Mucous Cloud. Damage gives an enslaved ally another save.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The aboleth breathes in air and water.
Mucous Cloud. While the aboleth is underwater, a creature that touches it or hits it in melee from 5 ft. or closer makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it can only breathe underwater for 1d4 hours due to disease.
Probing Telepathy. If a creature telepathically communicates with the aboleth and the aboleth can see it, the aboleth learns its greatest desires.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning. A creature must also make a DC 14 Constitution save or contract a disease. For the first minute it has no effect and any magic that cures disease can remove it. After that minute the skin turns slimy and translucent, the creature can regain HP only while underwater, and only heal or another disease-curing spell of 6th level or higher removes it. Outside a body of water it takes 6 (1d12) acid damage every 10 minutes unless its skin is moistened before that interval elapses.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning.
Enslave (3/day). One creature the aboleth can see within 30 ft. makes a DC 14 Wisdom save. On a failure it is magically Charmed and controlled, loses reactions, and can communicate telepathically with the aboleth at any distance. The charm ends if the aboleth dies or they are on different planes. The target can repeat the save when damaged and, at most once in 24 hours, whenever at least 1 mile away. A success ends the charm.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three actions per round, regained at the start of the aboleth’s turn. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth cannot use these while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Swipe (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Psychic Drain (2 actions). One creature Charmed by the aboleth takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage. The aboleth regains HP equal to the damage dealt.
sections.Lair actions:
Act on initiative count 20, losing ties. The aboleth cannot use a lair action when incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Phantasmal Force. Cast phantasmal force without components on any number of visible creatures within 60 ft. The aboleth takes no other lair actions while maintaining Concentration on it. Any creature whose save succeeds or whose effect ends is immune to this lair action for 24 hours unless it chooses to be affected.
Grasping Tide. A pool within 90 ft. surges. Each creature on the ground within 20 ft. of such a pool makes a DC 14 Strength save. Failure pulls it up to 20 ft. into the water and knocks it Prone. Wait until a different lair action has been used before choosing this again.
Psychic Water. Choose any number of visible creatures in the lair’s water within 90 ft. Each makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or takes 7 (2d6) psychic damage. Wait until a different lair action has been used before choosing this again.
sections.Regional effects:
Underground surfaces within 1 mile of the lair are slick difficult terrain. Enemies who drink water from a source within 1 mile vomit it back up within minutes. Both effects fade over 3d10 days after the aboleth dies.
Projected Image. As an action, create an intangible likeness within 1 mile of the lair, either at a spot the aboleth has seen or at one a creature it has Charmed can currently see. The likeness looks, sounds, and moves like the aboleth for as long as it maintains Concentration. It can perceive, speak, and use telepathy from the likeness’s position. Any damage to the likeness ends it.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 13–14.

ruleNotes: The lair action does not specify a save DC for phantasmal force. Use DC 14 for its Intelligence save and Investigation check as a table ruling, matching the other lair actions.

name: Aboleth
publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
description: The aboleth spreads slime pox through close contact and uses ancient memories as a psychic weapon.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception 20, Stealth 9. Resists acid. Immune to psychic damage. Darkvision 120 ft. Deep Speech and telepathy 120 ft.

sections.Ability modifiers: Str +5, Dex −1, Con +6, Int +8, Wis +6, Cha +4.
sections.Traits:
Aberrant Resilience. Resistance to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed and Stunned. Advantage on saves against effects that alter its form.
Amphibious. The aboleth breathes in air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, it can choose to succeed.
Probing Telepathy. It learns the greatest desires of a creature it can see if that creature communicates with it telepathically.
Slime Pox. The infected creature can breathe in air and water, can regain HP only underwater, and takes 6 (1d12) acid damage for every hour it stays out of water or its skin goes without added moisture. Every 24 hours, make a DC 16 Charisma save. After three failures it becomes the aboleth’s protective thrall. After three successes it remains infected and autonomous. The results need not be consecutive. Stop making saves when one outcome is reached. Only heal or similar magic cures the disease.
Slimy Skin. Touching the aboleth or hitting it in melee from 5 ft. or closer requires a DC 16 Constitution save against Slime Pox.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Tentacle and Psychic Bolt. If two tentacle attacks hit the same target, it makes a DC 16 Constitution save against Slime Pox.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning.
Psychic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic.
Psychic Torrent (recharge 5–6). Up to three visible creatures within 60 ft. each make a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure, take 49 (14d6) psychic damage and become Incapacitated through the end of the target’s next turn. A success halves the damage and prevents the condition.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three actions per round, regained at the start of the aboleth’s turn. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth cannot use these while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Pinpoint every creature and trap within 60 ft. automatically.
Swim (1 action). Swim up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Slime Drain (2 actions). One creature with Slime Pox within 30 ft. takes 10 (3d6) acid damage. The aboleth regains HP equal to the damage dealt.
sections.Printed source: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 236.

name: Lich
description: An undead wizard whose phylactery anchors its soul. A lich can keep artifacts and spellbooks close at hand while hiding the phylactery elsewhere.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Skills Arcana +19, History +12, Insight +9, Perception +9. Resists cold, lightning, and necrotic. Immune to poison damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Poisoned. Truesight 120 ft., passive Perception 19. Common and up to five other languages.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The lich can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Rejuvenation. If its phylactery still exists when the lich is destroyed, a new body forms within 5 ft. of it in 1d10 days. The lich returns with full HP.
Turn Resistance. The lich has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
Undead Nature. The lich doesn't need air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Spellcasting:
18th-level wizard spellcaster. Intelligence is its spellcasting ability (save DC 20, +12 to hit). The following spells are prepared.
At will (cantrips). Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Magic Missile, Shield, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Detect Thoughts, Invisibility, Melf's Acid Arrow, Mirror Image.
3rd level (3 slots). Animate Dead, Counterspell, Dispel Magic, Fireball.
4th level (3 slots). Blight, Dimension Door.
5th level (3 slots). Cloudkill, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot). Disintegrate, Globe of Invulnerability.
7th level (1 slot). Finger of Death, Plane Shift.
8th level (1 slot). Dominate Monster, Power Word Stun.
9th level (1 slot). Power Word Kill.
sections.Actions: Paralyzing Touch. Melee spell attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (3d6) cold damage. The target makes a DC 18 Constitution save or is Paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the paralysis on a success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The creature has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Cantrip (1 action). Cast one cantrip.
Paralyzing Touch (2 actions). Use Paralyzing Touch.
Frightening Gaze (2 actions). Choose one visible creature within 10 ft. It makes a DC 18 Wisdom save against this magic or is Frightened for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. After it succeeds or the effect ends, it is immune to this gaze for 24 hours.
Disrupt Life (3 actions). Each non-undead creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 18 Constitution save against this magic. Failure deals 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. Success halves it.
sections.Lair actions:
In its lair the lich is CR 22 (41,000 XP). On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option that was not used the previous round. The creature can't use a lair action while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Recover a Spell Slot. Roll 1d8. Regain one spent spell slot of the rolled level or lower. If no spent slot qualifies, the action has no effect.
Negative Energy Tether. Link to a visible creature within 30 ft. Whenever the lich takes damage, the target makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure the lich takes half the damage, rounded down, and the target takes the remainder. The link ends on initiative count 20 of the next round or when either creature leaves the lair.
Spirits of the Dead. Call apparitions of creatures that died in the lair to attack one visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 18 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (15d6) necrotic damage. Success halves it. The apparitions vanish after the attack.
sections.Phylactery:
Feed the Phylactery. If the lich casts Imprisonment for this purpose, it can trap the body and soul of one target in its phylactery in place of the usual imprisonment options. The lich and phylactery must be on the same plane, and the phylactery holds only one creature at a time.
Dispel Magic cast on the phylactery with a 9th-level slot releases its prisoner. After 24 hours inside, the prisoner is consumed and only divine intervention can restore them to life.
The phylactery may require a particular ritual, item, or weapon to destroy. The print leaves that requirement to the DM. Imprisonment is part of the printed phylactery procedure and does not appear in this stat block’s prepared spell list.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 202–203, with official errata.

name: Tarrasque
description: A towering, heavily armored titan that surfaces after long periods of dormancy. It tears through walls and can swallow creatures whole.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Immune to fire, poison, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Poisoned. Blindsight 120 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The tarrasque can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The tarrasque has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Reflective Carapace. If targeted by Magic Missile, a line spell, or any spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll 1d6. The tarrasque is unaffected on every result. On a 6, it reflects the effect back at the caster, who becomes the target as if the tarrasque cast the spell.
Siege Monster. The tarrasque deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The tarrasque may first use Frightful Presence. It then makes one Bite, two Claw attacks, one Horns attack, and one Tail attack. It can use Swallow in place of Bite.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 36 (4d12 + 10) piercing damage. A creature hit by it is Grappled (escape DC 20) and Restrained while that grapple lasts. The tarrasque cannot bite another target until the grapple ends.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 28 (4d8 + 10) slashing damage.
Horns. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 32 (4d10 + 10) piercing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit 24 (4d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit by it falls Prone unless it succeeds on a DC 20 Strength save.
Frightful Presence. Choose any creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of the tarrasque. Each makes a DC 17 Wisdom save or is Frightened for 1 minute. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the tarrasque is within its line of sight. Success ends the effect. A creature that saves or whose fear ends is immune to this Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack against a Large or smaller creature the tarrasque is grappling. A hit deals Bite damage, ends the grapple, and swallows it. A swallowed creature is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover from outside the tarrasque, and takes 56 (16d6) acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque's turns. If a swallowed creature deals at least 60 damage to the tarrasque in a single turn, the tarrasque makes a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure it regurgitates all swallowed creatures. They land Prone within 10 ft. of it. If the tarrasque dies, the restraint from swallowing ends. A swallowed creature can spend 30 ft. of movement to exit the corpse Prone.
sections.Legendary actions:
The creature has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Move (1 action). Move up to half its speed.
Chomp (2 actions). Make one Bite attack or use Swallow.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 286, with official errata.

name: Adult Red Dragon
description: A territorial dragon that watches the land from high peaks and guards its hoard in mountain caverns. Heat and vents make a volcanic lair especially dangerous to intruders.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Skills Perception +13, Stealth +6. Immune to fire damage. Blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 23. Common and Draconic.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The dragon may first use Frightful Presence. It then makes one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. Choose any creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of the dragon. Each makes a DC 19 Wisdom save or is Frightened for 1 minute. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that saves or whose fear ends is immune to this Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 60-ft. cone make a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 63 (18d6) fire damage. Success halves it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The creature has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option that was not used the previous round. The creature can't use a lair action while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Magma Geyser. Choose a ground point the dragon can see within 120 ft. Magma erupts in a 5-ft.-radius, 20-ft.-high column. Each creature in it makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves it.
Tremor. Each other creature on the ground within 60 ft. of the dragon makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or falls Prone.
Volcanic Gas. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. A 20-ft.-radius sphere of gas spreads around corners and is lightly obscured. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round. Each creature starting its turn inside makes a DC 13 Constitution save or is Poisoned until the end of its turn. A creature poisoned this way is also Incapacitated.
sections.Regional effects: Small earthquakes are common within 6 miles of the lair. Water sources within 1 mile are unnaturally warm and sulfurous. Rocky fissures within 1 mile form portals to the Elemental Plane of Fire and admit creatures from that plane. These effects fade over 1d10 days after the dragon dies.
sections.Variant spellcasting: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose five spells of 5th level or lower. The dragon can cast each once per day without material components. Its Charisma spell save DC is 19 and its spell attack bonus is +11. The book leaves the spell choices to the DM.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 98–99 and 86.

name: Beholder
description: A floating eye tyrant carves vertical passages to keep intruders below its firing line.

sections.Defenses and senses: Natural armor. Perception +12, passive Perception 22. Immune to Prone. Darkvision 120 ft. Deep Speech and Undercommon.
sections.Traits: Antimagic Cone. At the start of its turn, choose whether its central eye projects a 150-ft. cone and which direction it faces. Apply Antimagic Field within the cone, including to its own eye rays.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Roll three distinct d10 results, rerolling duplicates. Shoot the matching rays at one to three targets it can see within 120 ft.
sections.Eye rays:
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom DC 16 or Charmed by the eye tyrant for 1 hour. If it harms the target, the charm ends.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution DC 16 or Paralyzed for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom DC 16 or Frightened for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
4. Slowing Ray. Dexterity DC 16 or speed is halved for 1 minute. While slowed, the target cannot take reactions and can take only one of an action and a bonus action on its turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution DC 16. Failure deals 36 (8d8) necrotic damage. Success halves it.
6. Telekinetic Ray. A creature makes a DC 16 Strength save. On failure, move it up to 30 ft. in any direction. It is Restrained until the start of the eye tyrant’s next turn or until the eye tyrant becomes Incapacitated. An object weighing 300 lb. or less, neither worn nor carried, can move up to 30 ft. in any direction without a save. The ray can also work a simple tool or open a door or container.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom DC 16 or Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage or another creature spending an action to wake the target ends the sleep. Constructs and Undead are unaffected.
8. Petrification Ray. Dexterity DC 16 or Restrained and beginning to turn to stone. Repeat the save at the end of the target’s next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure leaves the target Petrified until Greater Restoration or other magic frees it.
9. Disintegration Ray. A creature makes a DC 16 Dexterity save or takes 45 (10d8) force damage. If that damage leaves it at 0 HP, its body turns to fine gray dust. A Large or smaller nonmagical object or creation of magical force is destroyed without a save. For a Huge or larger object or creation of magical force, destroy one 10-ft. cube of it.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity DC 16 or take 55 (10d10) necrotic damage. If this leaves the target at 0 HP, it dies.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three legendary actions. Spend one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Regain spent actions at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Eye Ray (1 action). Use one randomly rolled eye ray.
sections.Lair actions:
In its lair, the beholder is CR 14 (11,500 XP). Act on initiative count 20, losing ties. No lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before the first turn if surprised.
Slime. A 50-ft. square of ground within 120 ft. becomes Difficult Terrain until initiative count 20 next round.
Grasping Walls. Walls within 120 ft. sprout grasping limbs until initiative count 20 on the round after next. Choose which creatures that start their turn within 10 ft. of these walls must make a DC 15 Dexterity save or become Grappled. Escape with a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
Wall Eye. An eye opens on a solid surface within 60 ft. It fires one random eye ray at a target of the beholder’s choice that the beholder can see, then disappears.
Use all three effects before repeating one, and never repeat on consecutive rounds.
sections.Regional effects:
Within 1 mile of the lair, creatures sometimes feel watched. While the beholder sleeps, minor changes to natural surfaces or unattended nonmagical objects can appear within 1 mile and vanish after 24 hours.
After the beholder dies, these regional effects fade over 1d10 days.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 26–28.

name: Death Tyrant
description: This undead beholder surrounds its floating skull with spectral eyes and uses its former victims as guards.

sections.Defenses and senses: Natural armor. Perception +12, passive Perception 22. Immune to poison damage and to Charmed, Exhaustion, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned and Prone. Darkvision 120 ft. Deep Speech and Undercommon.
sections.Traits:
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep.
Negative Energy Cone. At the start of its turn, choose whether its central eye projects an invisible magical 150-ft. cone and which direction it faces. Creatures in the cone cannot regain HP. A humanoid that dies there keeps its initiative and rises at the start of its next turn as a Zombie under the tyrant’s command if its body has not been entirely destroyed.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Roll three distinct d10 results, rerolling duplicates. Shoot the matching rays at one to three targets it can see within 120 ft.
sections.Eye rays:
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Charmed by the eye tyrant for 1 hour. If it harms the target, the charm ends.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution DC 17 or Paralyzed for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Frightened for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
4. Slowing Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or speed is halved for 1 minute. While slowed, the target cannot take reactions and can take only one of an action and a bonus action on its turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution DC 17. Failure deals 36 (8d8) necrotic damage. Success halves it.
6. Telekinetic Ray. A creature makes a DC 17 Strength save. On failure, move it up to 30 ft. in any direction. It is Restrained until the start of the eye tyrant’s next turn or until the eye tyrant becomes Incapacitated. An object weighing 300 lb. or less, neither worn nor carried, can move up to 30 ft. in any direction without a save. The ray can also work a simple tool or open a door or container.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage or another creature spending an action to wake the target ends the sleep. Constructs and Undead are unaffected.
8. Petrification Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or Restrained and beginning to turn to stone. Repeat the save at the end of the target’s next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure leaves the target Petrified until Greater Restoration or other magic frees it.
9. Disintegration Ray. A creature makes a DC 17 Dexterity save or takes 45 (10d8) force damage. If that damage leaves it at 0 HP, its body turns to fine gray dust. A Large or smaller nonmagical object or creation of magical force is destroyed without a save. For a Huge or larger object or creation of magical force, destroy one 10-ft. cube of it.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or take 55 (10d10) necrotic damage. If this leaves the target at 0 HP, it dies.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three legendary actions. Spend one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Regain spent actions at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Eye Ray (1 action). Use one randomly rolled eye ray.
sections.Lair actions:
