Incite Rampage (recharge 5–6). Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. If it can hear the pack lord and has Rampage, it can use its reaction to make a melee attack.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 163.

name: Aarakocra
description: This winged scout watches for elemental incursions. An aarakocra can attack in a dive or throw a javelin from the air.
otherStatistics: Perception +5, passive Perception 15. Aarakocra and Auran.

sections.Traits: Dive Attack. A melee weapon attack deals 3 (1d6) extra damage if the aarakocra hits after flying at least 30 ft. in a straight dive toward the target.
sections.Actions:
Talon. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Summon Air Elemental. Five aarakocra within 30 ft. of one another can perform an aerial dance. Each spends its action and movement on three successive turns and maintains Concentration during the dance. After the last dancer finishes its third turn, an Air Elemental appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. of the group. It is friendly to the summoners and follows their spoken commands. It stays for 1 hour, until it dies, until all five summoners die, or until any summoner dismisses it as a bonus action. Each summoner must finish a Short Rest before it can perform the dance again. When the air elemental returns to the Elemental Plane of Air, aarakocra within 5 ft. of it may go with it.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 12, with official errata.

name: Abominable Yeti
description: A solitary alpine predator roughly three times the height of a human. Snow conceals its approach, and its gaze can freeze a quarry in place.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +5, Stealth +4. Immune to cold damage. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 15. Yeti.

sections.Traits:
Fear of Fire. Taking fire damage gives the yeti disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks through the end of its next turn.
Keen Smell. The yeti has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use smell.
Snow Camouflage. The yeti has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in snow-covered terrain.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The yeti may use Chilling Gaze and makes two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.
Chilling Gaze. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. If it can see the yeti, it must make a DC 18 Constitution save against this magic. A creature that fails and lacks cold immunity takes 21 (6d6) cold damage and is Paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the paralysis on a success. A creature that saves or whose paralysis ends gains immunity to this yeti's gaze for 1 hour.
Cold Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 18 Constitution save, taking 45 (10d8) cold damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 306.

name: Faerie Dragon (Older)
description: A green, blue, indigo, or violet faerie dragon. These older butterfly-winged dragons build on the magic they learned in earlier colors.
otherStatistics: Arcana +4, Perception +3, Stealth +7. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13. Draconic and Sylvan.

sections.Traits:
Superior Invisibility. As a bonus action, the dragon can turn itself and its worn or carried gear Invisible. It maintains Concentration as it would on a spell. The effect ends when its concentration ends.
Limited Telepathy. The dragon can communicate magically with any other faerie dragon within 60 ft.
Magic Resistance. The dragon has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.
sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Spellcasting. Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13). The dragon needs no material components. Each color adds its spells to those of all younger colors.
Red (5 years or less), 1/day each. Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
Orange (6–10 years), 1/day. Color Spray.
Yellow (11–20 years), 1/day. Mirror Image.
Green (21–30 years), 1/day. Suggestion.
Blue (31–40 years), 1/day. Major Image.
Indigo (41–50 years), 1/day. Hallucinatory Terrain.
Violet (51 years or more), 1/day. Polymorph.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 1 piercing damage.
Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6). Exhale a puff of gas at one creature within 5 ft. It must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose its reactions for 1 minute. At the start of each affected turn, roll 1d6. On 1–4, it takes no action or bonus action and spends all its movement moving in a random direction. On 5–6, it stays put and can only repeat the DC 11 Wisdom save, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 133.

name: Faerie Dragon (Younger)
description: A red, orange, or yellow faerie dragon. These cat-sized dragons hide from view to watch their pranks play out.
otherStatistics: Arcana +4, Perception +3, Stealth +7. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13. Draconic and Sylvan.

sections.Traits:
Superior Invisibility. As a bonus action, the dragon can turn itself and its worn or carried gear Invisible. It maintains Concentration as it would on a spell. The effect ends when its concentration ends.
Limited Telepathy. The dragon can communicate magically with any other faerie dragon within 60 ft.
Magic Resistance. The dragon has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.
sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Spellcasting. Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13). The dragon needs no material components. Each color adds its spells to those of all younger colors.
Red (5 years or less), 1/day each. Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
Orange (6–10 years), 1/day. Color Spray.
Yellow (11–20 years), 1/day. Mirror Image.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 1 piercing damage.
Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6). Exhale a puff of gas at one creature within 5 ft. It must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose its reactions for 1 minute. At the start of each affected turn, roll 1d6. On 1–4, it takes no action or bonus action and spends all its movement moving in a random direction. On 5–6, it stays put and can only repeat the DC 11 Wisdom save, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 133.

name: Githyanki Knight
description: A githyanki raider who can shape a silver sword by force of will. Its blade can sever an astral traveler from their body.
otherStatistics: Plate armor. Passive Perception 12. Gith.

sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Spellcasting (Psionics). Intelligence is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). No spell components are required.
At will. Mage Hand (the hand is invisible).
3/day each. Jump, Misty Step, Nondetection (self only), Tongues.
1/day each. Plane Shift, Telekinesis.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The knight makes two Silver Greatsword attacks.
Silver Greatsword. Magical melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage. On a critical hit against a target in an astral body, such as one created by Astral Projection, the knight can forgo damage to cut the cord linking that target to its material body.
sections.Equipment: The silver sword has the properties of a greatsword, with the properties of a +3 greatsword while wielded by its creator.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 158–160.

name: Githyanki Warrior
description: An astral raider who combines greatsword strikes with psionic mobility.
otherStatistics: Half plate armor. Passive Perception 11. Gith.

sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Spellcasting (Psionics). Intelligence is the spellcasting ability. No spell components are required.
At will. Mage Hand (the hand is invisible).
3/day each. Jump, Misty Step, Nondetection (self only).
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The warrior makes two Greatsword attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 160.

name: Githzerai Zerth
description: A githzerai monk who follows the teachings of Zerthimon. Its psionics bolster its defense, power its strikes, and let it cross planes.
otherStatistics: Arcana +6, Insight +6, Perception +6. Passive Perception 16. Gith.

sections.Traits: Psychic Defense. The zerth adds its Wisdom modifier to AC when it wears no armor and wields no shield. The listed AC includes this bonus.
sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Spellcasting (Psionics). Wisdom is the spellcasting ability (save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). No spell components are required.
At will. Mage Hand (the hand is invisible).
3/day each. Feather Fall, Jump, See Invisibility, Shield.
1/day each. Phantasmal Killer, Plane Shift.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The zerth makes two Unarmed Strikes.
Unarmed Strike. Magical melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 161.

name: Banshee
description: The ghost of an elf haunts the place she died. She covets beautiful objects and flies into a rage at the sight of her reflection.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained.
sections.Traits:
Detect Life. The banshee can magically sense creatures within 5 miles, except constructs and undead. She knows their general direction only.
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as difficult terrain for her movement. She takes 5 (1d10) force damage if she ends her turn inside an object.
Sorrow Bound. She cannot travel more than 5 miles from where she died.
Undead Nature. She needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Corrupting Touch. Melee spell attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 12 (3d6 + 2) necrotic damage.
Horrifying Visage. Each non-undead creature within 60 ft. that can see her makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. Failure leaves it Frightened for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each turn, with disadvantage if she is in its line of sight. Success ends the effect. Once the creature saves or the effect ends, it is immune to this banshee's Horrifying Visage for 24 hours.
Wail (1/day). She can wail only outside sunlight. Each creature within 30 ft. that can hear her makes a DC 13 Constitution save. Failure drops it to 0 HP. Success deals 10 (3d6) psychic damage. Constructs and undead are unaffected.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 23.

name: Vampire
description: A vampire drinks blood and must retreat to its coffin, crypt, or grave by day. It can carry its coffin or enough grave dirt elsewhere to establish another resting place.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. Outside sunlight and running water, the vampire can use an action to become a Tiny bat, a Medium cloud of mist, or its true form. As a bat, it cannot speak, has a walking speed of 5 ft. and flying speed of 30 ft., and otherwise retains its stats apart from size. Worn gear transforms with it, and carried gear does not. Death returns it to true form. As mist, it cannot use actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It weighs nothing, flies 20 ft. with hover, can stop in hostile creatures' spaces, fits anywhere air can pass without squeezing, and cannot pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves in mist form and is immune to nonmagical damage other than sunlight damage.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Misty Escape. At 0 HP outside its resting place, it becomes mist instead of falling Unconscious. It is destroyed if sunlight or running water prevents the change. At 0 HP in mist form, it cannot revert voluntarily and must reach its resting place in 2 hours or be destroyed. When it arrives, it reverts and is Paralyzed until it has at least 1 HP. An hour spent there at 0 HP restores 1 HP.
Regeneration. It regains 20 HP at the start of each turn if it has at least 1 HP and is outside sunlight and running water. Radiant damage or damage from holy water stops regeneration at the start of its next turn.
Spider Climb. It climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Undead Nature. It needs no air. A vampire without a formal burial rests beneath a foot of soil at the place where it became undead.
sections.Vampire weaknesses:
Forbiddance. An occupant must invite the vampire before it enters a residence.
Harmed by Running Water. Ending a turn in running water deals 20 acid damage to it.
Stake to the Heart. If a wooden piercing weapon pierces its heart while it is Incapacitated at its resting place, it is Paralyzed until the weapon is removed.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. Starting its turn in sunlight deals 20 radiant damage to it. It has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks in sunlight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack (vampire form only). It makes two attacks, with at most one Bite.
Unarmed Strike (vampire form only). Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. It can instead Grapple the target on a hit (escape DC 18).
Bite (bat or vampire form only). Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature that is willing, Grappled by this vampire, Incapacitated, or Restrained. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. Reduce the target's maximum HP and heal the vampire by the necrotic damage taken. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a Long Rest, and the target dies if its maximum HP becomes 0. A humanoid killed this way and buried in the ground rises the next night as a Vampire Spawn under its control.
Charm. Choose one humanoid the vampire sees within 30 ft. If the target sees it, the target makes a DC 17 Wisdom save against magic. Failure leaves the target Charmed, treating the vampire as a trusted friend to protect and heed. The target interprets the vampire's actions and requests as favorably as it can and is willing to be bitten. It retains control of its own actions. Each harmful act by the vampire or its allies lets the target repeat the save, ending the effect on success. The charm ends after 24 hours, if the vampire is destroyed, if the two are on different planes, or if the vampire uses a Bonus Action to end it.
Children of the Night (1/day). If the sun is down, it magically calls 2d4 Swarms of Bats or Swarms of Rats. Outdoors it can call 3d6 Wolves instead. The creatures arrive after 1d4 rounds, ally with the vampire, and obey its spoken orders. They stay for 1 hour or until the vampire dies or dismisses them with a Bonus Action.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three legendary actions per round, spent one option at a time after another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them only after its first turn.
Move. It moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Unarmed Strike. It makes one Unarmed Strike.
Bite (2 actions). It makes one Bite attack.
sections.Regional effects: Bats, rats, and wolves grow more numerous around its lair. Within 500 ft., plants wither and grow twisted and thorny, shadows stretch and sometimes move on their own, and fog clings to the ground and occasionally takes strange shapes. The effects end 2d6 days after the vampire is destroyed.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 295–297 (stat block p. 297).

name: Nothic
description: This one-eyed lurker watches intruders from the dark. It trades secrets pried from other minds for magic items.

sections.Traits: Keen Sight. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It makes two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Rotting Gaze. Choose one creature it sees within 30 ft. The creature takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage if it fails a DC 12 Constitution save against this magic.
Weird Insight. Choose one creature it sees within 30 ft. The creature contests the nothic's Wisdom (Insight) with its Charisma (Deception). If the nothic wins, it magically learns one fact or secret about that creature. A creature immune to Charmed automatically wins the contest.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 236.

name: Beholder Zombie
description: A raised beholder still floats, bites, and fires rays, though it has no control over which ray it uses.

sections.Languages: Understands Deep Speech and Undercommon but cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Undead Fortitude. If damage drops it to 0 HP, it makes a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken. Skip the save if radiant damage or a critical hit dropped it. A success leaves it at 1 HP.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) piercing damage.
Eye Ray. Choose a target it sees within 60 ft. and roll 1d4 for the ray against that target.
1. Paralyzing Ray. A creature that fails a DC 14 Constitution save is Paralyzed for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on success.
2. Fear Ray. A creature that fails a DC 14 Wisdom save is Frightened for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on success.
3. Enervation Ray. A creature makes a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 36 (8d8) necrotic damage on failure or half on success.
4. Disintegration Ray. A creature that fails a DC 14 Dexterity save takes 45 (10d8) force damage. If this drops it to 0 HP, its body turns to dust. The ray destroys a Large or smaller nonmagical object or creation of magical force outright. For a Huge or larger object of either kind, it disintegrates a 10-ft. cube of it.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 316.

name: Revenant
description: The revenant animates a corpse to hunt a creature that wronged it. Its quest ends when its adversary dies or a year passes, at which point its body crumbles and its soul moves on.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Stunned.
sections.Traits:
Regeneration. At the start of each turn it regains 10 HP. Fire or radiant damage stops this healing at the start of its next turn. Its body is destroyed only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and does not regenerate.
Rejuvenation. When its body is destroyed, its soul stays behind. After 24 hours it animates another humanoid corpse on the same plane and returns to full HP. A Wish spell cast before it gains a new body can send it to the afterlife permanently.
Turn Immunity. Effects that turn undead do not affect it.
Vengeful Tracker. It knows the distance and direction to creatures it seeks revenge against, even across planes, and knows when a creature it tracks dies. The revenant hunts multiple adversaries one by one, starting with the creature that killed it.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It makes two Fist attacks.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, plus 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage if the revenant has sworn vengeance against the target. It can instead Grapple a Large or smaller target on a hit (escape DC 14).
Vengeful Glare. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. against which it has sworn vengeance. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, the target is Paralyzed until the revenant damages it or the end of the revenant's next turn. When the paralysis ends, the target is Frightened of the revenant for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the fear, with disadvantage if it can see the revenant.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 259.

name: Poltergeist
description: This invisible specter throws furniture and creatures with its mind.

sections.Variant: Uses the Specter base profile with CR 2, Invisibility, and Forceful Slam and Telekinetic Thrust in place of Life Drain.
sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Languages: Understands all languages it knew in life but cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Invisibility. It is Invisible.
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as difficult terrain for its movement. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to it.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Forceful Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (3d6) force damage.
Telekinetic Thrust. Choose one Medium or smaller creature or unattended object of up to 150 lb. within 30 ft. Against a creature, contest the poltergeist's Charisma check with the target's Strength check. If the poltergeist wins, it hurls the creature up to 30 ft. in any direction, including up. If the creature then hits a hard surface or heavy object, it takes 1d6 damage per 10 ft. moved. The text leaves the damage type unspecified. An object nobody is wearing or carrying can be hurled up to 30 ft. in any direction without a check. The poltergeist can use that object to make a ranged attack at +4 against one creature in its path, dealing 5 (2d4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 279.

name: Psychic Gray Ooze
description: A mature gray ooze can develop enough intelligence to attack another creature's mind.

sections.Variant: Uses the Gray Ooze base profile with Intelligence 6 and the additional Psychic Crush action.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone.
sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. It is blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 8.
sections.Traits:
Amorphous. The ooze can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Corrode Metal. After a hit from a nonmagical metal weapon, that weapon permanently loses 1 from its damage rolls. Penalties stack and destroy it at −5. Nonmagical metal ammunition is destroyed after it hits and deals damage. The ooze can eat through 2 inches of nonmagical metal in one round.
False Appearance. A motionless ooze looks like an oily puddle or wet rock.
Ooze Nature. It needs no sleep.
sections.Actions:
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning plus 7 (2d6) acid damage. Nonmagical metal armor worn by the target takes a permanent, stacking −1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor breaks once its AC drops to 10.
Psychic Crush (recharge 5–6). Choose one creature it senses within 60 ft. The creature makes a DC 10 Intelligence save, taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on failure or half on success.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 240, 243.

name: Owlbear
description: An owlbear hunts dense woodland at night. Bones and partly eaten carcasses lie scattered around its den.

sections.Traits: Keen Sight and Smell. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight or smell.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and one Claws attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 249.

name: Peryton
description: A winged, stag-headed hunter watches mountain passes for humanoid prey. Its shadow looks human until it eats a fresh heart.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: Understands Common and Elvish. Cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Dive Attack. After diving at least 30 ft. straight toward a target while flying, the peryton deals 9 (2d8) extra damage if it hits that target with a melee weapon attack.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy's reach does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Keen Sight and Smell. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight or smell.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Gore attack and one Talons attack.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (2d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 251. Includes the official Monster Manual errata.

name: Young Remorhaz
description: A young remorhaz waits beneath snow and ice for prey to move overhead. Frost giants raise some hatchlings to guard their strongholds.

sections.Senses: Darkvision 60 ft. Tremorsense 60 ft. Passive Perception 10.
sections.Traits: Heated Body. A creature takes 7 (2d6) fire damage if it touches the remorhaz or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 20 (3d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 258.

name: Half-Ogre
description: A half-ogre typically stands about eight feet tall. One descended from an ogre and an orc is also called an ogrillon.

sections.Actions:
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d8 + 3) slashing damage with one hand or 14 (2d10 + 3) with two.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 238.

name: Half-Red Dragon Veteran
description: A human veteran with red dragon ancestry. The sample wears plate in place of the ordinary veteran's splint armor.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 10 ft. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks. If the veteran has its shortsword drawn, it can also make one Shortsword attack.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage with one hand or 8 (1d10 + 3) with two.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.
Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. On failure it takes 24 (7d6) fire damage. On success it takes half.
sections.Half-dragon template:
Start with a beast, humanoid, giant, or monstrosity. Keep its statistics except for the template changes. Give it blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft., and Draconic in addition to its languages.
Color determines resistance. Black and copper resist acid. Blue and bronze resist lightning. Brass, gold, and red resist fire. Green resists poison. Silver and white resist cold.
Give the creature its dragon color's breath weapon. Use a wyrmling's breath for Large or smaller, a young dragon's for Huge, and an adult dragon's for Gargantuan. The minimum starting CRs to use this template without recalculating CR are 2, 7, and 8 for those size categories, respectively. If the base creature falls below that threshold, recalculate its CR using the Dungeon Master's Guide.
sections.Errata: Use the corrected sample profile. It has no listed saving throw proficiencies or Parry reaction.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 180. Includes the official Monster Manual errata.

name: Empyrean
classification: Huge celestial (titan), chaotic good (75%) or neutral evil (25%)
description: A child of the gods whose moods can alter the landscape. When it dies, its spirit returns to its home plane, where a divine parent may raise it.

sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks). No material components.
At will. Greater Restoration, Pass without Trace, Water Breathing, Water Walk.
1/day each. Commune, Dispel Evil and Good, Earthquake, Fire Storm, Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Actions:
Maul. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 31 (6d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be Stunned until the end of the empyrean's next turn.
Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +15 to hit, range 600 ft., one target. Hit 24 (7d6) damage. Choose acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, radiant, or thunder.
sections.Legendary actions:
The empyrean has three legendary actions and regains spent uses at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature's turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to take actions. If Surprised, it must wait until after its first turn in combat.
Attack. Make one attack.
Bolster. Each nonhostile creature within 120 ft. gains advantage on ability checks and saves and cannot be Charmed or Frightened until the end of the empyrean's next turn.
Trembling Strike (costs 2 actions). Strike the ground with the maul. Each other creature on the ground within 60 ft. must pass a DC 25 Strength save or fall Prone.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 130. Includes the official Monster Manual errata.

name: Grick Alpha
description: An oversized grick that often leads a pack. It waits in rocky crevices or above a well-traveled passage and strikes when prey comes within reach.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits: Stone Camouflage. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in rocky terrain.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Tail attack and one Tentacles attack. If Tentacles hits, it can make one Beak attack against the same target.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 22 (4d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 173. Includes the official Monster Manual errata.

name: Jackalwere
description: A jackal with the power to take human form. Jackalweres waylay travelers and use their sleep gaze to capture victims for lamias.

sections.Languages: Common. It can't speak in jackal form.
sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action it takes the form of a specific Medium human, a Medium jackal-humanoid hybrid, or its true Small jackal form. Only its size can change its statistics. Its equipment keeps its form. When it dies, the jackalwere returns to its true form.
Keen Hearing and Smell. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. It has advantage on attacks against a creature if one or more of its allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and that ally is not Incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Bite (jackal or hybrid form). Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Scimitar (human or hybrid form). Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Sleep Gaze. One creature the jackalwere can see within 30 ft. must make a DC 10 Wisdom save. On a failure, magical sleep makes it Unconscious for 10 minutes, or until someone spends an action shaking it awake. A successful save makes the creature immune to this jackalwere's gaze for 24 hours. Undead and creatures immune to Charmed are unaffected.
sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 193, with the global damage immunity wording from the 2018 errata.

name: Kenku
description: A wingless, feathered humanoid that communicates by reproducing sounds it has heard. A flock can use animal calls as signals.

sections.Languages: Understands Auran and Common. It speaks through Mimicry.
sections.Traits:
Ambusher. During the first round of combat, it has advantage on attack rolls against creatures it surprised.
Mimicry. It can reproduce sounds it has heard, including voices. A listener recognizes the imitation with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.
sections.Actions:
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit for 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 194, with the Ambusher timing from the 2018 errata.

name: Bullywug
description: A frog-headed swamp raider. Bullywugs train giant frogs and bring captive trespassers before their self-styled rulers.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Speak with Frogs and Toads. It can speak in Bullywug to convey simple ideas to frogs and toads.
Swamp Camouflage. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in swamp terrain.
Standing Leap. It can long jump up to 20 ft. and high jump up to 10 ft. A running start is optional.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It makes one Bite and one melee Spear attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage with two hands in melee.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 35.

name: Kuo-toa
description: An amphibious Underdark warrior with a net and an adhesive shield. Kuo-toa can bring deities into being through shared belief.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Otherworldly Perception. It senses any Invisible creature or creature on the Ethereal Plane within 30 ft. It can pinpoint those that are moving.
Slippery. It has advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape a grapple.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage with two hands in melee.
Net. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 5/15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. A hit leaves the target Restrained. A creature can spend an action to free itself or another creature with a successful DC 10 Strength check. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the AC 10 net destroys it and frees the target unharmed.
sections.Reactions: Sticky Shield. When a creature misses the kuo-toa with a melee weapon attack, the kuo-toa catches the weapon with its shield. The attacker must succeed on a DC 11 Strength saving throw to keep the weapon from sticking. A stuck weapon is unusable. The wielder is Grappled while it is stuck if the wielder can't or won't release it. A creature can take an action and make a DC 11 Strength check to pull the weapon free.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 199.

name: Kuo-toa Archpriest
description: The ruler of a kuo-toa domain and a cleric of the god it demands its subjects worship. It grants spells to its whips and can withdraw that power.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Otherworldly Perception. It senses any Invisible creature or creature on the Ethereal Plane within 30 ft. It can pinpoint those that are moving.
Slippery. It has advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape a grapple.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Spellcasting:
The archpriest casts as a 10th-level cleric, using Wisdom (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will: guidance, sacred flame, thaumaturgy.
1st level, 4 slots: detect magic, sanctuary, shield of faith.
2nd level, 3 slots: hold person, spiritual weapon.
3rd level, 3 slots: spirit guardians, tongues.
4th level, 3 slots: control water, divination.
5th level, 2 slots: mass cure wounds, scrying.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It makes two melee attacks.
Scepter. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) lightning damage.
Unarmed Strike. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 200, with the Unarmed Strike damage from the errata.

name: Kuo-toa Monitor
description: An enforcer who watches for dissent and carries out the archpriest's orders. Its unarmed strikes keep opponents from taking reactions.

sections.Armor: Natural armor with the monitor's Wisdom modifier added.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Otherworldly Perception. It senses any Invisible creature or creature on the Ethereal Plane within 30 ft. It can pinpoint those that are moving.
Slippery. It has advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape a grapple.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It makes one Bite attack and two Unarmed Strikes.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Unarmed Strike. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) lightning damage. The target can't take reactions until the end of the monitor's next turn.
sections.Variant: The monitor uses the Whip's statistics with AC 13, CR 3 (700 XP), and the actions above. The variant removes Spellcasting.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), monitor variant p. 198 and base Whip profile p. 200.

name: Kuo-toa Whip
description: A priest who draws its magic from the archpriest's favor. A whip can pin a captive with its pincer staff while its allies close in.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Otherworldly Perception. It senses any Invisible creature or creature on the Ethereal Plane within 30 ft. It can pinpoint those that are moving.
Slippery. It has advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape a grapple.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.

The whip casts as a 2nd-level cleric, using Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will: sacred flame, thaumaturgy.
1st level, 3 slots: bane, shield of faith.

sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 200.

name: Winged Kobold
description: Also called an urd, this kobold has leathery wings and uses high ledges to drop stones on intruders.

sections.Traits:
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Pack Tactics. It has advantage on attacks against a creature if one or more of its allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and that ally is not Incapacitated.

Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Dropped Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, one target directly below the kobold. Hit for 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 195.

name: Needle Blight
description: A walking thicket that shoots needles. When it senses danger, it sends pollen on the wind to alert nearby needle blights.

sections.Defenses: Immune to Blinded and Deafened.
sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. The blight is blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 9.
sections.Actions:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (2d4 + 1) piercing damage.
Needles. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. Hit 8 (2d6 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 32.

name: Vine Blight
description: A tangle of creeping vines that hides in the undergrowth and turns the surrounding plants against its prey.

sections.Defenses: Immune to Blinded and Deafened.
sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. The blight is blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 10.
sections.Traits: False Appearance. A motionless vine blight looks just like a tangle of vines.
sections.Actions:
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller target is also Grappled (escape DC 12) and Restrained for the duration of the grapple. While that grapple lasts, the blight cannot use Constrict on another target.
Entangling Plants (Recharge 5-6). Roots and vines fill a 15-ft. radius centered on the blight. They wither after 1 minute. Until then, the area is difficult terrain for creatures other than plants. When the plants appear, each creature the blight chooses in the area makes a DC 12 Strength save. On a failure, it is Restrained. As an action, a creature can make a DC 12 Strength check to free itself or an entangled creature within reach.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 32.

name: Sahuagin Baron
description: A four-armed sahuagin that rules an undersea domain, using sharks to support its raids.

sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. It has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Limited Amphibiousness. It breathes air and water. Without submerging at least once every 4 hours, it begins to suffocate.
Shark Telepathy. It can give magical telepathic commands to any shark within 120 ft.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two attacks with Claws or Trident.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.
Trident. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) when wielded in two hands in melee.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 264.

name: Sahuagin Priestess
description: A cleric of the shark god Sekolah who can command sharks and call up a spectral trident.

sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. It has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.

2nd level (3 slots). Hold Person, Spiritual Weapon (trident).

Claws. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d4 + 1) slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 264.

name: Quaggoth
description: A pale Underdark climber that fights with its claws and grows more dangerous when wounded.

sections.Defenses: Immune to poison damage and the Poisoned condition.
sections.Traits: Wounded Fury. At 10 HP or fewer, it has advantage on attack rolls. Each melee attack that hits deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 256. Passive Perception follows the official errata.

name: Quaggoth Thonot
description: A quaggoth that becomes the keeper of tribal lore after developing psionic powers.

sections.Defenses: Immune to poison damage and the Poisoned condition.
sections.Traits: Wounded Fury. At 10 HP or fewer, it has advantage on attack rolls. Each melee attack that hits deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage.

Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

Psionics. Wisdom, spell save DC 11. These spells require no components.
At will. Feather Fall, Mage Hand (invisible hand).
1/day each. Cure Wounds, Enlarge/Reduce, Heat Metal.

description: An Underdark hunter that blends into cave walls and leaves a sharp, clinging stench.

Chameleon Skin. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide.
Stench. When a creature other than a troglodyte starts its turn within 5 ft., it makes a DC 12 Constitution save. On a failure, it is Poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, it is immune to the Stench of every troglodyte for 1 hour.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on sight.

sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 290.

Magic Resistance. Roll saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.

Abomination form only. Charisma, save DC 15, no material components.

3/day: Suggestion.
1/day: Fear.

name: Night Hag (Coven Variant)
description: An exiled Feywild hag who sends nightmares to corrupt mortals and collect their souls. This hag belongs to a three-member coven.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The hag has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). No material components.
At will: Detect Magic, Magic Missile.
2/day each: Plane Shift (self only), Ray of Enfeeblement, Sleep.
sections.Actions:
Claws (hag form only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Change Shape. The hag magically becomes a Small or Medium female humanoid or resumes her true form. Her statistics stay the same and her equipment keeps its original form. She returns to her true form when she dies.
Etherealness. While carrying a Heartstone, the hag can magically cross between the Material and Ethereal Planes.
Nightmare Haunting (1/day). From the Ethereal Plane, the hag magically touches a sleeping humanoid on the Material Plane. Protection from Evil and Good or Magic Circle blocks the touch. The target suffers visions while contact continues. If the visions last at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from that rest and its maximum HP decreases by 5 (1d10). Greater Restoration or similar magic ends the reduction. If its maximum HP reaches 0 this way, the target dies, and if it was evil, its soul is caught in the hag’s Soul Bag.
sections.Night hag items:
Heartstone. Carrying this very rare stone lets the hag use Etherealness. Its touch also cures any disease. The hag takes 30 days to make one.
Soul Bag. This very rare item holds one evil soul at a time. Only the hag who made it can use it to catch a soul with Nightmare Haunting. Making one takes 7 days and a humanoid sacrifice.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 176, 178–179. The coven sidebar is on p. 176. The official errata corrects innate spellcasting, Claws, and resistance wording.
sections.Variant rules: Night Hag (Coven) is the other library label for this printed coven profile.
sections.Shared spellcasting:
A coven has three hags of any type. All three can use these wizard spells while they are within 30 ft. of one another. Track one pool of spell slots for the whole coven. Each hag casts as a 12th-level spellcaster using Intelligence. This hag uses spell save DC 15 and +7 to hit with spell attacks for this list.
1st level (4 slots): Identify, Ray of Sickness.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Locate Object.
3rd level (3 slots): Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots): Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot): Eyebite.
sections.Hag Eye: A coven can have one Hag Eye. A coven member on the same plane can spend an action to see through it. The eye has AC 10, 1 HP, and darkvision 60 ft. If it is destroyed, each coven member takes 3d10 psychic damage and becomes Blinded for 24 hours. All three hags must perform a 1-hour ritual to make a new eye. They cannot do so while Blinded, and an action outside the ritual makes them start over.

name: Sea Hag (Coven Variant)
description: A hag of polluted waters whose true face terrifies humanoids. She uses illusions to pass for another creature. This hag belongs to a three-member coven.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The hag breathes air and water.
Horrific Appearance. A humanoid that starts its turn within 30 ft. and sees the hag’s true form makes a DC 11 Wisdom save or becomes Frightened for 1 minute. It can save again at the end of each turn, with disadvantage if the hag is in its line of sight. A success ends the condition. Once the creature saves or the effect ends for it, it is immune to this hag’s Horrific Appearance for 24 hours. The creature can avert its eyes to skip the initial save unless it is Surprised or the hag reveals her true form suddenly. A creature that averts its eyes has disadvantage on attack rolls against her until the start of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Death Glare. Choose a Frightened creature within 30 ft. that the hag can see. If it can see her, it must make a DC 11 Wisdom save against the magic or drop to 0 HP.
Illusory Appearance. The hag magically disguises herself and her equipment as an ugly creature of her general size and humanoid shape. She can dismiss the effect as a bonus action, and it ends when she dies. Physical contact reveals discrepancies. Otherwise, spotting the illusion takes an action to inspect it and a successful DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

description: A troll whose severed limbs fend for themselves until it regrows them.

sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. The troll has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
Regeneration. The troll regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. If it takes acid or fire damage, it cannot regenerate at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.

sections.Loathsome Limbs:
If the troll takes 15 or more slashing damage at once, roll a d20. On 1–10, no part comes off. On 11–14, sever one remaining leg. On 15–18, sever one remaining arm. On 19–20, decapitate it. A decapitated troll dies only if it cannot regenerate. When it dies, its detached head dies too.
Detached parts. Each has AC 13, 10 HP and the troll’s Regeneration. Each acts on the troll’s initiative with its own movement and action. If the troll completes a short or long rest without reattaching the part, it grows a replacement and the detached part dies.
Leg. A detached leg has speed 5 ft. and cannot attack. The troll’s speed halves after losing one leg. With both legs gone, it falls Prone and can crawl if it has arms. With just one arm it crawls at half speed. With no arms or legs its speed is 0 and speed bonuses do not apply.
Arm. A detached arm has speed 5 ft. and makes one Claw attack on its turn. It has disadvantage unless the troll can see both the arm and the target. Each lost arm removes one Claw from the troll’s Multiattack.
Head. The detached head cannot move, retains Keen Smell, and can Bite only a target in its space. The body loses Bite and is Blinded unless its head can see the body.

sections.Actions:
Fists. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 216.

name: Adult Blue Dracolich
description: An adult blue dragon whose spirit animates its own bones through a phylactery gem.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed and Poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Roll saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The dracolich may use Frightful Presence, then makes one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 18 (2d10 + 7) piercing plus 5 (1d10) lightning damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 16 (2d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. The dracolich chooses creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of it. Each makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. On a failure, the creature is Frightened for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds or whose fear ends is immune to this dracolich's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Lightning Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 5 ft. wide makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. Failure deals 66 (12d10) lightning damage. Success halves it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dracolich has 3 legendary actions. It uses one option at a time, at the end of another creature's turn, and regains spent actions at the start of its own turn. It can't use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must wait until after its first turn.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 14 (2d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dracolich can then fly up to half its flying speed.
sections.Phylactery: When the body is destroyed, the spirit returns to its gem if the gem and body are on the same plane. If the gem then touches another dragon's corpse, the spirit can animate that body and return as a dracolich. If the gem is on another plane when the body is destroyed, the spirit passes into the afterlife.
sections.Lair options: The printed example has no listed lair actions. The template lets the DM keep, remove, or replace the base dragon's lair actions.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 83–84. The official errata corrects saves, skills, passive Perception and weapon attack bonuses.

name: Adult Red Dracolich
description: An adult red dragon restored to its own skeleton by the spirit bound to its phylactery gem.

sections.Template: Apply the printed dracolich template to the Adult Red Dragon. Change its type to undead and add the listed resistances, immunities and Magic Resistance. The book gives no separate red dracolich stat block or CR or XP adjustment. This profile carries over the base dragon's CR 17 and 18,000 XP.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed and Poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Roll saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The dracolich may first use Frightful Presence. It then makes one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. Choose any creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of the dracolich. Each makes a DC 19 Wisdom save or is Frightened for 1 minute. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that saves or whose fear ends is immune to this dracolich's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 60-ft. cone make a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 63 (18d6) fire damage. Success halves it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dracolich has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dracolich can then fly up to half its flying speed.
sections.Phylactery: When the body is destroyed, the spirit returns to its gem if the gem and body are on the same plane. If the gem then touches another dragon's corpse, the spirit can animate that body and return as a dracolich. If the gem is on another plane when the body is destroyed, the spirit passes into the afterlife.
sections.Lair actions:
If the DM retains the adult red dragon's lair actions, use these options. The template also allows the DM to remove them or substitute new ones.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option that was not used the previous round. The creature can't use a lair action while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Magma Geyser. Choose a ground point the dracolich can see within 120 ft. Magma erupts in a 5-ft.-radius, 20-ft.-high column. Each creature in it makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves it.
Tremor. Each other creature on the ground within 60 ft. of the dracolich makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or falls Prone.
Volcanic Gas. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. A 20-ft.-radius sphere of gas spreads around corners and is lightly obscured. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round. Each creature starting its turn inside makes a DC 13 Constitution save or is Poisoned until the end of its turn. A creature poisoned this way is also Incapacitated.
sections.Regional effects: If using the original lair's regional effects, small earthquakes are common within 6 miles of the lair. Water sources within 1 mile are unnaturally warm and sulfurous. Rocky fissures within 1 mile form portals to the Elemental Plane of Fire and admit creatures from that plane. These effects fade over 1d10 days after the dracolich is destroyed.
sections.Variant spellcasting: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose five spells of 5th level or lower. The dracolich can cast each once per day without material components. Its Charisma spell save DC is 19 and its spell attack bonus is +11. The book leaves the spell choices to the DM.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 83 for the template, pp. 98–99 for the adult red dragon and lair, and p. 86 for optional dragon spellcasting.

name: Demilich (Trap Soul)
description: Acererak and other demiliches of his tradition set soul gems into their skulls to feed their phylacteries.

sections.Traits:
Avoidance. If a saving throw would normally halve damage on a success, the demilich takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Turn Immunity. Immune to effects that turn Undead.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep. Use the printed 80 HP.
Enduring Existence. An intact phylactery restores the destroyed skull in 1d10 days. A demilich that still has the will to feed a soul to its phylactery can return to lich form by doing so.
sections.Actions:
Howl (Recharge 5–6). Every creature within 30 ft. that can hear the howl makes a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure drops it to 0 HP. Success leaves it Frightened until the end of its next turn.
Life Drain. Choose up to three visible creatures within 10 ft. Each makes a DC 19 Constitution save or takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. The demilich heals HP equal to the total damage dealt.
Trap Soul. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. It makes a DC 19 Charisma save. On a failure, magic traps its soul in one of the demilich's gems and its body and carried equipment disappear. On a success, it takes 24 (7d6) necrotic damage, which still traps its soul if it brings the creature to 0 HP. The demilich devours an imprisoned soul after 24 hours. At 0 HP the demilich crumbles to powder and leaves its gems behind. Crushing a gem frees any soul still inside. Its body reforms in the nearest unoccupied space in the same state it was in when trapped.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three legendary actions. Spend one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Regain spent actions at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Flight (1 action). Fly up to half its flying speed.
Cloud of Dust (1 action). Each creature within 10 ft., even around a corner, makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Blinded until the end of the demilich’s next turn. On a success that creature is immune to this effect until the end of the demilich’s next turn.
Energy Drain (2 actions). Every creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, reduce maximum HP by 10 (3d6). A target dies if its maximum falls to 0. Greater Restoration or similar magic can restore the lost maximum.
Vile Curse (3 actions). One visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On failure it is magically cursed and has disadvantage on attack rolls and saves. It repeats the save at the end of each turn and ends the curse on success.
sections.Lair actions:
In its lair, the demilich is CR 23 (50,000 XP). Act on initiative count 20, losing ties. No lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before the first turn if surprised. Roll a d20. On 11 or higher, choose an effect. Never repeat the same effect on consecutive rounds.
Tremor. Each creature on the tomb floor makes a DC 19 Dexterity save or falls Prone.
Antimagic. Choose one visible creature within 60 ft. Antimagic Field fills its space and moves with it until initiative count 20 next round.
Seal Healing. Choose any number of visible creatures within 30 ft. They cannot regain HP until initiative count 20 next round.
sections.Lair traits:
Use any of these optional tomb traits. A non-evil creature takes 16 (3d10) necrotic damage the first time it enters. Monsters in the tomb have advantage on saves against Charmed, Frightened and turning. A ward prevents unauthorized creatures from using teleportation or planar travel to enter or leave, but allows such movement entirely within the tomb.
After the demilich is destroyed, these effects fade over 10 days.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 48–49. Use the Acererak and His Disciples sidebar and the corrected Hit Dice.
sections.Variant: This is the Acererak and His Disciples variant. The library also lists it as Demilich (Variant).
sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from magic weapons.
sections.Damage immunities: Necrotic, poison and psychic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone and Stunned.

ruleNotes: The lair introduction mentions extra uses for legendary actions, but this printing does not specify a different action budget. The stat block gives three each round.
The Undead Nature prose says to maximize the Hit Dice. The official errata gives 80 HP with 32d4, which matches the average. Use the listed 80 HP for this profile.

name: Drider Spellcaster
description: A former drow cleric whose magic survived the transformation into a drider.
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 120 ft. Elvish, Undercommon.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saving throws against being Charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Spider Climb. The drider climbs difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict the drider’s movement.
sections.Innate spellcasting: Wisdom (spell save DC 14), with no material components. At will: Dancing Lights. 1/day each: Darkness, Faerie Fire.
sections.Spellcasting:
7th-level cleric spellcaster. Wisdom (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). Prepared spells:
Cantrips at will: Poison Spray, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots): Bane, Detect Magic, Sanctuary.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Silence.
3rd level (3 slots): Clairvoyance, Dispel Magic.
4th level (2 slots): Divination, Freedom of Movement.
sections.Variant: This is the cleric example listed elsewhere in the library as Drider (variant). It keeps the Drider's base traits and adds cleric Spellcasting. Wisdom 16 raises Perception, passive Perception and the innate spell save DC by 1. The sidebar has no separate CR.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three longsword attacks or three longbow attacks. One of them can be replaced with a bite.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 2 (1d4) piercing plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) with two hands.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing plus 4 (1d8) poison damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 120, including the spellcasting variant and official range errata.

description: A spiderlike creature that tends spiders and traps prey in dense forest webs.

sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The ettercap climbs difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
Web Sense. When it touches a web, it knows the location of any other creature touching the same web.
Web Walker. Webbing does not impede its movement.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing plus 4 (1d8) poison damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save. On failure it is Poisoned for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on a success.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit, the target is Restrained. The target can spend an action on a DC 11 Strength check to break free. Destroying the web also frees it. The web has AC 10 and 5 HP. It is vulnerable to fire and immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 131. Web damage defenses include the official errata.

name: Ice Devil
description: A towering insectile commander of the infernal armies, with powerful mandibles and a barbed tail.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness leaves the devil's darkvision unchanged.
Magic Resistance. The devil has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite, one Claws, and one Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing and 10 (3d6) cold damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d4 + 5) slashing and 10 (3d6) cold damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning and 10 (3d6) cold damage.
Wall of Ice (Recharge 6). Magically form an opaque ice barrier on a solid surface the devil can see within 60 ft. The ice is 1 ft. thick. The devil chooses a wall up to 30 ft. long and 10 ft. high or a hemispherical dome up to 20 ft. across.
When it forms, each creature occupying its space is pushed out by the shortest route. The creature can choose which side it ends up on unless it is Incapacitated. It then rolls a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 35 (10d6) cold damage on a failure or half on a success.
The barrier lasts 1 minute or ends early if the devil becomes Incapacitated or dies. Each 10-ft. section has AC 5 and 30 HP, is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to acid, cold, necrotic, poison, and psychic damage.
A destroyed section leaves frigid air in its space. A creature that finishes passing through the air on a turn, including by forced movement, makes a DC 17 Constitution save. It takes 17 (5d6) cold damage on a failure or half on a success. The air clears when the rest of the barrier vanishes.
sections.Infernal return: A devil that dies outside the Nine Hells vanishes in sulfurous smoke or dissolves into ichor. It immediately reforms at full strength on its home layer. Death in the Nine Hells destroys it permanently.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 67, 69 and 75. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Erinyes

sections.Damage resistances: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.

name: Green Hag
description: A swamp or woodland hag who uses false cries for help to lure travelers into danger.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. She can breathe air and water.
Mimicry. She can imitate animal sounds and humanoid voices. A listener identifies the imitation with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 12). She needs no material components.
At will: Dancing Lights, Minor Illusion, Vicious Mockery.
sections.Actions:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Illusory Appearance. The hag disguises herself and everything she wears or carries as a creature of her general size and humanoid shape. She can end the effect with a bonus action, and it ends if she dies. Touch can reveal discrepancies between the illusion and her body. A creature can also spend an action inspecting the disguise and identify it with a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check.
Invisible Passage. She becomes Invisible, as does everything she wears or carries. The effect ends when she attacks, casts a spell, or loses Concentration as if concentrating on a spell. During the effect she leaves no physical evidence of her passage. Only magic can track her.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 177.

sections.Variant rules: Green Hag (Coven) is the other library label for the same printed coven profile.
sections.Shared spellcasting:
A coven has three hags of any type. All three can use these wizard spells while they are within 30 ft. of one another. Track one pool of spell slots for the whole coven. Each hag casts as a 12th-level spellcaster using Intelligence. This hag uses spell save DC 13 and +5 to hit with spell attacks for this list.
1st level (4 slots): Identify, Ray of Sickness.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Locate Object.
3rd level (3 slots): Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots): Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot): Eyebite.
sections.Hag Eye: A coven can have one Hag Eye. A coven member on the same plane can spend an action to see through it. The eye has AC 10, 1 HP, and darkvision 60 ft. If it is destroyed, each coven member takes 3d10 psychic damage and becomes Blinded for 24 hours. All three hags must perform a 1-hour ritual to make a new eye. They cannot do so while Blinded, and an action outside the ritual makes them start over.
