name: Aboleth
description: This amphibious aberration gathers servants in sunken ruins and preserves memories of long-dead worlds.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Eldritch Restoration. When destroyed, the aboleth returns in a new body at full HP after 5d10 days. It reappears in the Far Realm or another location chosen by the DM.
Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Mucus Cloud. While the aboleth is underwater, each creature within a 5-ft. Emanation from it makes a DC 14 Constitution save at the end of the aboleth’s turn. Failure curses the creature. Its skin becomes slimy, it can breathe air and water, and it can regain HP only underwater. Outside a body of water it takes 6 (1d12) acid damage at the end of every 10 minutes unless its skin is moistened before that interval is up.
Probing Telepathy. When a creature the aboleth can see talks to it telepathically, it learns that creature’s greatest desires.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks, then use Consume Memories or Dominate Mind if available.
Tentacle. Melee attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. One of the four tentacles also Grapples a target that is Large or smaller (escape DC 14).
Consume Memories. One creature within 30 ft. that the aboleth has Charmed or Grappled makes a DC 16 Intelligence save. Failure deals 10 (3d6) psychic damage and success halves it. The aboleth learns the memories of a Humanoid reduced to 0 HP by this action.
Dominate Mind (2/day). One visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 16 Wisdom save. Failure leaves it Charmed until the aboleth dies, the two are on different planes, or the creature succeeds on a repeat save. While Charmed it acts as the aboleth’s ally, obeys its control within 60 ft., and can communicate telepathically with it at any distance. It repeats the save whenever it takes damage and after every 24 hours it spends at least 1 mile away.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Lash. Make one Tentacle attack.
Psychic Drain. If the aboleth has a creature Charmed or Grappled, use Consume Memories and regain 5 (1d10) HP.
sections.Regional effects:
Foul Water. Water sources within 1 mile of the lair are befouled. Anyone other than the aboleth or its allies who drinks this water must make a DC 15 Constitution save or become Poisoned for 1 hour.
Psionic Projection. In its lair the aboleth can cast Project Image without components. It uses Intelligence (save DC 16), the spell reaches 1 mile, and its telepathy can originate in the image’s space.
Both effects end immediately if the aboleth dies or its lair moves.
sections.In its lair: 7,200 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 12.

name: Beholder
description: A floating eye tyrant carves tunnels with its rays and collects the adventurers it petrifies.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Use Eye Rays three times.
Bite. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Choose a visible target within 120 ft. and roll 1d10 for its magical ray. Reroll a ray the beholder has already used during this turn. All saves below are DC 16.
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) psychic damage and leaves the target Charmed for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Paralyzed. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) psychic damage and leaves the target Frightened until the end of its next turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
4. Slowing Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Until the end of its next turn, the target has half Speed, cannot take Reactions, and has to choose between taking an action and taking a Bonus Action on its turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the other effects.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) poison damage and leaves the target Poisoned until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned this way, it cannot regain HP. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
6. Telekinetic Ray. Strength save. A Gargantuan target succeeds automatically. On failure the beholder moves the target up to 30 ft. in any direction and Restrains it until the start of the beholder’s next turn or until the beholder is Incapacitated. This ray can also manipulate objects precisely, for example to open a door or operate a tool.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom save. Constructs and Undead succeed automatically. On failure the target is Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage ends the effect. A creature within 5 ft. can also use an action to wake the target.
8. Petrification Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Restrained. If it is still Restrained at the end of its next turn, it repeats the save. Success ends the effect. Failure changes Restrained to Petrified.
9. Disintegration Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 36 (8d8) force damage and disintegrates a 10-ft. cube of a targeted nonmagical object or magical force creation. Success halves the damage. Either way, a creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray turns to dust.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) necrotic damage and success halves it. A creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray dies.
sections.Bonus actions: Antimagic Cone. Project a 150-ft. Cone from the central eye. Until the start of the beholder’s next turn, the area acts as Antimagic Field and suppresses even its own Eye Rays.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Chomp. Make two Bite attacks.
Glare. Use Eye Rays.
sections.Regional effects:
Scopophobia. Creatures within 1 mile feel watched. A creature other than the beholder or its allies that finishes a Short Rest within that area makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On failure the rest grants no benefit.
Warping Terrain. Any creature other than the beholder that rolls a natural 1 on a D20 Test within 1 mile of the lair falls Prone.
Both effects end immediately if the beholder dies or its lair moves.
sections.In its lair: 11,500 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 35–36. The stat block is on p. 36 and the regional effects are on p. 35.

name: Death Tyrant
description: A beholder can pursue its designs after death as an immense floating skull orbited by ten magical eyes.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone.
sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Use Eye Rays three times.
Bite. Melee attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Choose a visible target within 120 ft. and roll 1d10 for its magical ray. Reroll a ray the death tyrant has already used during this turn. All saves below are DC 17.
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) psychic damage and leaves the target Charmed for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Paralyzed. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 10 (3d6) psychic damage and leaves the target Frightened until the end of its next turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
4. Slowing Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Until the end of its next turn, the target has half Speed, cannot take Reactions, and has to choose between taking an action and taking a Bonus Action on its turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the other effects.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 16 (3d10) poison damage and leaves the target Poisoned until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned this way, it cannot regain HP. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
6. Telekinetic Ray. Strength save. A Gargantuan target succeeds automatically. On failure the death tyrant moves the target up to 30 ft. in any direction and Restrains it until the start of the death tyrant’s next turn or until the death tyrant is Incapacitated. This ray can also manipulate objects precisely, for example to open a door or operate a tool.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom save. Constructs and Undead succeed automatically. On failure the target is Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage ends the effect. A creature within 5 ft. can also use an action to wake the target.
8. Petrification Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Restrained. If it is still Restrained at the end of its next turn, it repeats the save. Success ends the effect. Failure changes Restrained to Petrified.
9. Disintegration Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 36 (8d8) force damage and disintegrates a 10-ft. cube of a targeted nonmagical object or magical force creation. Success halves the damage. Either way, a creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray turns to dust.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) necrotic damage and success halves it. A creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray dies.
sections.Bonus actions: Negative Energy Cone. An imperceptible magical wave from its central eye covers a 150-ft. Cone. Creatures in the cone cannot regain HP until its next turn starts. Any intact Humanoid corpse in the cone immediately rises as its controlled Zombie and acts right after it on the same initiative count.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Chomp. Make two Bite attacks.
Glare. Use Eye Rays.
sections.Regional effects:
Negative Energy Suffusion. Whenever a spell restores a creature’s HP within 1 mile of the lair, subtract 1d10 from the amount healed.
Scopophobia. Creatures within 1 mile feel watched. A creature other than the death tyrant or its allies that finishes a Short Rest within that area makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On failure the rest grants no benefit.
Both effects end immediately if the death tyrant dies or its lair moves.
sections.In its lair: 13,000 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 94–95. The stat block is on p. 95 and the regional effects are on p. 94.

name: Lich
description: A lich binds its soul to a hidden spirit jar. It can outlast the loss of its body while that jar remains intact.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (4/day, 5/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Spirit Jar. If destroyed while it has a spirit jar, the lich returns at full HP after 1d10 days. Its new body appears in an unoccupied space in its lair.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Eldritch Burst and Paralyzing Touch.
Eldritch Burst. Melee or ranged attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit deals 31 (4d12 + 5) force damage.
Paralyzing Touch. Melee attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit deals 15 (3d6 + 5) cold damage and leaves the target Paralyzed until the start of the lich’s next turn.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of these spells as an action, using Intelligence (spell save DC 20).
At will. Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Fireball (level 5), Invisibility, Lightning Bolt (level 5), Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
2/day each. Animate Dead, Dimension Door, Plane Shift.
1/day each. Chain Lightning, Finger of Death, Power Word Kill, Scrying.
sections.Reactions: Protective Magic. Cast Counterspell or Shield when the chosen spell’s trigger occurs. Use the same spellcasting ability and save DC as Spellcasting.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Deathly Teleport. Teleport up to 60 ft. to a visible unoccupied space. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space left behind takes 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Disrupt Life. Each non-Undead creature in a 20-ft. Emanation from the lich makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 31 (9d6) necrotic damage and success halves it. After using this option, wait until the start of its next turn before using it again.
Frightening Gaze. The lich casts Fear using Intelligence (DC 20), as in its Spellcasting action. It can't use this option again until the start of its next turn.
sections.Regional effects:
All-Seeing. In its lair the lich can cast Clairvoyance with no components, using the ability listed under Spellcasting.
Inevitable Siphon. The lich consumes the soul of any Humanoid that dies within 1 mile of its lair. Only True Resurrection or Wish can bring that Humanoid back to life.
Both effects end immediately if the lich is destroyed or moves its lair. They return if the lich gains a new body through Spirit Jar.
sections.In its lair: 41,000 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 196.

name: Demilich
description: A lich whose body has decayed can rise again as a floating skull, often set with gems or marked with arcane sigils.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Stunned.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Undead Restoration. If destroyed, the demilich regains full HP when it reforms after 1d10 days. Casting Wish on its remains prevents this return.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Necrotic Burst attacks.
Necrotic Burst. Melee or ranged attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit deals 24 (7d6) necrotic damage.
Howl (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. Emanation from the demilich makes a DC 19 Constitution save. Failure deals 70 (20d6) psychic damage. Each target is Frightened until the start of the demilich’s next turn regardless of the save result.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Energy Drain. One visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 19 Constitution save. Failure reduces its HP maximum by 14 (4d6). After use, wait until the start of the demilich’s next turn before choosing this option again.
Grave-Dust Flight. Fly up to the demilich’s Fly Speed. Each creature within 5 ft. of its path makes a DC 19 Constitution save once. Failure leaves that creature Blinded until the end of the demilich’s next turn. After use, wait until the start of that turn before choosing this option again.
Necrosis. Make one Necrotic Burst attack.
sections.Regional effects:
Enervating Domain. When a creature other than the demilich or an ally finishes a Long Rest within 1 mile of the lair, it makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure reduces its HP maximum by 1d4 until it finishes a Long Rest outside the area.
Travel Ward. Teleportation and planar travel cannot take creatures into or out of the lair.
Both effects end immediately if the demilich dies or its lair moves.
sections.In its lair: 22,000 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 96.

name: Tarrasque
description: This immense, spiked titan wakes only rarely. It attacks large creatures and tears apart bridges, ships, and buildings.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (6/day). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Reflective Carapace. Roll 1d6 when the tarrasque is targeted by Magic Missile or a spell requiring a ranged attack roll. The tarrasque is unaffected. On a 6, redirect the spell to the caster.
Siege Monster. Deals double damage to structures and objects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and three more attacks using Claw or Tail in any combination.
Bite. Melee attack, +19 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) piercing damage and Grapples the target (escape DC 20). Until the grapple ends the target is Restrained and cannot teleport.
Claw. Melee attack, +19 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee attack, +19 to hit, reach 30 ft. Hit deals 23 (3d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit also falls Prone.
Thunderous Bellow (recharge 5–6). Every creature and every object that is neither worn nor carried in a 150-ft. Cone makes a DC 27 Constitution save. Failure deals 78 (12d12) thunder damage and leaves the target Deafened and Frightened until the end of its next turn. Success halves the damage and avoids both conditions.
sections.Bonus actions:
Swallow. One Large or smaller creature Grappled by the tarrasque makes a DC 27 Strength save. On failure, the grapple ends and the creature is swallowed. The tarrasque can have up to six creatures inside it. A swallowed creature is Blinded and Restrained, cannot teleport, has Total Cover against outside attacks and effects, and takes 56 (16d6) acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque’s turns.
When a creature inside deals at least 60 damage to the tarrasque in a single turn, it makes a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure it expels everyone it swallowed, and they fall Prone within 10 ft. If the tarrasque dies, swallowed creatures stop being Restrained. They can spend 20 ft. of movement to escape and exit Prone.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses. Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Onslaught. Move up to half the tarrasque’s Speed and make a Claw or Tail attack.
World-Shaking Movement. Move up to its Speed. At the end of that movement, each creature in a 60-ft. Emanation from the tarrasque loses Concentration. Medium and smaller creatures there also fall Prone. Wait until the start of the tarrasque’s next turn before repeating this option.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 305.

name: Kraken
description: These immense tentacled titans were weapons of the gods. They rise from deep lairs to rip through fleets and coastal settlements.

sections.Languages: understands Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial but can't speak; telepathy 120 ft..
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Legendary Resistance (4/day, 5/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Siege Monster. Deals double damage to structures and objects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks, then use Fling, Lightning Strike, or Swallow.
Tentacle. Melee attack, +17 to hit, reach 30 ft. Hit deals 24 (4d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. One of the ten tentacles Grapples its target (escape DC 20) and Restrains it until the grapple ends.
Fling. Throw a Large or smaller creature Grappled by the kraken into a visible space within 60 ft. that is not in the air. The thrown creature and all creatures in that space make DC 25 Dexterity saves. Failure deals 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and leaves the target Prone. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
Lightning Strike. One visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 33 (6d10) lightning damage and success halves it.
Swallow. One creature Grappled by the kraken makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing damage. A Large or smaller target that fails is also swallowed and its grapple ends. The kraken can have up to four creatures swallowed. A swallowed creature is Restrained, has Total Cover against outside attacks and effects, and takes 24 (7d6) acid damage at the start of each of its own turns.
When a creature inside deals at least 50 damage to the kraken in a single turn, the kraken makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure, every swallowed creature is expelled and falls Prone within 10 ft. If the kraken dies, swallowed creatures stop being Restrained. They can spend 15 ft. of movement to escape the corpse and exit Prone.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Storm Bolt. Use Lightning Strike.
Toxic Ink. Use while underwater. Each creature in a 15-ft. Emanation from the kraken makes a DC 23 Constitution save. Failure leaves it Blinded and Poisoned until the end of the kraken’s next turn. The kraken then moves up to its Speed. It cannot use this option again until the start of its next turn.
sections.Regional effects:
Ocean Tyrant. Beasts are Charmed while within 1 mile of the lair.
Sea and Storms. In its lair, the kraken can cast Control Weather using Intelligence and without spell components.
Both effects end immediately if the kraken dies or its lair moves.
sections.In its lair: 62,000 XP. The traits and Legendary actions sections give the increased resource limits.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 187.

name: Mind Flayer
description: A psionic hunter that feeds on brains and draws its victims into schemes of domination.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The mind flayer has Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Tentacles. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 22 (4d8 + 4) Psychic damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit by the attack is Grappled by all the mind flayer's tentacles (escape DC 14). It is also Stunned until the grapple ends.
Extract Brain. One creature grappled by the mind flayer's Tentacles makes a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) Piercing damage. Success halves the damage. If the damage leaves the target at 0 HP, the mind flayer kills it and eats its brain.
Mind Blast (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Intelligence save. Failure deals 31 (6d8 + 4) Psychic damage and leaves the target Stunned until the end of the mind flayer's next turn. Success halves the damage and prevents the stun.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of these spells as an action. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability, with save DC 15. These spells require no components.
At will. Detect Thoughts.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 214.

name: Mind Flayer Arcanist
description: The arcanist combines psionics with spellcraft. Other mind flayers tend to fear or despise these experiments.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The arcanist has Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Arcane Tentacles attacks.
Arcane Tentacles. Melee or ranged attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. A hit deals 27 (4d10 + 5) Psychic damage. The arcanist can teleport the target up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space on a surface or liquid large enough to support the target. If the damage reduces the target to 0 HP, the arcanist kills it and magically consumes its brain.
Mind Burst (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 40-ft. emanation from the arcanist makes a DC 17 Intelligence save. Failure deals 41 (8d8 + 5) Psychic damage and leaves the target Stunned until the end of the arcanist's next turn. Success halves the damage and prevents the stun.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of these spells as an action. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability, with save DC 17. These spells require no components.
At will. Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible).
1/day each. Clairvoyance, Dimension Door, Fireball (level 5), Lightning Bolt (level 5), Plane Shift (self only), Sending.
sections.Reactions: Shield (2/day). Cast Shield when the spell's trigger occurs. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 214.

name: Intellect Devourer
description: This walking brain hunts for bodies it can occupy. It uses the host's knowledge to hide the substitution and serve its mind flayer creators.

sections.Languages: Understands Deep Speech but can't speak. Telepathy 60 ft..
sections.Traits: Detect Intelligence. It magically locates creatures within 300 ft. whose Intelligence is 3 or higher. Barriers can't block this sense.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claw attack and use Devour Intellect.
Claw. Melee attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) Slashing damage.
Devour Intellect. One visible creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 12 Intelligence save. Failure deals 11 (2d10) Psychic damage and leaves the target Stunned until the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.
Steal Body. Target one Small or Medium Humanoid or Beast within 5 ft. that is Incapacitated and has 10 HP or fewer. The target makes a DC 12 Intelligence save. On a failure, the intellect devourer possesses the target, eats its brain, and teleports into its skull.
Inside the host, the intellect devourer has Total Cover against attacks and effects from outside. It uses the host's statistics except for its own Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, understanding of Deep Speech, telepathy, and Detect Intelligence. It acquires the host's knowledge, including spells and languages.
The intellect devourer must leave if the host body dies or Wish restores the host's brain. It can also spend 5 ft. of movement to leave voluntarily, teleporting to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the host. The vacated body dies unless its brain returns before the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 179.

name: Gelatinous Cube
description: A nearly invisible block of acid that sweeps dungeon corridors. Anything it can't dissolve may remain suspended inside.

sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone.
sections.Traits:
Ooze Cube. The transparent cube fills its space. A creature entering that space is subject to Engulf and makes the save with Disadvantage. Occupants have Total Cover. The cube holds one Large creature or up to four Medium or Small creatures.
A creature within 5 ft. can use an action to extract a creature or object with a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check. A successful pull deals 10 (3d6) Acid damage to the creature doing the pulling.
Transparent. A creature that hasn't seen the cube move or act needs a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice it, even in plain sight.
sections.Actions:
Pseudopod. Melee attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 12 (3d6 + 2) Acid damage.
Engulf. Move up to the cube's Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. It can pass through the space of a Large or smaller creature if it has room to hold it. Each creature whose space it enters for the first time during this move makes a DC 12 Dexterity save.
On a failed save, the creature takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage and is engulfed. An engulfed creature is Restrained, suffocates, and can't cast spells with a Verbal component. It moves with the cube and takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the cube's turns. It can use an action to make a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check. On a success, it escapes into the nearest unoccupied space.
On a successful save, the creature takes half the damage and moves into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the cube. The save fails instead if no such space is available.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 129.

name: Rust Monster
description: A beetle-like scavenger that locates iron and steel by scent and corrodes the metal before eating it.

sections.Traits: Iron Scent. The rust monster pinpoints ferrous metal within 30 ft.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and use Antennae twice.
Bite. Melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.
Antennae. Choose one piece of nonmagical metal armor or one nonmagical metal weapon a creature within 5 ft. wears or carries. That creature makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. On a failure, the item takes a cumulative −1 penalty to the AC it provides or to attack rolls made with it. Destroy the armor if the penalty drops its AC to 10, or the weapon if its penalty reaches −5. Mending removes the penalty from the item.
Destroy Metal. Touch an unworn, uncarried nonmagical metal object within 5 ft. to destroy a 1-ft. cube of its material.
sections.Reactions: Reflexive Antennae. When an attack roll hits the rust monster, it uses Antennae.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 263.

name: Mimic
description: A shapeshifting ambusher that passes for furniture or another ordinary object until prey reaches for it.

sections.Traits: Adhesive (object form only). Anything that touches the mimic sticks to it. A Huge or smaller creature stuck this way is Grappled (escape DC 13) and has Disadvantage on checks to escape.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. The mimic has Advantage if it is grappling the target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage, or 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage if the mimic is grappling the target. In either case, add 4 (1d8) Acid damage.
Pseudopod. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Acid damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by this attack is Grappled (escape DC 13) and has Disadvantage on checks to escape.
sections.Bonus actions: Shape-Shift. Take the appearance of a Medium or Small object, or resume the mimic's true blob form. Both forms use the same statistics. Everything the mimic wears or carries keeps its shape.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 212.

name: Owlbear
description: A beaked forest predator that can climb after prey and pursue a trail for miles.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 234.

name: Banshee
description: A spirit consumed by sorrow or bitterness, the banshee warns of disaster or brings it with a fatal wail.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, bludgeoning, fire, lightning, piercing, slashing, thunder.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Detect Life. The banshee magically senses the direction of creatures within 1 mile, except Constructs and Undead.
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as Difficult Terrain for this creature's movement. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Corrupting Touch attacks and use Horrify.
Corrupting Touch. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) necrotic damage.
Horrify. Choose a creature within 60 ft. that the banshee can see and that can see it. The target makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure it is Frightened until the start of the banshee's next turn. A successful save grants immunity to this banshee's Horrify for 24 hours.
Deathly Wail (1/day). Use only outside sunlight. Each creature within 30 ft. that hears the wail and is neither a Construct nor Undead makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, a target with 25 HP or fewer drops to 0 HP. A target with more HP takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 29.

name: Ghost
description: A restless spirit haunts a meaningful place until its unfinished business is resolved or it is put to rest.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, bludgeoning, cold, fire, lightning, piercing, slashing, thunder.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Ethereal Sight. From the Material Plane, the ghost can see 60 ft. into the Ethereal Plane.
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as Difficult Terrain for this creature's movement. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Withering Touch attacks.
Withering Touch. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 19 (3d10 + 3) necrotic damage.
Etherealness. Cast Etherealness using Charisma and no spell components. The ghost is visible from the Material Plane while it is on the Border Ethereal and from the Border Ethereal while it is on the Material Plane. It cannot affect anything on the opposite plane or be affected from there.
Horrific Visage. Each creature in a 60-ft. cone that can see the ghost and is not Undead makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure it takes 10 (2d6 + 3) psychic damage and is Frightened until the start of the ghost's next turn. A successful save grants immunity to this ghost's Horrific Visage for 24 hours.
Possession (Recharge 6). One Humanoid the ghost can see within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Charisma save. On a failure the ghost vanishes into the target and controls its body. The target remains aware and is Incapacitated. Only effects specifically targeting Undead can target the ghost. It keeps its game statistics apart from using the target's Speed and its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers.
Possession ends when the body drops to 0 HP or the ghost leaves as a bonus action. The ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the target. A successful save or the end of possession grants the target immunity to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours.
sections.Bonus actions: End Possession. The ghost can leave the host as described in Possession.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 131.

name: Vampire
classification: Small or Medium undead, lawful evil
description: An undead predator passes for mortal, feeding for generations and keeping a hidden refuge from daylight.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Misty Escape. At 0 HP outside its resting place, the vampire uses Shape-Shift to become mist without taking an action. It is destroyed if it cannot use Shape-Shift. At 0 HP the mist has 2 hours to get home and cannot return to vampire form elsewhere. At the resting place the vampire resumes its true form and is Paralyzed until it has HP again. It regains 1 HP after 1 hour there.
Spider Climb. The vampire climbs difficult surfaces and ceilings without making ability checks.
sections.Vampire weaknesses:
Forbiddance. An occupant must invite the vampire before it can enter a residence.
Running Water. The vampire takes 20 acid damage if it ends its turn in running water.
Sunlight. The vampire takes 20 radiant damage if its turn starts in sunlight. While there, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
Stake to the Heart. A piercing weapon driven into the heart while the vampire is Incapacitated in its resting place leaves it Paralyzed until the weapon comes out.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack (vampire form only). Make two Grave Strike attacks and use Bite.
Grave Strike (vampire form only). Melee attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. A Large or smaller creature is also Grappled by one of the vampire's two hands (escape DC 14).
Bite (bat or vampire form only). Choose one creature within 5 ft. that is willing, Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained. The target makes a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage. Reduce its HP maximum by the necrotic damage it took and restore that many HP to the vampire. A Humanoid this damage reduces to 0 HP rises under the vampire's control as a Vampire Spawn at the next sunset if buried first.
sections.Bonus actions:
Charm (Recharge 5–6). Cast Charm Person using Charisma (DC 17) and no spell components. The spell lasts 24 hours. A target Charmed this way is willing to receive the vampire's Bite, and that Bite's damage does not end the spell. After the spell ends, the target does not know the vampire Charmed it.
Shape-Shift. Outside sunlight and running water, take the form of a Tiny bat or a Medium cloud of mist, or return to vampire form. Worn objects transform. The bat has Speed 5 ft. and Fly Speed 30 ft. and cannot speak. Its other statistics are unchanged apart from size and Speed. The mist has Speed 5 ft. and Fly Speed 20 ft. (hover). It is weightless, cannot take actions, speak, or manipulate objects, and can occupy an enemy's space. It can pass through spaces air can pass through but cannot pass through liquid. It has Resistance to all damage except damage it takes from sunlight.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three uses, or four in the lair. Spend 1 use to take one of these options at the end of another creature's turn. The creature regains all spent uses at the start of each of its turns.
Beguile. Cast Command using Charisma (DC 17) and no spell components. The vampire cannot use Beguile again until the start of its next turn.
Deathless Strike. Move up to half Speed, then make one Grave Strike attack.
sections.Lair: In its lair the vampire has four Legendary Resistance uses per day and four legendary action uses. Award 11,500 XP for an encounter in the lair.
sections.Regional effects:
Children of the Night. From dusk to dawn, Beasts of Medium size or smaller within 1 mile of the lair are Charmed.
Looming Shadows. Any creature that finishes a Short Rest within 1 mile makes a DC 15 Wisdom save unless it is the vampire or one of its allies. A creature that fails gets no benefit from the rest.
Mists. Persistent fog Lightly Obscures the area within 1 mile. It does not affect the vampire or any creature it chooses.
These effects end immediately when the vampire dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 316–317. The stat block is on p. 317 and its regional effects are on p. 316.

name: Vampire Spawn
classification: Small or Medium undead, neutral evil
description: A recently raised vampire often hunts for its creator, closing on prey with claws before feeding.

sections.Traits: Spider Climb. The vampire climbs difficult surfaces and ceilings without making ability checks.
sections.Vampire weaknesses:
Forbiddance. An occupant must invite the vampire before it can enter a residence.
Running Water. The vampire takes 20 acid damage if it ends its turn in running water.
Sunlight. The vampire takes 20 radiant damage if its turn starts in sunlight. While there, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
Stake to the Heart. Driving a piercing weapon into the spawn's heart while it is Incapacitated destroys it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and use Bite.
Claw. Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage. A Medium or smaller creature is also Grappled by one of the spawn's two claws (escape DC 13).
Bite. Choose one creature within 5 ft. that is willing, Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained. The target makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. Reduce its HP maximum by the necrotic damage it took and restore that many HP to the spawn.
sections.Bonus actions: Deathless Agility. Take the Dash or Disengage action.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 315.

name: Death Knight
classification: Small or Medium undead, chaotic evil
description: An armored undead warlord leads legions or broods in a ruined stronghold, bound to undeath by an unatoned past.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The death knight has Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Marshal Undead. Chosen Undead in a 60-ft. Emanation around the death knight have Advantage on attack rolls and saves. It cannot choose itself or use this trait while Incapacitated.
Undead Restoration. If destroyed before it atones for its evil, the death knight returns with full HP in a new body after 1d10 days. The body appears at a place significant to the knight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Dread Blade attacks.
Dread Blade. Melee attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.
Hellfire Orb (Recharge 5–6). Choose a point the death knight can see within 120 ft. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius Sphere centered there makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. A failure deals 35 (10d6) fire damage plus 35 (10d6) necrotic damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of these spells as an action using Charisma (DC 18). No material components are needed.
At will. Command, Phantom Steed.
2/day each. Destructive Wave (necrotic), Dispel Magic.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon, the death knight gains +6 AC against that attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss.
sections.Legendary actions:
Three uses. Spend 1 use to take one of these options at the end of another creature's turn. The creature regains all spent uses at the start of each of its turns.
Dread Authority. Use Spellcasting to cast Command. The death knight cannot use Dread Authority again until the start of its next turn.
Fell Word. Choose one creature the death knight can see within 120 ft. It makes a DC 18 Constitution save. A failure deals 17 (5d6) necrotic damage and reduces the target's HP maximum by the damage taken. Regardless of the result, the death knight cannot use Fell Word again until the start of its next turn.
Lunge. Move up to half Speed and make one Dread Blade attack.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 92.

name: Wight
description: An undead warrior keeps its old grudges and draws life from victims, turning slain Humanoids into servants.

sections.Traits: Sunlight Sensitivity. The creature has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while in sunlight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Necrotic Sword or Necrotic Bow in any combination. Replace up to one attack with Life Drain.
Necrotic Sword. Melee attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) necrotic damage.
Necrotic Bow. Ranged attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) necrotic damage.
Life Drain. One creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 6 (1d8 + 2) necrotic damage and its HP maximum drops by the damage taken. A Humanoid slain by Life Drain rises as a Zombie under the wight's control 24 hours later unless restored to life or its body is destroyed. The wight can control up to twelve such Zombies at a time.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 332.

name: Wraith
classification: Small or Medium undead, neutral evil
description: This embodiment of malice haunts places where cruelty or disaster left a mark, claiming nearby dead as specters.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, bludgeoning, cold, fire, piercing, slashing.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as Difficult Terrain for this creature's movement. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to it.
Sunlight Sensitivity. The creature has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while in sunlight.
sections.Actions:
Life Drain. Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 21 (4d8 + 3) necrotic damage. A creature's HP maximum drops by the damage it took.
Create Specter. Choose a Humanoid corpse within 10 ft. that has been dead for 1 minute or less. Its spirit rises as a Specter under the wraith's control, in the corpse's space or the nearest unoccupied space. The wraith can control up to seven Specters at a time.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 336.

name: Balor
description: A towering demon fights with a whip of fire and a blade of lightning. It can teleport itself or carry another willing demon out of danger.

sections.Traits:
Death Throes. The balor explodes when it dies. Every creature within a 30-ft. Emanation from it makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 31 (9d6) force damage plus 31 (9d6) fire damage. On a success, take half damage. If the balor died outside the Abyss, it immediately gains a new body at full HP somewhere in the Abyss, regardless of the saves.
Fire Aura. At the end of each of the balor's turns, every creature within a 5-ft. Emanation from it takes 13 (3d8) fire damage.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The creature can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Flame Whip attack and one Lightning Blade attack.
Flame Whip. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 30 ft. A hit deals 18 (3d6 + 8) force damage plus 17 (5d6) fire damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, pull it up to 25 ft. straight toward the balor and knock it Prone.
Lightning Blade. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) force damage plus 22 (4d10) lightning damage. The target cannot take Reactions until the start of the balor's next turn.
sections.Bonus actions: Teleport. Teleport the balor or one willing demon within 10 ft. of it up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space the balor can see.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 26.

name: Pit Fiend
description: A powerful devil batters foes with its mace and claws, leaves a lingering venom with its bite, and overwhelms groups with bursts of hellfire.

sections.Traits:
Diabolical Restoration. Death outside the Nine Hells makes the devil vanish in sulfurous smoke. It immediately gains a new body at full HP somewhere in the Nine Hells.
Fear Aura. While the pit fiend is free of the Incapacitated condition, it projects a 20-ft. Emanation. An enemy that starts its turn in the aura makes a DC 21 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Frightened until the start of its next turn. On a success, it is immune to this pit fiend's aura for 24 hours.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The creature can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack, two Devilish Claw attacks, and one Fiery Mace attack.
Bite. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 18 (3d6 + 8) piercing damage. A creature hit must make a DC 21 Constitution save. On a failure, it is Poisoned by this bite. While Poisoned this way, it cannot regain HP and takes 21 (6d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
Devilish Claw. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 26 (4d8 + 8) necrotic damage.
Fiery Mace. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 22 (4d6 + 8) force damage plus 21 (6d6) fire damage.
Hellfire Spellcasting (recharge 4–6). Cast Fireball twice at level 5. Replace either one of those castings with Hold Monster at level 7 or Wall of Fire if desired. The spells use Charisma, have save DC 21, and require no material components.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 243.

name: Erinyes
description: An armored, winged devil fights with a withering sword and uses a magic rope to bind its enemies from a distance.

sections.Traits:
Diabolical Restoration. Death outside the Nine Hells makes the devil vanish in sulfurous smoke. It immediately gains a new body at full HP somewhere in the Nine Hells.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
Magic Rope. The erinyes can use Entangling Rope while bearing its magic rope. The rope has AC 20, 90 HP, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP, after spending at least 1 hour at least 5 ft. from the erinyes, or when the erinyes dies. The erinyes can restore the rope in full at the end of a Short or Long Rest if it is damaged or destroyed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Withering Sword attacks. The erinyes can also use Entangling Rope.
Withering Sword. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Entangling Rope (requires Magic Rope). Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It makes a DC 16 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) force damage and is Restrained until the rope is destroyed, the erinyes releases it as a Bonus Action, or the erinyes uses Entangling Rope again.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack roll hits the erinyes while it is holding a weapon, it can add 4 to its AC against that attack. This can turn the hit into a miss.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 114.

name: Glabrezu
description: A four-armed demon seizes enemies with its pincers, then beats them with its smaller arms or casts a spell.

sections.Traits:
Demonic Restoration. Death outside the Abyss makes the glabrezu dissolve into ichor. It immediately gains a new body at full HP somewhere in the Abyss.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Pincer attacks, and use either Pummel or Spellcasting.
Pincer. Melee attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit is also Grappled by one of the glabrezu's two pincers (escape DC 15).
Pummel. Choose one creature Grappled by the glabrezu. It makes a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of the following spells as an action. The spells use Intelligence, have save DC 16, and require no material components.
At will. Darkness, Detect Magic, Dispel Magic.
1/day each. Confusion, Fly, Power Word Stun.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 138.

name: Cambion
description: This winged fiend fights with its claws or hurls fire from a distance. Its spells let it change appearance, issue commands, and dominate a person.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Claw, Fire Ray, or one of each.
Claw. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
Fire Ray. Ranged attack, +7 to hit, range 120 ft. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) fire damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one of the following spells as an action. The spells use Charisma, have save DC 14, and require no material components.
2/day each. Alter Self, Command (level 3), Detect Magic.
1/day each. Dominate Person (level 8), Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 65.

name: Quasit
description: A tiny demon poisons foes with its claws, then hides by changing shape or turning invisible.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
sections.Actions:
Rend. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) slashing damage and inflicts Poisoned until the start of the quasit's next turn.
Scare (1/day). Choose one creature within 20 ft. It makes a DC 10 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Frightened. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
Shape-Shift. The quasit takes the likeness of a bat (walk 10 ft., fly 40 ft.), centipede (walk 40 ft., climb 40 ft.), or toad (walk 40 ft., swim 40 ft.), or it returns to its true form. Only its speed changes. Worn and carried equipment stays as it is.
Invisibility. Cast Invisibility on itself using Charisma, with no spell components.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 252.

name: Imp
description: A small devil relies on a venomous sting, Invisibility, and unassuming animal forms.

sections.Senses: Darkvision 120 ft. The imp can see through magical Darkness.
sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
sections.Actions:
Sting. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Shape-Shift. The imp takes the likeness of a rat (walk 20 ft.), raven (walk 20 ft., fly 60 ft.), or spider (walk 20 ft., climb 20 ft.), or it returns to its true form. Only its speed changes. Worn and carried equipment stays as it is.
Invisibility. Cast Invisibility on itself using Charisma, with no spell components.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 177.

name: Adult Black Dragon
description: This cruel swamp dragon spreads choking fog and spoils the water around its lair.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes both air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by using Spellcasting for level 3 Melf's Acid Arrow.
Rend. Melee attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Acid damage.
Acid Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. line, 5 ft. wide, makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. Failure deals 54 (12d8) Acid damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 17, spell attacks +9.
At will. Detect Magic, Fear, Melf's Acid Arrow (level 3).
1/day each. Speak with Dead, Vitriolic Sphere.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Cloud of Insects. One visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d10) Poison damage and has Disadvantage on saves to maintain Concentration through the end of its next turn. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Frightful Presence. Use Spellcasting to cast Fear. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 13,000 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Acrid Haze. Thick, foul fog leaves the area within 1 mile Lightly Obscured. Travel there takes twice as long for creatures other than the dragon and its allies.
Foul Water. Water sources within 1 mile are magically polluted. A creature drinking from one makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Poisoned for 1 hour.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 39 and 40 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult Blue Dragon
description: This desert and coastal dragon surrounds its lair with storms and unstable ground.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by using Spellcasting for Shatter.
Rend. Melee attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 16 (2d8 + 7) Slashing damage plus 5 (1d10) Lightning damage.
Lightning Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 90-ft. line, 5 ft. wide, makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. Failure deals 60 (11d10) Lightning damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 18.
At will. Detect Magic, Invisibility, Mage Hand, Shatter.
1/day each. Scrying, Sending.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Cloaked Flight. Use Spellcasting to cast Invisibility on the dragon itself. It can then fly up to half its Fly Speed. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Sonic Boom. Use Spellcasting to cast Shatter. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Tail Swipe. Make one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 18,000 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Sinkholes. When a creature other than the dragon or an ally finishes a Long Rest within 1 mile of the lair, roll 1d20. On a 1, the ground opens beneath it. A failed DC 15 Dexterity save drops it 2d4 × 10 ft. into the sinkhole.
Spiteful Storms. Thunderstorms and dust devils leave the area within 1 mile Lightly Obscured.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 49 and 50 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult Green Dragon
description: This forest dragon uses magic to spy through nearby animals and turn its chosen hunting ground toxic.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes both air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by using Spellcasting for level 3 Mind Spike.
Rend. Melee attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 15 (2d8 + 6) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.
Poison Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 18 Constitution save. Failure deals 56 (16d6) Poison damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 17.
At will. Detect Magic, Mind Spike (level 3).
1/day. Geas.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Mind Invasion. Use Spellcasting to cast Mind Spike at level 3.
Noxious Miasma. Center a 20-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 7 (2d6) Poison damage and a −2 AC penalty until the end of its next turn. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 15,000 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Beast Spies. Within 1 mile of the lair, Tiny Beasts magically understand Draconic and can speak telepathically with the dragon.
Poisonous Thicket. Plants contaminate the air within 1 mile. A creature other than the dragon or an ally that finishes a Long Rest there makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Poisoned for 1 hour.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 153 and 154 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult Red Dragon
description: This mountain or hill dragon turns nearby lands hot and fills the air with ash.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by using Spellcasting for Scorching Ray.
Rend. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 13 (1d10 + 8) Slashing damage plus 5 (2d4) Fire damage.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 59 (17d6) Fire damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 20, spell attacks +12.
At will. Command (level 2), Detect Magic, Scorching Ray.
1/day. Fireball.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Commanding Presence. Use Spellcasting to cast Command at level 2. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Fiery Rays. Use Spellcasting to cast Scorching Ray. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.

Burning Heat. Extreme heat extends 1 mile from the lair. In the area, a burning creature or object takes 1d4 extra Fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 255 and 256 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult White Dragon
speed: 40 ft., burrow 30 ft., fly 80 ft., swim 40 ft.
description: This arctic dragon climbs on ice and hunts through freezing fog.

sections.Traits:
Ice Walk. The dragon crosses or climbs ice without an ability check. Difficult Terrain made of snow or ice costs it no extra movement.
Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Cold damage.
Cold Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 19 Constitution save. Failure deals 54 (12d8) Cold damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Freezing Burst. Center a 30-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 7 (2d6) Cold damage and its Speed is 0 until the end of its next turn. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Frightful Presence. The dragon casts Fear without Material components, using Charisma with spell save DC 14. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 11,500 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Frigid Cold. Extreme cold extends 1 mile from the lair, and all water there is frigid water. Use the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide rules for those hazards.
Glacial Gloom. Cold fog leaves the region within 1 mile Lightly Obscured. Any creature other than the dragon or an ally that finishes a Long Rest in the area makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, its Speed drops by 10 ft. for 1 hour.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 329 and 330 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult Gold Dragon
description: This dragon tempers intruders with weakening magic, warns visitors through its lair fog, and can visit their dreams.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes both air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by Weakening Breath or by using Spellcasting for level 2 Guiding Bolt.
Rend. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Fire damage.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 66 (12d10) Fire damage. Success halves the damage.
Weakening Breath. Each creature in a 60-ft. cone that is not already affected makes a DC 21 Strength save. Failure gives it Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests and reduces its damage rolls by 3 (1d6). It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 21, spell attacks +13.
At will. Detect Magic, Guiding Bolt (level 2), Shapechange. Shapechange is limited to Beast or Humanoid forms. The dragon gains no Temporary Hit Points from it and needs neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain it.
1/day each. Flame Strike, Zone of Truth.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Banish. One visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 21 Charisma save. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) Force damage and is Incapacitated in a harmless demiplane until the start of the dragon's next turn. It returns in an unoccupied space of the dragon's choice within 120 ft. of the dragon. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Guiding Light. Use Spellcasting to cast Guiding Bolt at level 2.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 20,000 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Dream Messenger. From its lair, the dragon can cast Dream using Charisma and no Material components. It can target any creature within 6 miles.
Foretelling Fog. Opalescent fog leaves the area within 1 mile Lightly Obscured. The fog foreshadows danger, so creatures there cannot be surprised.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 145 and 146 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Adult Silver Dragon
description: This dragon favors mountains and cities. Near its lair, winds slow falls and it can change the weather.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. One can be replaced by Paralyzing Breath or by using Spellcasting for Ice Knife.
Rend. Melee attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Cold damage.
Cold Breath (recharge 5–6). Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 54 (12d8) Cold damage. Success halves the damage.
Paralyzing Breath. Every creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 20 Constitution save. On the first failure, it is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn and repeats the save then. On a second failure, it is Paralyzed. A Paralyzed target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells uses an action and requires no Material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability. Spell save DC 19, spell attacks +11.
At will. Detect Magic, Hold Monster, Ice Knife, Shapechange. Shapechange is limited to Beast or Humanoid forms. The dragon gains no Temporary Hit Points from it and needs neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain it.
1/day each. Ice Storm (level 5), Zone of Truth.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Chill. Use Spellcasting to cast Hold Monster. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Cold Gale. Each creature in a 60-ft. line, 10 ft. wide, makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) Cold damage and is pushed up to 30 ft. straight away from the dragon. On a success, it takes half damage only. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: In the lair, this encounter is worth 18,000 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.
sections.Regional effects:
Gentle Gusts. A creature falling within 1 mile of the lair descends at 60 ft. per round and takes no falling damage.
Sun and Storms. From its lair, the dragon can cast Control Weather using Charisma and no Material components.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), pp. 279 and 280 for the stat block and regional effects.

name: Air Elemental
description: A wind spirit gathers clouds and gusts into the rough shape of a body. It batters foes and whirls them away.

sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Traits: Air Form. The elemental can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch at its usual movement cost. It can enter another creature's space and stop there.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Thunderous Slam attacks.
Thunderous Slam. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) thunder damage.
Whirlwind (recharge 4–6). Choose one Medium or smaller creature in the elemental's space. It makes a DC 13 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 24 (4d10 + 2) thunder damage, is pushed up to 20 ft. straight away from the elemental, and falls Prone. On a success, it takes half damage.
sections.Habitats: Deserts, mountains, and the Elemental Plane of Air.
sections.Appearance (1d6): 1. Cumulus or wisps of cirrus. 2. Swirls of bright gas. 3. An acrid cloud. 4. Clouds that form animals or simple shapes. 5. A mist that barely hides a sinister face. 6. Churning thunderclouds.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 13.

name: Earth Elemental
description: A spirit of the Plane of Earth forms a heavy body from rock and minerals. It can move through natural stone and bring down buildings with its fists.

sections.Traits:
Earth Glide. Burrow through unworked, nonmagical earth or stone without disturbing it.
Siege Monster. The elemental deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Slam and Rock Launch.
Slam. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Rock Launch. Ranged attack, +8 to hit, range 60 ft. On a hit, deal 8 (1d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by the rock falls Prone.
sections.Habitats: Mountains, the Elemental Plane of Earth, and the Underdark.
sections.Appearance (1d8): 1. Colorful crystals. 2. Lumps of cooled magma. 3. Moss, grass, or roots. 4. Peat or rotting matter. 5. Shells embedded in sand. 6. Broken masonry. 7. Stripes of contrasting rock. 8. Veins of ore. Composition has no effect on the stat block and gives the body no added monetary value.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 108.

name: Fire Elemental
description: A spirit gives shape to flame, smoke, and cinders. Even a brief brush with it can ignite a creature or object.

sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Fire Aura. At the end of the elemental's turn, each creature in its 10-ft. Emanation takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. Creatures and flammable objects in the area start burning.
Fire Form. It can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch at its usual movement cost. It can enter a creature's space and stop there. The first time on a turn that it enters a creature's space, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.
Illumination. It sheds Bright Light out to 30 ft. and Dim Light for another 30 ft.
Water Susceptibility. It takes 3 (1d6) cold damage per 5 ft. of movement in water and per gallon of water splashed on it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Burn attacks.
Burn. Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) fire damage. A creature or flammable object hit by the attack also starts burning.
sections.Burning hazard: A burning creature or object takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of its turns. A creature can spend an action to drop Prone and roll, putting out the fire on itself. Dousing, submerging, or smothering the fire also puts it out. See Burning in the 2024 rules glossary.
sections.Habitats: Deserts and the Elemental Plane of Fire.
sections.Appearance (1d8): 1. Colored gas. 2. A pillar of divine or infernal fire. 3. Flames that suggest a creature or skeleton. 4. Blue, white, or other unusually colored flame. 5. A still or anguished humanoid outline. 6. Smoke that traces shapes or sigils. 7. Soot with a distinctive scent. 8. A whirl of cinders and debris.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 118. Burning follows Player's Handbook (2024), p. 362.

name: Water Elemental
description: A spirit shapes water into a moving surge. It can flood over foes, pinning them inside its body.

sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Freeze. Cold damage reduces the elemental's Speed by 20 ft. until the end of its next turn.
Water Form. It can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch at its usual movement cost. It can enter an enemy's space and stop there.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit by the attack falls Prone.
Whelm (recharge 4–6). Each creature in the elemental's space makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature that fails is also Grappled (escape DC 14). While Grappled by Whelm, the creature is Restrained, suffocates unless it can breathe water, and takes 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the elemental's turns. Whelm can hold one Large creature or up to two Medium or smaller creatures at once. A creature within 5 ft. of the elemental can spend an action and make a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check to pull a creature out. On a successful save against Whelm, the target takes half damage.
sections.Suffocation hazard: A target suffocating in Whelm gains one level of Exhaustion at the end of each of its own turns. Once it can breathe again, remove the Exhaustion it gained from suffocation. See Suffocation in the 2024 rules glossary.
sections.Habitats: Coasts, swamps, underwater, and the Elemental Plane of Water.
sections.Appearance (1d4): 1. Frigid or near boiling. 2. Bubbling. 3. Clear, muddy, or polluted. 4. Carrying seaweed or small aquatic creatures.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 322. Suffocation follows the 2024 rules glossary.

name: Invisible Stalker
description: A bodiless air spirit tracks its quarry unseen. Spellcasters summon stalkers to kill or steal, and a faint stir in the air may be the only sign of one.

sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Air Form. The stalker can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch at its usual movement cost. It can enter an enemy's space and stop there.
Invisibility. The stalker has the Invisible condition.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Wind Swipe attacks. The stalker can replace one of those attacks with Vortex.
Wind Swipe. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 11 (2d6 + 4) force damage.
Vortex. Choose one Large or smaller creature in the stalker's space. It makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 7 (1d8 + 3) thunder damage and is Grappled (escape DC 13). While Grappled by Vortex, it cannot cast spells that have a Verbal component. At the start of each of the stalker's turns, the target takes 7 (2d6) thunder damage until the grapple ends.
sections.Uncontrolled stalkers (1d6): 1. The breath of a god or monster. 2. A guardian of a portal or magical site. 3. A remnant of violent thoughts from a battle. 4. Magic that escaped control. 5. A servant of an elemental ruler such as Yan-C-Bin. 6. A stalker trying to create the conditions needed to finish an old assignment.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 180.

name: Shambling Mound
description: A mass of vegetation moves through marsh and undergrowth. It catches creatures with its vines and draws them inside to feed its growth.

sections.Traits: Lightning Absorption. When subjected to lightning damage, the mound regains hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Charged Tendril attacks. The mound can replace one of those attacks with Engulf.
Charged Tendril. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. On a hit, deal 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) lightning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the mound pulls it 5 ft. straight toward itself.
Engulf. Choose one Medium or smaller creature within 5 ft. The target makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure, the mound pulls it into its space and the target is Grappled (escape DC 14). While Grappled by Engulf, the target is Blinded and Restrained and takes 10 (3d6) lightning damage at the start of each of its own turns. It moves with the mound at no extra movement cost to the mound. Engulf can hold only one creature at a time.
sections.Origins and appearance (1d6): 1. Covered in alien flowers or Feywild blooms. 2. Carrying a rune-covered standing stone in its torso. 3. Hosting vermin or fungi. 4. A knot of vines around skeletons. 5. Mutated and leaking glowing waste. 6. The remains of an ancient tree or Treant.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 276.

name: Treant
description: A living tree of great age guards its forest and calls nearby trees to help defend it.

sections.Traits: Siege Monster. The treant deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Hail of Bark. Ranged attack, +10 to hit, range 180 ft. On a hit, deal 28 (4d10 + 6) piercing damage.
Animate Trees (1/day). Magically animate up to two trees the treant can see within 60 ft. An animated tree uses this Treant stat block. Set its Intelligence and Charisma to 1, remove its ability to speak, and remove Animate Trees from its actions.
