Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. A hit restrains the creature. It can use an action to break the webbing with a successful DC 12 Strength check. Destroying the webbing also frees the creature. The webbing has AC 10 and 5 HP, vulnerability to fire damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.At the table: After Web is used, roll a d6 at the start of the spider’s turns. Web returns on a 5 or 6, or after the spider finishes a short or long rest.

name: Giant Toad
otherStatistics: Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 10. No listed skills or languages.
appearance: A squat gray-brown toad with warty skin, two rounded swellings behind the eyes, and heavy folded hindlegs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules, Version 1.0 (November 2018), p. 136.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The toad breathes both air and water.
Standing Leap. Its long jump can reach 20 ft. and its high jump 10 ft. It needs no running start for either.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 5 (1d10) poison damage and grapple the target (escape DC 13). The target is restrained for the duration of the grapple, and the toad cannot use Bite against another target while it maintains that grapple.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack against one Medium or smaller target the toad is grappling. On a hit, the toad swallows the target and the grapple ends. A swallowed target is blinded and restrained, has total cover from attacks and other effects outside the toad, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the toad’s turns. The toad can have only one target swallowed at a time. If the toad dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can spend 5 ft. of movement to climb out of the corpse, emerging prone.

name: Warhorse (Chain Mail Barding)
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 11. No listed skills, special senses or languages.
appearance: A sturdy light-bay warhorse with a black mane and tail, dark lower legs, and fitted chain mail barding in this variant.

sections.Printed source:
Monster Manual, first printing (September 2014), Appendix A, printed p. 340, Warhorse and Variant: Warhorse Armor. https://online.anyflip.com/pqhqn/sezy/index.html#p=341

sections.Barding: Chain Mail barding gives AC 16 under the printed Warhorse Armor table. Use the fixed AC for this heavy barding. The armor gives disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. sections.Traits: Trampling Charge. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Hooves on the same turn. The creature makes a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, it falls prone. sections.At the table: A rider controlling the warhorse can have it Dash, Disengage, or Dodge. An independent mount acts on its own initiative and can use its listed attacks.

classification: Medium swarm of Tiny beasts, unaligned
appearance: A loose cloud of small brown bats with pointed ears and spread, leathery wings.

sections.Traits:
Echolocation. The swarm loses the use of blindsight while deafened.
Keen Hearing. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on hearing.
Swarm. This swarm and another creature can occupy the same space. It can pass through openings that fit one Tiny bat. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.
sections.Actions: Bites. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. On a hit, deal 5 (2d4) piercing damage above half maximum HP or 2 (1d4) piercing damage at half maximum HP or less.
sections.At the table: With the printed 22 HP maximum, use the lower piercing damage at 11 HP or less.

name: Crocodile
publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement

sections.Traits: Hold Breath. The crocodile can hold its breath for 15 minutes.

sections.At the table: Bite starts the grapple on a hit. The grappled creature may spend its action to try a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to escape.

publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement, August 8, 2014, version 1, printed and p. 8.
sections.Traits: Charge. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit it with Ram that turn. The hit deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage. If the target is a creature, it must pass a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Actions:
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit against one prone creature within 5 ft. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.At the table: The printed Charge rider gives 2d6 additional damage without stating its type. The target’s save determines prone. Hooves is its own action against an already prone creature.

name: Giant Centipede
publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement
otherStatistics: AC from natural armor. Blindsight 30 ft. Passive Perception 8. No listed languages.
appearance: A reddish-brown segmented arthropod with long antennae, curved venom claws, and paired ochre legs along its body.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement, August 8, 2014, version 1, printed and p. 9.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit against one creature within 5 ft. On a hit, deal 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. The creature makes a DC 11 Constitution save and takes 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failure. If this poison damage drops it to 0 HP, it is stable but poisoned for 1 hour, even after it regains HP. It is paralyzed while poisoned by this effect.
sections.At the table: A successful save avoids the poison damage. The special stable, poisoned and paralyzed effects require the poison damage itself to reduce the target to 0 HP.

name: Giant Frog
publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement
otherStatistics: Perception +2, Stealth +3. Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 12. No languages.
appearance: A broad-headed, mottled frog with thick folded hind legs and webbed toes.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen Online Supplement, August 8, 2014 release, version 1, Monsters p. 10.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The frog can breathe air and water.
Standing Leap. The frog can long jump up to 20 ft. or high jump up to 10 ft. from standing or with a running start.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. On a hit, deal 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage and grapple the target (escape DC 11). The target is restrained until the grapple ends. During that grapple, the frog cannot Bite another target.
Swallow. Make one Bite attack against a Small or smaller target that the frog is grappling. A hit swallows the target and ends the grapple. Inside, the target is blinded and restrained and has total cover against attacks and effects from outside the frog. It takes 5 (2d4) acid damage at the start of each of the frog’s turns. The frog can hold one swallowed target at a time. If the frog dies, the swallowed creature is no longer restrained by the frog and may spend 5 ft. of movement to exit the corpse prone.
sections.At the table: Bite imposes the grapple on a hit. DC 11 applies to escaping it. Use the frog’s turn to time the swallowed target’s acid damage.

name: Giant Spider
publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Stealth +7. Blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. No languages.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen Online Supplement, August 8, 2014 release, version 1, Monsters p. 10.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. Climb difficult surfaces, including ceiling undersides, without an ability check.
Web Sense. While touching a web, the spider knows the exact location of other creatures touching that web.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict the spider’s movement.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage and require a DC 11 Constitution save. The creature takes 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If this poison damage reduces the creature to 0 HP, it becomes stable and poisoned for 1 hour. It is paralyzed while poisoned this way. Regaining hit points during that hour does not end the poison.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. A hit restrains the target in webbing. The target can use an action to burst the web with a successful DC 12 Strength check. The web can also be attacked and destroyed. It has AC 10, 5 HP, vulnerability to fire and immunity to bludgeoning, poison and psychic damage.

name: Stirge
publication: Hoard of the Dragon Queen - Online Supplement
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 9. No listed skills or languages.
appearance: A tiny batlike blood feeder with dusty brown fur, leathery wings, hooked feet and a long needle-shaped proboscis.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen Online Supplement, August 8, 2014 release, version 1, Monsters p. 17.
sections.Actions: Blood Drain. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one creature. On a hit, deal 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage and attach to the target. The attached stirge stops attacking. At the start of each of its turns, the target loses 5 (1d4 + 3) hit points from blood loss. The stirge can detach by spending 5 ft. of its movement. It does so after draining 10 hit points of blood from the target or when the target dies. Any creature, including the target, can detach the stirge as an action.
sections.At the table: Resolve piercing damage on the initial attack, then track the later blood loss at the start of the stirge’s turns.

name: Bison
otherStatistics: Initiative +0. AC is 13 (−1 size, +4 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 13. Space/reach 10 ft./5 ft. Base attack +3. Grapple +13. Fortitude +7, Reflex +4, Will +1.
appearance: A broad, shaggy bison with a high shoulder hump, heavy forequarters, and short upward-curving horns.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Bison. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/bison.htm
sections.Full attack: One Gore +8 melee, 1d8 + 9 damage.
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.
sections.Skills and feats:
Skills. Listen +7, Spot +5.
Feats. Alertness, Endurance. Endurance grants +4 on the checks and saves listed for the feat, including Constitution checks to keep running, hold breath or withstand a forced march.
sections.Encounter ecology: Environment. Temperate plains. Organization. Solitary or herd (6–30). Bison usually flee. They may become aggressive while protecting their young or during mating season. Treasure none. Advancement. 6–7 HD (Large). Level adjustment none listed.
sections.Special attacks: Stampede (Ex). A frightened herd flees together in a random direction away from the perceived danger. It runs over anything of Large size or smaller in its path and deals 1d12 damage for each five bison in the herd. Reflex DC 18 halves the damage. The save DC is Strength-based.

name: Camel
otherStatistics: Initiative +3. AC is 13 (−1 size, +3 Dex, +1 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 10. Space/reach 10 ft./5 ft. Base attack +2. Grapple +10. Fortitude +5, Reflex +6, Will +1.
appearance: A sandy dromedary with one hump, long legs, an arched neck and broad two-toed feet.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Camel. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/camel.htm
sections.Attack: Bite +0 melee, 1d4 + 2 damage. The bite is secondary and adds half the Strength bonus.
sections.Full attack: One secondary Bite +0 melee, 1d4 + 2 damage.
sections.Special qualities:

sections.Skills and feats:
Skills. Listen +5, Spot +5.
Feats. Alertness, Endurance. Endurance grants +4 on the checks and saves listed for the feat, including Constitution checks to keep running, hold breath or withstand a forced march.
sections.Encounter ecology: Environment. Warm deserts. Organization. Domesticated or herd (6–30). The dromedary stands about 7 ft. at the shoulder, with its hump about 1 ft. higher. Camels can travel long distances without food or water. Treasure none. Advancement. None listed. Level adjustment none listed.
sections.Carrying capacity: Light load up to 300 lb. Medium load 301–600 lb. Heavy load 601–900 lb. Drag limit 4,500 lb.
sections.Bactrian camel: The two-humped variety is stockier and suited to cooler, rocky terrain. Its speed is 40 ft. and Constitution is 16.

name: Dire Rat
otherStatistics: Initiative +3. AC is 15 (+1 size, +3 Dex, +1 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Space/reach 5 ft./5 ft. Base attack +0. Grapple -4. Fortitude +3, Reflex +5, Will +3.
appearance: A low, bristly brown rat with a long curved bare tail, a pointed snout and prominent incisors.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersDi-Do.rtf, Dire Animal, Dire Rat. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/direRat.htm
sections.Attack: Bite +4 melee, 1d4 damage plus exposure to filth fever.
sections.Full attack: One Bite +4 melee, 1d4 damage plus exposure to filth fever.
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.
sections.Skills and feats:
Skills. Climb +11, Hide +8, Listen +4, Move Silently +4, Spot +4, Swim +11. Apply the printed +8 racial bonuses to Climb and Swim. Both checks use Dexterity. The rat can take 10 on Climb even while rushed or threatened.
Feats. Alertness, Weapon Finesse (bonus feat).
sections.Encounter ecology: Environment. Any. Organization. Solitary or pack (11–20). Dire rats scavenge, defend their nests and territory, and attack boldly in packs. Treasure none. Advancement. 2–3 HD (Small), 4–6 HD (Medium). Level adjustment none listed.
sections.Special attacks: Disease (Ex), filth fever. A bitten creature makes an immediate DC 11 Fortitude save. On failure, incubation lasts 1d3 days, then the creature takes 1d3 Dexterity and 1d3 Constitution damage. Each day afterward, a failed DC 11 Fortitude save repeats the damage. Two consecutive successful daily saves end the disease. The DC is Constitution-based.

name: Giant Crocodile
otherStatistics: Initiative +1. AC is 16 (−2 size, +1 Dex, +7 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 15. Space/reach 15 ft./10 ft. Base attack +5. Grapple +21. Fortitude +9, Reflex +6, Will +3.
appearance: A low, broad-snouted crocodile with armored olive-brown scales, short splayed legs and a long tapering tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Crocodile, Giant, and Crocodile combat. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/crocodile.htm#giantCrocodile
sections.Attack: Bite +11 melee for 2d8 + 12 damage, or Tail Slap +11 melee for 1d12 + 12 damage.
sections.Full attack: One Bite +11 melee for 2d8 + 12 damage, or one Tail Slap +11 melee for 1d12 + 12 damage.
sections.Special qualities:
Hold Breath (Ex). It can hold its breath for four times its Constitution score, or 76 rounds, before it risks drowning.
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
sections.Skills and feats:
Skills. Hide +1, Listen +5, Spot +5, Swim +16. In water, add a +4 racial bonus to Hide. At the surface with only eyes and nostrils exposed, it also gets +10 cover to Hide. The +8 racial Swim bonus applies to special actions and hazards. It can take 10 on Swim while distracted or endangered, and can run when swimming in a straight line.
Feats. Alertness, Endurance, Skill Focus (Hide). Endurance adds +4 to Constitution checks to hold breath after the listed interval.
sections.Encounter ecology: Environment. Warm marshes, Salt water. Organization. Solitary or colony (6–11). Giant crocodiles use the smaller crocodile’s ambush behavior, waiting low in the water and trying to drag a grabbed victim deeper. Treasure none. Advancement. 8–14 HD (Huge). Level adjustment none listed.
sections.Special attacks: Improved Grab (Ex). After it hits a Large or smaller foe with Bite, the crocodile can immediately attempt a grapple as a free action without a touch attack or an attack of opportunity. On a win, it draws the target into its space and may drag it if the victim is within its drag limit. It can grapple normally or hold with its jaws at −20 on grapple checks to avoid becoming grappled itself. Winning the initial grab adds no damage. Later successful grapple checks with the hold deal Bite damage. The crocodile uses opposed grapple checks to pin or move a struggling target.
sections.At the table: A target escapes with an opposed grapple check in place of an attack or a standard-action Escape Artist check against the crocodile’s grapple check. Escaping a pin leaves the target in the grapple. After the crocodile’s breath-holding interval, use escalating Constitution checks beginning at DC 10. Failure starts drowning, with 0 HP and unconsciousness on the first round, −1 HP on the next, and death on the third.

name: Monkey
otherStatistics: Initiative +2. AC is 14 (+2 size, +2 Dex), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Space/reach 2-1/2 ft./0 ft. Base attack +0. Grapple -12. Fortitude +2, Reflex +4, Will +1.

sections.At the table: The 3.5 combat minimum gives the monkey 1 damage on a hit after penalties. With 0-ft. reach, it enters the target’s space to bite and normally provokes an attack of opportunity for doing so.

name: Deinonychus
otherStatistics: Initiative +2. AC 16 (−1 size, +2 Dex, +5 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 14. Base attack +3, grapple +11. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +8, Ref +6, Will +2.
appearance: A lean green pack raptor with a pale green underside, dark mottling, grasping forelimbs, raised hind talons, and a long, stiff tail. It weighs about 600 lb.

sections.Printed source: Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersDi-Do.rtf, DINOSAUR, DEINONYCHUS and its following combat text. https://olimot.github.io/srd-v3.5/monsters/monsters-di-do.html#deinonychus
sections.Full attack: Talons +6 melee (2d6 + 4), two foreclaws +1 melee (1d3 + 2 each), and bite +1 melee (2d4 + 2). The hind talons count as one attack.
sections.Special attacks: Pounce (Ex). It can make a full attack when it charges.
sections.Special qualities: Low-light vision doubles normal human sight distance in dim light and retains color and detail. Scent (Ex). Detects opponents at 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double these ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction. Within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.
sections.Skills and feats: Hide +8, Jump +26, Listen +10, Spot +10, Survival +10. Run, Track. Racial +8 on each listed skill. With Track, a fresh scent trail normally starts at DC 10, adjusted for odor strength, number of creatures and trail age. Each cold hour adds 2. Poor visibility and the surface do not hinder scent tracking.
sections.Encounter ecology: It stalks from cover and uses its speed to pounce. Packs hunt together. Encounter one, a pair, or a pack of 3–6. Advancement 5–8 HD (Large). No treasure or listed level adjustment.
sections.Print distinction: This SRD archive uses Large size, 10-ft. space, and 2d6 + 4 talons. Wizards’ February 2006 Monster Manual errata uses Medium size, 5-ft. space, and 1d8 + 4 talons in its replacement table.

name: Cheetah

Cutting out requires a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 damage to the digestive tract (AC 13). The wound closes after that creature leaves. name: Bat Swarm
otherStatistics: Fortitude +3, Reflex +7, Will +3.
appearance: A flight of small brown bats with pointed wings, spread in a loose cluster.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersS.rtf, BAT SWARM. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/swarm.htm#batSwarm
sections.Combat statistics: Initiative +2. AC 16 (+4 size, +2 Dexterity), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Base attack +2, grapple none. Space 10 ft., reach 0 ft.
sections.Attack: Swarm. Automatically deal 1d6 damage to each creature whose space the swarm occupies at the end of its move. There is no attack roll or miss chance from cover or concealment.
sections.Full attack: Swarm. Automatically deal 1d6 damage to each creature whose space the swarm occupies at the end of its move. There is no attack roll or miss chance from cover or concealment.
sections.Special attacks:
Distraction (Ex). A living creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space must make a DC 11 Fortitude save or be nauseated for 1 round. The general subtype limits this to creatures vulnerable to the swarm’s damage. A nauseated creature can take only one move action per turn. Casting or concentrating on spells in the swarm requires a Concentration check at DC 20 + spell level. Skills demanding concentration require a DC 20 Concentration check.
Wounding (Ex). A living creature damaged by the swarm then loses 1 HP per round from bleeding. Additional wounds do not increase the rate. A DC 10 Heal check, a cure spell, or other healing magic stops it.
sections.Special qualities:
Blindsense (Ex). Locate creatures within 20 ft. Total concealment still applies unless the swarm can actually see them. Swarm damage ignores concealment.
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light.
Swarm traits. One pool of HP and one set of saves. Occupy a shared, shapeable 10-ft. space and fit through gaps large enough for one bat. Entering or moving through a hostile space provokes as normal. The swarm never threatens or makes opportunity attacks. It cannot grapple and is unaffected by grappling, trips, bull rushes, critical hits, or flanking. Effects aimed at a fixed number of creatures do not affect it, subject to the hive-mind exception for mind-affecting effects. Area effects deal 50% more damage. At 0 HP it disperses. It does not become staggered or dying. If rendered unconscious by nonlethal damage, it disperses until HP exceed that damage. Resolve strong wind against Diminutive size.
Weapon damage. Use weapon damage immunity under the shared subtype rule, supported by the 2006 Monster Manual errata. The SRD entry still has the earlier half-damage line.
Shared swarm vulnerabilities. A lit torch used as an improvised weapon deals 1d3 fire damage on a hit. A thrown lit lantern deals 1d4 fire damage to creatures in adjacent squares where it breaks. Energy damage from a weapon can still apply if the weapon’s ordinary damage does not.
sections.Skills and feats:
Listen +11, Spot +11. Each includes a +4 racial bonus that is lost if blindsense is negated.
Feats: Alertness, Lightning Reflexes.
sections.Encounter ecology: Temperate deserts. Solitary, flight of 2–4 swarms, or colony of 11–20 swarms. No treasure or advancement. Level adjustment —. Nocturnal and never found aboveground in daylight. It tries to surround warm-blooded prey.
sections.Printing conflicts:
Armor Class. The table prints touch 14 and flat-footed 12. Its listed +4 size and +2 Dexterity would give touch 16 and flat-footed 14 using the standard AC rules.
Weapon damage. The Bat Swarm table lists half damage from slashing and piercing. The shared Diminutive Swarm subtype grants immunity to all weapon damage, confirmed for the Bat Swarm in the 17 February 2006 Monster Manual v3.5 errata. Use immunity at the table.

name: Rat Swarm
otherStatistics: Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 12. AC modifiers +2 size and +2 Dex. Base attack +3, no grapple modifier. Space 10 ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +2.
appearance: A dense mound of many small brown rats, with overlapping backs, rounded ears and intertwined pink tails.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersS.rtf, RAT SWARM. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/swarm.htm#ratSwarm
sections.Attack: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. At the end of its movement, deal damage automatically to each creature whose space it shares. There is no attack roll or miss chance for concealment or cover. The attack is nonmagical.
sections.Full attack: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. The automatic Swarm Attack uses the same rules in both entries.
sections.Special attacks:
Disease (Ex). Filth fever is delivered by the swarm attack. Make an immediate DC 12 Fortitude save to prevent infection. On a failure, after 1d3 days take 1d3 Dex and 1d3 Con damage. Save at DC 12 daily afterward or repeat the ability damage. Two successes in a row clear the disease.
Distraction (Ex). A living creature that begins its turn in the swarm’s square makes a DC 12 Fortitude save or is nauseated for 1 round. A nauseated creature can take only one move action per turn and cannot attack, cast spells or concentrate. The shared subtype wording specifies living creatures vulnerable to the swarm’s damage. Both printed triggers are recorded here.
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light, with color and detail.
Scent. Detect by smell out to 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind or 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action gives the direction. Pinpoint the source within 5 ft.
Tiny swarm. Halve damage from slashing and piercing weapons. It cannot be critically hit or flanked. The swarm cannot grapple or be grappled, tripped, or bull rushed. It breaks up at 0 HP or below and does not become staggered or dying from damage. Losing HP above 0 does not reduce its attack or defenses.
sections.Swarm movement: One nonflying Tiny swarm represents about 300 rats and uses one set of stats and saves. It can cover any four contiguous squares and fit through gaps a constituent rat can use. It shares spaces with creatures of any size and can pass through them. Moving into or through an opponent’s space can provoke an attack of opportunity. The swarm does not threaten creatures or make attacks of opportunity.
sections.Swarm spell and effect rules: Immune to effects that target a fixed number of creatures. The shared mind-affecting exception requires intelligence and a hive mind, and this block lists no hive mind. Area effects deal 50% extra damage. Casting a spell or maintaining concentration in the swarm’s area requires a Concentration check at DC 20 + spell level. Skills requiring patience or focus require a DC 20 Concentration check. An improvised lit torch deals 1d3 fire on a hit, and a broken thrown lit lantern deals 1d4 fire in adjacent squares. A weapon’s added energy damage applies in full. Sufficient damage reduction and incorporeality can prevent the swarm attack’s ordinary damage.
sections.Nonlethal dispersal: If nonlethal damage renders the swarm unconscious it disperses until its HP exceed its nonlethal damage.
sections.Skills and feats: Balance +10, Climb +10, Hide +14, Listen +6, Spot +7, Swim +10. Racial bonuses are +4 on Hide and Move Silently, +8 on Balance, Climb and Swim. The swarm uses Dex for Climb and Swim. It can take 10 on Climb and Swim even under pressure and can run while swimming straight. Feats are Alertness and Weapon Finesse.
sections.Encounter ecology: Any environment. Solitary, pack of 2–4 swarms, or infestation of 7–12 swarms. It surrounds warm-blooded prey. No advancement, level adjustment, or treasure.
sections.Printed discrepancies: The RTF gives 13 HP for 4d8, whose usual mean is 18. Use the listed HP 13. The creature and subtype use different phrasing for the Distraction trigger, as shown above.
