sections.Traits:
Innate Spellcasting (Psionics). Intelligence, save DC 13, with no components. The swarm casts only while above half HP. Command, Comprehend Languages, and Detect Thoughts are at will. Confusion and Dominate Monster are each once per day, with expended uses recovered after a long rest.
Swarm. The swarm and other creatures can occupy the same space. It fits through any opening a Tiny rat could use. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.
Telepathic Shroud. The swarm is immune to effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts and to all divination spells.
sections.Actions: Bites. Melee weapon attack +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. A hit deals 14 (4d6) piercing damage. At half HP or lower it deals 7 (2d6) piercing instead.
sections.Damage and condition defenses: Resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. Immune to charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned.
sections.Bonus actions: Illumination. Shed dim light within 5 ft. of the swarm, increase it to bright light in a 5- to 20-ft. radius with the same distance of dim light beyond that, or extinguish it.
sections.2014 spell procedures:
Command, at will. Action, 60 ft., one visible creature. On a failed DC 13 Wisdom save it follows a one-word order on its next turn. It must understand the language. Undead and directly harmful commands are ineligible. The spell ends if the target cannot comply. The DM resolves orders outside the listed examples. Approach ends the turn when it reaches within 5 ft. of the swarm by the shortest route. Drop ends the turn after dropping held items. Flee spends the turn moving away as quickly as it can. Grovel drops it prone and ends the turn. Halt prevents movement and actions, with minimum flight allowed if needed to stay aloft.
Comprehend Languages, at will. Action, self, 1 hour. Understand literal spoken language the swarm hears and writing it sees while touching the written surface. Read one page per minute. It cannot decode ciphers or signs outside a written language.
Detect Thoughts, at will. Action, self, concentration up to 1 minute. Read the surface thoughts of a visible creature within 30 ft. The creature must have Intelligence 4 or higher and speak a language. On a later action, switch targets or probe deeper. A probe alerts the target, which makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. Success ends the spell. Failure reveals reasoning, emotional state, and a major concern. A probed creature can use an action to end the spell by winning an Intelligence contest against the swarm while it remains the focus. On casting or as an action the swarm can also search for eligible unseen minds within 30 ft., then read them while in range. Two feet of rock, 2 inches of non-lead metal, or a thin sheet of lead blocks that search.
Confusion, 1/day. Action, 90 ft., concentration up to 1 minute. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere around a point in range makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. A failure prevents reactions and requires a d10 at the start of each turn. On 1, roll a d8 for direction and spend all movement going that way without acting. On 2–6, the creature stays still and does nothing. On 7–8, it spends its action on one melee attack against a random creature in reach. If there is none, it does nothing. On 9–10, it moves and acts as usual. A DC 13 Wisdom save at the end of its turn ends the effect on that creature.
Dominate Monster, 1/day. Action, 60 ft., a visible creature, concentration up to 1 hour. The target makes a DC 13 Wisdom save, with advantage if the swarm or its allies are fighting it. Failure charms it. While conscious and on the same plane, the swarm can issue simple commands by telepathy without an action. If orders run out it protects itself. The swarm can spend an action for precise control through the end of its next turn and can spend its own reaction to direct the target’s reaction. Each time the target takes damage, another DC 13 Wisdom save can end the spell.
sections.HP threshold: With its printed maximum of 36 HP, the swarm can cast at 19 HP or more. At 18 HP or less, use the smaller Bites damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: The rats combine their memories and minds when they swarm and communicate as one. A rat separated from the swarm begins with Intelligence 15, loses 1 Intelligence per day to a minimum of 4, and returns to 15 when it rejoins any such swarm. Illithid colonies can receive a swarm’s reports within the elder brain’s telepathic range.
sections.Source notes:
The swarm’s Telepathic Shroud covers all divination spells. The same block lists Detect Thoughts and Comprehend Languages, both self-range divinations, with no explicit self-cast exception. Both printed rules are retained.
The 2014 Command language and harmful-order restrictions still apply. Volo grants component-free casting and separately lists telepathy 30 ft.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack. The lizard can replace either one with Swallow.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage and grapples the target (escape DC 15). The target remains restrained and the lizard cannot bite a different target until that grapple ends.

Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target the lizard is not grappling. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.

Swallow. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature the lizard is grappling. On a hit the target takes 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage, is swallowed, and is released from the grapple. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the lizard, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each lizard turn. The lizard can hold one swallowed target at a time. If the lizard dies, the swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.
sections.Encounter notes: In the Forge of Fury the troglodytes chain a white-scaled specimen near a stream. It lashes with its tail before trying to seize and swallow prey.

sections.Traits: Camouflage. Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in any terrain. The variant removes Hold Breath. Water Breathing is inherited from Giant Octopus and permits breathing only underwater. See the table ruling.
sections.Actions:
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 15-ft. reach, one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 16) and restrained for the duration. The rocktopus cannot use Tentacles on a different target until the grapple ends.
Ink Cloud. Underwater only. Ink heavily obscures the 20-ft. radius around the rocktopus for 1 minute. A significant current can disperse it sooner. After releasing the ink, it can Dash as a bonus action. Recharge after a short or long rest.
sections.Encounter ecology: A land-adapted octopus can change color to blend into rock, lie in cracks, and ambush smaller creatures.
sections.Source notes: The passage calls it a Giant Octopus variant and supplies walk 20 ft. and climb 10 ft. It removes Hold Breath and replaces Underwater Camouflage with unconditional Camouflage. The passage gives no explicit replacement for swim 60 ft., Water Breathing, or Ink Cloud. Tentacles retains the base attack. The inherited Water Breathing trait conflicts with the published land ecology. Allowing it to breathe air is a table ruling.
sections.At the table: For the published land encounter, allow air breathing as a DM ruling. Keep Ink Cloud underwater-only. A Tentacles hit grapples the target immediately. It can spend an action to attempt a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) escape check.

otherStatistics: Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 10. Speaks Common.
appearance: A brown rat with rounded ears, whiskers, and a long hairless tail.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 102. Base statistics use Rat in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 335. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=103
sections.Traits: Keen Smell. The rat has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 1 piercing damage.
sections.Adventure context: Jeryth Phaulkon has one of her awakened rats guide Emerald Enclave characters to the secret staircase in the Castle Ward sewers that leads to Xanathar’s lair.

name: Diatryma
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. The summoned bird understands the summoner’s languages. The base block lists no languages.
appearance: A colorful flightless bird with a broad heavy beak, blue-gray mantle, russet plumage, and thick legs.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 191. Base statistics use Axe Beak in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 317. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=192
sections.Actions: Beak. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Feather of Diatryma Summoning: The rare feather requires attunement. Use an action to speak the command word and toss the feather into a Large unoccupied space on the ground within 5 ft. The bird appears for up to 6 hours. It reverts sooner at 0 HP or if the user touches it and spends an action to repeat the command word. The feather can summon again after 7 days have elapsed from the reversion. The summoned bird is friendly to the user and their companions and can be ridden. It understands the user’s languages and follows spoken commands. In the absence of orders, it defends itself and takes no other actions.

name: Falcon
otherStatistics: Perception +4. Passive Perception 14. Languages none.
appearance: A compact falcon with pointed folded wings, a barred cream breast, and a dark leather falconry hood.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 53. Base statistics use Hawk in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 330. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=54
sections.Traits: Keen Sight. The falcon has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
sections.Actions: Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 1 slashing damage.
sections.Adventure context: Lord Gralhund keeps the falcon hooded in a cage in the Den and Trophy Room, area G10.

name: Maxeene
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. Speaks Common.
appearance: A muscular chestnut draft mare with a dark mane, a pale blaze, and feathered fetlocks.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 37. Base statistics use Draft Horse in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 321. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=38
sections.Actions: Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Harper mission: Find Maxeene with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check. A successful DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check convinces her the characters are Harpers. She recalls carrying two passengers whose descriptions match Davil Starsong and Yagra Stonefist to the Yawning Portal and overhearing their discussion of hiring spies to find Xanathar Guild hideouts. Each Harper character earns 1 renown.

name: Obliteros
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +3. Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 13. Speaks and understands Aquan.
appearance: An immense gray shark with a pale underside, a triangular dorsal fin, and visible rows of teeth.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 66. Base statistics use Giant Shark in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 328. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=67
sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Water Breathing. It can breathe only underwater.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.
sections.Harbor encounter: When the characters search Waterdeep’s harbor for treasure in Grinda Garloth’s submersible, roll any die. An even result means Obliteros attacks.

name: Sylgar
otherStatistics: Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 8. Languages none.
appearance: A small orange-gold fish with a pale belly, translucent fins, and a gently forked tail.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, first printing, September 2018, p. 220. Base statistics use Quipper in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 335. https://online.anyflip.com/degf/fwng/mobile/index.html#p=221
sections.Traits: Water Breathing. Sylgar can breathe only underwater.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 1 piercing damage.
sections.Adventure context: When a character uses Sylgar as leverage over Xanathar, a DC 16 Charisma (Intimidation) check determines the response. On a success, Xanathar agrees to almost any request. On a failure, it demands Sylgar’s release and follows through on its threat to disintegrate the character if they refuse.

name: Crow
publication: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 13. Languages none.
appearance: A small black corvid with a stout bill and layered dark flight feathers.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Level 23, Mad Wizard’s Lair, p. 302, 36. Gate to Triboar. Uses the Raven from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 335.
sections.Traits: Mimicry. It can copy simple sounds it has heard. A creature hearing an imitation can identify it with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.
sections.Actions: Beak. Make a +4 melee weapon attack against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 1 piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: The crow perches on the northern standing stone. It caws at people entering the room and bonds with a randomly chosen character.

name: Giant Flying Spider
publication: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Blindsight 10 ft. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages none.
appearance: A large dark-bodied spider with eight jointed legs and a pair of smoky wings.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Level 10, Muiral’s Gauntlet, p. 150, 30a. Main Cavern. Uses the Giant Spider from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 328.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The creature can traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Web Sense. While touching a web, it pinpoints any other creature touching that same web.
Web Walker. It ignores the movement restrictions of webbing.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Make a +5 melee weapon attack against one creature within 5 ft. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failure or half as much on a success. If the poison drops it to 0 HP, it is stable and Poisoned for 1 hour even if it regains HP. It is Paralyzed while Poisoned this way.
Web (recharge 5–6). Make a +5 ranged weapon attack against one creature, range 30/60 ft. A hit Restrains it in webbing. It can take an action to burst free with a successful DC 12 Strength check. The web can also be destroyed. It has AC 10, 5 HP, vulnerability to fire and immunity to bludgeoning, poison and psychic damage.
sections.Encounter: Five flying spiders join the cavern patrol. They fly around the cavern and build web nests in the caps of zurkhwood mushrooms.

name: Giant Lizard (variant)
publication: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages none.
appearance: A large mottled green climbing lizard with a long tapering tail and broad gripping toes.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Level 10, Muiral’s Gauntlet, p. 147, 25a. Hall of the Dark Seldarine and 30a. Main Cavern. Uses the Giant Lizard and Variant: Giant Lizard Traits from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 326.
sections.Traits: Spider Climb. The creature can traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
sections.Actions: Bite. Make a +4 melee weapon attack against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: The docile lizards are drow mounts. Two wear riding gear in the hall. More are ridden by the cavern patrol.

name: Haungharassk
publication: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. Cannot speak. The adventure does not specify any languages it understands.
appearance: An elephant-sized snail with long eyestalks, a broad creeping foot and a gleaming coiled golden shell threaded with brighter gold.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Level 20, Runestone Caverns, p. 258, 8d. Golden Haungharassk and Aftermath.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The creature can traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Salt Sensitivity. Throwing 1 pound of salt onto its skin deals 1d6 acid damage to the snail.
Magical Properties. Detect magic shows a strong abjuration aura. A creature can take an action to touch the live snail and gain 6 temporary HP for 24 hours. A creature or object that touches it also gains the effect of remove curse. Once the snail dies, its touch stops granting these benefits.
sections.Actions: No attacks.
sections.Encounter: Characters can lead it by offering plants, fungi or algae. A successful DC 10 Intelligence (Nature) check identifies acceptable food. The glowing fungus in its cavern regrows when picked and dies if taken away. Halaster checks on the snail by scrying each day. If he detects that it was taken or killed, his shouts echo through the caverns.
sections.Treasure: If the snail is killed, characters can strip 100 lb. of gold worth 20,000 gp from the shell in a few hours. Killing the snail grants 0 XP.
sections.Source notes: The encounter gives 0 XP and no CR number. This display retains the indexed CR 0. Passive Perception 10 derives from Wisdom 10.

name: Space Hamster
publication: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
otherStatistics: Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages none.
appearance: A small, rounded hamster with a blunt whiskered muzzle, rounded ears and short paws.

sections.Printed source: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Level 19, Caverns of Ooze, p. 251, 13c. Galley and Mess Hall, Treasure. Uses the Rat from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 335.
sections.Traits: Keen Smell. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
sections.Actions: No attacks.
sections.Encounter: Removing the sending stone from the wall brings the hamster out of its lair in the ship’s wall. It poses no danger. A character can befriend it by offering food.

name: Giant Space Hamster
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Passive Perception 11. Languages —.
appearance: A heavy golden-brown hamster with rounded ears, full cheeks, small paws and a cream belly.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Boo’s Astral Menagerie, in Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, first printing, August 2022, p. 56. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/2821167-giant-space-hamster
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: These bear-sized plant-eaters generally avoid other creatures. They can be trained as mounts or pack animals. Gnomish attempts to power spelljamming ships with giant hamster wheels have failed so far.

name: Space Eel
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages —.
appearance: A blue-slate eel with a long coiled body, violet fins, a toothed mouth and a pointed tail spine.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Boo’s Astral Menagerie, in Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, first printing, August 2022, p. 55. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/2821197-space-eel
sections.Traits: Unusual Nature. The eel does not need air.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. While unattached, make one Bite attack and one Tail Spine attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage and attaches the eel. While attached, the eel cannot Bite. The target instead takes 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage at the start of each of the eel’s turns. Any creature, including the target, can use its action to remove the eel.
Tail Spine. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage. The target must pass a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target is paralyzed for as long as that poison lasts. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Bonus Actions: Detach. The eel can use a bonus action to detach itself from its target.
sections.Encounter ecology: These 5-ft.-long scavengers often trail ships to feed on barnacles. They usually avoid larger creatures unless starving, and Wildspace hunters prize their meat.

name: Space Guppy
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages —.
appearance: A short bronze-gold fish with a rounded face, dark blue eyes and flowing apricot fins.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Boo’s Astral Menagerie, in Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, first printing, August 2022, p. 55. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/2821198-space-guppy
sections.Traits:
Air Envelope. In a vacuum, a guppy with at least 1 HP can generate an air envelope around itself. The envelope sustains the guppy and one other Tiny creature in its space indefinitely.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke opportunity attacks.
sections.Actions: Tail Slap. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 1 bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: These 2- to 3-ft.-long flying fish sometimes serve as mounts for chwinga astronauts, sprites and other Tiny creatures.

name: Space Mollymawk
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Perception +5. Passive Perception 15. Languages —.
appearance: An albatross-like bird with long gray-white wings, dark flight feathers and a hooked bill.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Boo’s Astral Menagerie, in Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, first printing, August 2022, p. 57. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/2821200-space-mollymawk
sections.Traits:
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Hold Breath. The mollymawk can hold its breath for 15 minutes.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Adults are about 3 ft. tall with a 10-ft. wingspan. They scavenge around spelljamming ships and travel between their air envelopes. Some Wildspace crews consider it bad luck to kill one.

name: Space Swine
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. AC 16 with half-plate barding. Perception +4, Survival +4. Passive Perception 14. Languages —.
appearance: A bristly brown boar with curved tusks, hooves and two large feathered wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Boo’s Astral Menagerie, in Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, first printing, August 2022, p. 57. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/2821201-space-swine
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Combat variant: Battle-trained space swine are called death squealers and typically wear half-plate barding, raising AC from 11 to 16.
sections.Encounter ecology: Dohwars breed these winged boars to track, carry loads and serve as mounts for Small creatures. Adults stand about 3 ft. at the shoulder, are 5 to 6 ft. long and favor truffles.

name: Giant Dragonfly
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 10. No listed languages. Proficiency bonus +2.
appearance: A metallic blue-green dragonfly with large compound eyes, four clear veined wings and a long, tapered abdomen.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, first printing, August 2021, Appendix C, Creatures, Giant Dragonfly, p. 234. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/twbtw
sections.Traits: Drone. Its wingbeats can be heard as a loud drone up to 120 ft. away.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Uncanny Dodge. The dragonfly halves the damage from an attack against it if it can see the attacker.
sections.Encounter ecology: The printed dragonfly spans 20 ft. across the wings and feeds on smaller insects. The carnival trains some giant dragonflies to carry riders.

name: Giant Snail
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. No listed languages. Proficiency bonus +2.
appearance: A russet-brown snail with long eyestalks, a broad muscular foot and a sturdy brown spiral shell with a dark band.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, first printing, August 2021, Appendix C, Creatures, Giant Snail, p. 234. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/twbtw
sections.Traits: Salt Osmosis. Starting its turn in contact with at least 1 pound of salt deals the snail 1d4 necrotic damage. A creature can use an action to sprinkle 1 pound of salt on the snail. Provided the snail has not withdrawn into its shell, it takes 1d4 necrotic damage immediately and another 1d4 necrotic damage at the start of its next turn, when the salt rubs off.
sections.Actions:
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Shell Defense. The snail withdraws into its shell and gains +4 AC until it emerges. It can emerge as a bonus action on its turn.
sections.Encounter ecology: The carnival’s eight unusually fast racing snails have their own event rules.

name: Giant Swan
otherStatistics: Perception +4. Passive Perception 14. Speaks Common and Auran.
appearance: A white swan with an upright S-curved neck, a black-based orange bill and dark webbed feet.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, first printing, August 2021, Chapter 1, Witchlight Carnival, Gondola Swans, p. 38. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/twbtw Base statistics are from the 2014 Monster Manual, Giant Eagle, p. 324. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16881-giant-eagle
sections.Variant rules: Use the 2014 Giant Eagle statistics. The swan has no Talons attack. It can make two Beak attacks as one action and speaks Common and Auran.
sections.Traits: Keen Sight. The swan has advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Actions:
Two Beak Attacks. The swan makes two Beak attacks as an action.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Giant swans pull gondolas along the river that borders the carnival.

name: Pollenella the Honeybee
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. No listed languages. Proficiency bonus +2.
appearance: An orange-sized queen honeybee with a fuzzy thorax, a long banded abdomen and translucent veined wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, first printing, August 2021, Chapter 4, Yon, Amidor and Gleam, Pollenella the Honeybee, p. 135. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/twbtw
sections.Actions: Sting. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Pollenella is an orange-sized queen honeybee. Amidor freed her from a cyclops beekeeper and travels with her in Yon.

name: Giant Octopus
otherStatistics: Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 14. No languages.
appearance: A reddish brown octopus with eight curling arms and rows of pale suckers.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Rise of Tiamat Online Supplement v0.2, p. 16.
sections.Traits:
Hold Breath. It can hold its breath for 1 hour out of water.
Underwater Camouflage. It has advantage on underwater Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Water Breathing. It can breathe only underwater.
sections.Actions:
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 16) and remains restrained until the grapple ends. The octopus cannot use Tentacles on another target during that grapple.
Ink Cloud (recharges after a short or long rest). If the octopus is underwater, it releases ink in a 20-ft. radius around itself. The area is heavily obscured for 1 minute. A significant current can disperse the ink. After releasing it, the octopus can Dash as a bonus action.

name: Polar Bear
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 13. No listed special senses or languages.
appearance: A heavy cream-white bear with a long muzzle, rounded ears, and broad paws.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Rise of Tiamat Online Supplement v0.2, p. 22.
sections.Traits: Keen Smell. The bear has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

name: Warhorse
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 11. No listed skills, special senses, or languages.
appearance: A bay horse with a dark mane, tail, and lower legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Rise of Tiamat Online Supplement v0.2, p. 26.
sections.Traits: Trampling Charge. If the horse moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hits it with Hooves on the same turn, the target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the horse can make another Hooves attack against it as a bonus action.
sections.Actions: Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printing note: This supplement v0.2 prints Hooves at +4 to hit on p. 26. The separate 2014 Monster Manual errata changes its own Warhorse on p. 340 to +6. This entry follows the supplement.

name: Wolf
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 13. No listed special senses or languages.
appearance: A gray-brown wolf with pointed ears, a pale throat and legs, and a thick tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Rise of Tiamat Online Supplement v0.2, p. 27.
sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. It has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of that creature.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit must make a DC 11 Strength save or fall prone.

name: Elk
publication: DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. No languages or special senses.
appearance: A gold-brown elk with a dark mane, branching antlers, and a pale rump.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast D&D Adventurers League, Shawn Merwin, Suits of the Mists (DDAL4-01, ©2016), Mission 4, Glyphs, Appendix: Monster/NPC Statistics, printed and p. 36. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/177576/DDAL401-Suits-of-the-Mists-5e
sections.Traits: Charge. If the elk moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and then hits it with Ram on the same turn, deal an additional 7 (2d6) damage. A creature hit this way must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Actions:
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone target. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter notes: Five golden elk drink from an icy stream in the Quivering Forest. One is dying and can be separated from the herd.

name: Fire Stirge
publication: DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists
otherStatistics: AC includes natural armor. Cold damage vulnerability. Fire damage resistance. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 9. No languages.
appearance: A reddish brown flying creature with leathery wings, jointed legs, and a long pointed proboscis.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast D&D Adventurers League, Shawn Merwin, Suits of the Mists (DDAL4-01, ©2016), Mission 1, Stars, Appendix: Monster/NPC Statistics, printed and p. 14. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/177576/DDAL401-Suits-of-the-Mists-5e
sections.Actions:
Blood Drain. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage and the stirge attaches to the target. While attached it does not attack. At the start of each of the stirge’s turns the target loses 5 (1d4 + 3) HP to blood loss. The stirge can detach by spending 5 ft. of its movement. It does so after draining 10 HP of blood from the target or if the target dies. Any creature, including the target, can take an action to detach it.

Flare (Recharge 6). The stirge exhales fire into a 5-foot square adjacent to itself. A creature in the square makes a DC 10 Dexterity save, taking 5 (2d4) damage on a failure and no damage on a success.
sections.Encounter notes: Four fire stirges initially harass Hricu. Four more join the fight in the third round.

name: Giant Bat
publication: DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists
otherStatistics: Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A heavy brown bat with large ears and broad leathery wings extended in flight.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast D&D Adventurers League, Shawn Merwin, Suits of the Mists (DDAL4-01, ©2016), Mission 5, Mists, Appendix: Monster/NPC Statistics, printed and p. 42. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/177576/DDAL401-Suits-of-the-Mists-5e
sections.Traits:
Echolocation. The bat loses use of its blindsight while deafened.

Keen Hearing. The bat has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter notes: Four giant bats emerge from Barovia. They use the fog to conceal their movement as they swoop past the children and attack the characters.

name: Ice Cat
publication: DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists
otherStatistics: Perception +4. Stealth +6. Fire damage vulnerability. Cold damage resistance. Passive Perception 14. No languages or special senses.
appearance: A pale spotted feline with a thick coat, tufted ears, and a thick ringed tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast D&D Adventurers League, Shawn Merwin, Suits of the Mists (DDAL4-01, ©2016), Mission 1, Stars, Appendix: Monster/NPC Statistics, printed and p. 14. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/177576/DDAL401-Suits-of-the-Mists-5e
sections.Traits:
Ice Walk. The cat can cross and climb ice without making an ability check. Ice or snow difficult terrain costs no extra movement.

Keen Smell. The cat has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

Pounce. If the cat moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hits it with Claw on the same turn, the creature must succeed on a DC 12 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the cat can make one Bite against it as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter notes: Four cats rest among boulders at the top of an icy slope. They can pursue prey onto the ice and prefer to avoid the flame thistles.

name: Mastiff
publication: DDAL04-01 - The Suits of the Mists
otherStatistics: Perception +3. Passive Perception 13. No languages or special senses.
appearance: A tall, muscular tawny dog with a short coat, heavy muzzle, and dark facial mask.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast D&D Adventurers League, Shawn Merwin, Suits of the Mists (DDAL4-01, ©2016), Mission 4, Glyphs, Appendix: Monster/NPC Statistics, printed and p. 35. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/177576/DDAL401-Suits-of-the-Mists-5e
sections.Traits: Keen Hearing and Smell. The mastiff has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

name: Giant Two-Headed Goat
otherStatistics: AC includes natural armor. Languages none.
appearance: A horse-sized red-furred goat with two heads and curved, pitchfork-like horns.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Harried in Hillsfar, DDEX3-1, 2015, p. 14. The Birth, Demon Goats.
sections.Traits:
Charge. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit it with Ram on the same turn. The target takes 5 (2d4) extra bludgeoning damage. If it is a creature, it falls prone on a failed DC 13 Strength saving throw.
Sure-Footed. The goat has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws against effects that would knock it prone.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Ram attacks against different targets.
Ram. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter: The barnyard fight starts about 40 ft. away after the goats leave the barn. The default group is one giant two-headed goat and six goats. Saving Jovee removes three goats unless the party refuses Verner and attacks the newborns. If the party attacks the newborns, the goats grow immediately and the characters have advantage on their first attacks. For a weak party, the encounter adjustment removes four goats. The goats charge when they can. For a strong or very strong party, double the giant goat's hit points.

Once the alpha and at least half the other dogs are defeated, remaining dogs Disengage and flee. Remove three wild dogs for a weak party or add three for a strong or very strong party. The party has advantage on initiative if the first DC 10 Charisma check to get Pynroth's location succeeds, or disadvantage if it fails by more than 5.

otherStatistics: Languages none.

publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

Standing Leap. The moorbounder can long jump up to 40 ft. or high jump up to 20 ft. from a standstill or after a run.

Multiattack. Make one Blades attack and one Claw attack.

sections.Encounter ecology: The bristled offshoot hunts in the marshes and muddy foothills of Xhorhas. Its sharp hide makes it a poor mount.
sections.Encounter application: In Moorbounder Mayhem on p. 43, two bristled moorbounders threaten a mounted scout. A character can spend an action to frighten one away with a successful DC 21 Charisma (Intimidation) check.
sections.Source notes: The adventure prints a standalone Beast block on p. 203. The attack is Claw in this printing.

name: Moonshark
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +3. Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A massive slate-gray shark with a silver spear lodged in its side. A thick rope holds a gold-and-emerald amulet to its body.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Chapter 1, A Fateful Competition, E10 Moonshark Lair, p. 33. Use the Giant Shark base block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 328. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/a-fateful-competition#TheEmeraldGrotto
sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Water Breathing. The shark breathes only underwater.
Silver Spear. While the spear is lodged in its side, the shark sheds bright silver light within 10 ft. and dim light for another 10 ft. A character within 5 ft. can use an action to dislodge the spear with a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Spear-assisted swim. While the spear is embedded, if the shark uses its action to Bite and misses, it can spend a bonus action to swim up to 25 ft. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
sections.Emerald Eye: The rope holding the amulet has AC 17 and 5 HP, and characters can attack it to cut the amulet free. If the shark is dead or incapacitated, a character can remove the rope as an action.
sections.Encounter ecology: The Moonshark prowls the final chamber of Jigow’s Emerald Grotto. It attacks creatures entering its chamber.
sections.Encounter application: If the party crossed the grotto in 10 rounds or fewer, the rivals arrive after the shark encounter. At 11 to 15 rounds, the rivals enter and roll initiative in round 3. Unless hostile to the characters, they help fight the shark. Hostile rivals pursue the amulet or interfere with the characters without intentionally killing them. At 16 rounds or more, the rivals arrive first and reduce the shark to 75 HP before the characters roll initiative. At 0 HP the shark knocks over the southern pillar, breaking open the passage to E11.
sections.Source notes: The adventure inherits the Giant Shark block and gives effects tied to a removable spear. The Huge Beast classification comes from the 2014 parent block.

name: Young Horizonback Tortoise
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. Understands Goblin but cannot speak.
appearance: A fifteen-foot-tall tortoise with a high dome of overlapping shell plates, a thick beaked head, and sturdy legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Chapter 1, A Fateful Competition, J6 Herding the Horizonbacks, p. 26. Use the Ankylosaurus base block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 79. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/a-fateful-competition#AdventureStart
sections.Traits: Amphibious. The tortoise can breathe air and water.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, 10 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 18 (4d6 + 4) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Base-block action: The inherited Ankylosaurus Tail is a +7 melee weapon attack with 10 ft. reach against one target. It deals 18 (4d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Encounter ecology: Jigow’s young horizonbacks move from a paddock to fields west of the Jumble, where they start training as mounts and mobile buildings.
sections.Encounter application: Maneuvering a tortoise takes three successful Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks, starting at DC 12 and increasing by 1 after each check. On a failed check, it bucks the rider, who must make a DC 13 Dexterity save or fall for 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. Remounting requires a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. Failure prompts a Bite. A tortoise charmed through animal friendship or a similar effect does not buck its handler on a failed check, and the handler has advantage on checks to guide it.
sections.Source notes: The printed variant gives the tortoise a Bite modeled on the 2014 Ankylosaurus Tail. The adventure describes use of Bite and never expressly removes Tail. The indexed summary presents Bite alone. The Huge Beast classification comes from the parent block.

name: Giant Frog
otherStatistics: Perception +2 and Stealth +3. Darkvision 30 ft. Passive Perception 12. Languages none.
appearance: A broad-mouthed frog with mottled skin, large eyes, and folded powerful hind legs.

sections.Printed source: DDEX2-1 City of Danger, 2015 release , p. 32. Adventure context on pp. 30, 31.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The frog breathes air and water.
Standing Leap. It can long jump up to 20 ft. or high jump up to 10 ft., with or without a running start.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. Hit for 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage and grapple the target (escape DC 11). While that grapple lasts, the target is restrained and the frog cannot bite a different target.
Swallow. Make one Bite attack against a Small or smaller target the frog is grappling. On a hit, the target is swallowed and the grapple ends. The frog can hold one swallowed creature at a time. That creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from attacks and effects outside the frog, and takes 5 (2d4) acid damage at the start of each of the frog’s turns. When the frog dies, it stops restraining the swallowed creature. That creature can use 5 ft. of movement to escape the corpse and emerges prone.
sections.Deep Guardians encounter: Two giant frogs and four bullywugs patrol the partly submerged grotto below Mulmaster Bay. The guardians investigate when the trap is triggered. Add one giant frog for a strong or very strong party.

Wasps ignore a character treated in the prior 2 hours. They also ignore a character treated shortly before the lizardfolk encounter if the group has not since taken a long rest. A treated character forfeits that protection by attacking a wasp. If Sting paralyzes an adventurer, a wasp carries that adventurer back to the nest. The wasps fight to the death.
