publication: DDEX1-09 - Outlaws of the Iron Route
otherStatistics: Darkvision 60 ft. Languages none.
appearance: A chestnut weasel with a cream throat, long belly and raised, curling tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Outlaws of the Iron Route, DDEX1-9, December 2014, Appendix 1, p. 26.
sections.Traits: Keen Hearing and Smell. The weasel has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: The caverns hold three kobolds and five giant weasels, three of them chained. At the first sign of trouble, a kobold rushes to free them. The weasels attack anyone who threatens their handlers. For a very weak or weak party, remove one weasel. For a very strong party, add one.

name: Spider
publication: DDEX1-09 - Outlaws of the Iron Route
otherStatistics: Darkvision 30 ft. Languages none.
appearance: A small mottled tan spider with a rounded abdomen and eight thin, banded legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Outlaws of the Iron Route, DDEX1-9, December 2014, Appendix 1, p. 31.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. Climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without an ability check.
Web Sense. While touching a web, the spider knows the exact location of any other creature touching it.
Web Walker. Webbing does not impede its movement.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 1 piercing damage. On a failed DC 9 Constitution save, the target also takes 2 (1d4) poison damage.
sections.Encounter: One kobold can throw its spider jar up to 20 ft. Make a ranged improvised-weapon attack against a creature or object. On a hit the jar shatters for 1 piercing damage. Roll 1d6 for the spiders that land on the target. Each spider attacks once and then skitters away.

name: Armored Saber-Toothed Tiger
otherStatistics: Specially fitted half plate. Perception +3, Stealth +6. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A broad-shouldered saber-toothed cat wearing fitted half-plate barding.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Curse of Strahd, first printing, march 2016, Chapter 5, The Town of Vallaki, N5 Arasek Stockyard, p. 115. Inherits the Saber-Toothed Tiger stat block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 336. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cos/the-town-of-vallaki#AreasofVallaki
sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. The tiger has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on scent.
Pounce. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Claw on that turn. The creature falls prone on a failed DC 14 Strength save. A prone target can then be bitten once as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter application: The tiger was trained to hunt Vistani servants of Strahd, per the p. 115 erratum. If released, it can track Rictavio or Piccolo by scent. Rictavio can stop an attack and coax it into the wagon. During the Tyger, Tyger event on pp. 123–124, it roams until hurt, then attacks the perceived source of the harm.
sections.Encounter ecology: Rictavio keeps the tiger in his carnival wagon in Vallaki and feeds it through the roof hatch.
sections.Source notes:
The first printing replaces the base armor, HP, and challenge. It gives 84 HP without a replacement Hit Dice formula.
The printed base block gives +6 to hit and +5 damage on both attacks. The adventure does not change either value.
Publisher errata changes p. 115 to target Strahd’s Vistani servants and removes recognition by scent and clothing from that paragraph. Page 116 of the first printing describes broader targeting and is not separately amended in the errata.

name: Piccolo
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A small, dark-furred monkey with pale fur around the eyes, a curled tail, and a custom ballerina tutu.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Curse of Strahd, first printing, march 2016, Chapter 5, The Town of Vallaki, N7 Blinsky Toys, p. 118. Inherits the Baboon stat block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 318. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cos/the-town-of-vallaki#AreasofVallaki
sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. Piccolo has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally is within 5 ft. of that target and the ally is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +1 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 1 (1d4 − 1) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Rictavio gave Piccolo to Gadolf Blinsky. Blinsky trains him to fetch toys from shelves that are hard to reach.
sections.Source notes: The adventure names Piccolo as a monkey, explicitly using the Baboon rules. The tutu has no rules effect.

name: Sangzor
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A nine-foot-tall mountain goat with slate-gray fur, a lowered head, and an intent stare.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Curse of Strahd, first printing, march 2016, Chapter 9, Tsolenka Pass, Bloodhorn’s Charge, p. 160. Inherits the Giant Goat stat block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 326. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cos/tsolenka-pass#SpecialEvents
sections.Traits:
Charge. If Sangzor moves 20 ft. or more in a straight line toward a target and hits with Ram on the same turn, the attack deals 5 (2d4) extra bludgeoning damage. A creature hit falls prone if it fails a DC 13 Strength save.
Sure-Footed. Sangzor has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock it prone.
sections.Actions: Ram. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Defenses: Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Encounter application: If no character has passive Wisdom (Perception) 16 or higher, the party is surprised. Sangzor charges downhill. A target hit by the charge that fails the save tumbles 100 ft. to a ledge. Sangzor flees after taking 10 or more damage. Mist and snow limit visibility to 60 ft., and the goat escapes through a cleft once out of sight.
sections.Pelt: Berserkers in Strahd’s domain respect a creature wearing Sangzor’s pelt and leave the wearer and companions alone unless provoked.
sections.Encounter ecology: Mountain folk have hunted Sangzor, also called Bloodhorn, for years. Its gray fur blends into the rock above Tsolenka Pass.
sections.Source notes: The adventure changes Intelligence, alignment, HP, resistances, and challenge. It gives 33 HP without a replacement Hit Dice formula.

name: Lion
publication: DDEX2-04 - Mayhem in the Earthspur Mines
otherStatistics: Perception +3, Stealth +6. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A tawny lion with a full mane and heavy forepaws.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, DDEX2-04 - Mayhem in the Earthspur Mines, d&d expeditions release, april 1, 2015, Appendix, Monster/NPC Statistics, p. 26. https://www.dmsguild.com/product/170478/DDEX204-Mayhem-in-the-Earthspur-Mines-5e
sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. The lion has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on scent.
Pack Tactics. The lion has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally is within 5 ft. of that target and the ally is not incapacitated.
Pounce. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Claw on that turn. The creature falls prone on a failed DC 13 Strength save. A prone target can then be bitten once as a bonus action.
Running Leap. A 10-ft. running start lets the lion long jump up to 25 ft.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Darmov adds two lions to the arena when more than two characters join Bhún Ludwakazar in the fight.
sections.Source notes: The standalone block on p. 26 gives CR 1 and 200 XP. The adventure’s Combat Awards table on p. 23 lists 100 XP per lion for session rewards.

name: Mastiff
otherStatistics: Perception +3. Passive Perception 13. Languages none.
appearance: A fawn mastiff with a broad black muzzle, dropped ears, and a heavy chest.

sections.Printed source: DDEX3-14 Death on the Wall, March 1, 2016 release , p. 23. Patrol and kennel context on pp. 11–12.
sections.Traits: Keen Hearing and Smell. The mastiff has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Strength saving throw or fall prone.
sections.Patrols and kennels: The Yûlash camp keeps four mastiffs. One accompanies two guards on a patrol that moves through the camp. The patrol calls to unidentified people and demands identification before taking hostile action. The dogs at the kennel are tethered to a rail and cannot move more than 10 ft. from the kennel.

name: Winter Wolf
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 15. Languages Common, Giant and Winter Wolf.
appearance: A great shaggy wolf with a heavy white-gray coat and a broad muzzle. The encounter describes burning red eyes.

sections.Printed source: DDAL04-12 The Raven, version 1.0, p. 22. The encounter and party adjustments are on pp. 11–12.
sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. It has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if one of its allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and the ally is not incapacitated.
Snow Camouflage. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Make a +6 melee weapon attack against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 11 piercing damage. The printed dice expression is 2d6 + 3. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall Prone.
Cold Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 18 (4d8) cold damage. On a success it takes half as much.
sections.Encounter: Six winter wolves attack from the mist. They retreat into cover between attacks and focus on prone characters. The icy ground is difficult terrain and imposes disadvantage on saves to avoid falling prone. The wolves circle a fortified camp, harry sentries and prevent sleep. Characters who cannot sleep gain one level of exhaustion. If any reach two levels of exhaustion, the wolves attack. The pack gives up if the party gets 8 miles from the campsite. To run for it, count the party as having traveled 8 hours. At the end of each additional hour, each character makes a Constitution save at DC 10 plus hours traveled past 8 or gains one exhaustion level. Eluding the wolves awards 250 XP per character.
sections.Party strength: The encounter adjustments do not stack. Weak removes one Winter Wolf. Strong increases Cold Breath to a DC 13 save and 27 cold damage. Very Strong makes the same breath change and adds one Winter Wolf. The Very Weak line says to remove two Dire Wolves even though the main encounter lists six Winter Wolves.
sections.Treasure: A successful DC 11 Dexterity (Survival) check skins a killed wolf without ruining its pelt. Each intact pelt is worth 50 gp. If the party skins every killed wolf in the encounter, see p. 16 for Larga’s barter terms for a full set of pelts.
sections.Source notes: The appendix calls this a Beast. Bite’s printed fixed damage and dice expression disagree, so this profile uses the fixed 11 and records the printed roll. Cold Breath has no printed recharge. The Strong and Very Strong breath adjustments give a fixed damage number without dice.

name: Deathjump Spider
otherStatistics: Level 4 Skirmisher. Initiative +8. Fortitude 17, Reflex 18, Will 16. Bloodied 27. Perception +9, tremorsense 5 squares. Resist 5 poison. Languages —.
appearance: A human-sized, patterned brown spider with eight dark eyes, prominent fangs and eight jointed legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Scepter Tower of Spellgard, Adventure Book Two, pp. 41, 59, 60, 63. T1, Tower Stores. T12, Battlement. T13, Secure Storerooms. T15, Rooftop Battlement.
sections.Printed ability modifiers: Str +5, Dex +6, Con +4, Int -3, Wis +4, Cha +1.
sections.Printed powers:
Bite. Melee basic, standard, at-will, Poison. +6 vs. AC. On a hit, deal 2d6 + 3 damage. The target takes ongoing 5 poison damage and is slowed. One save ends both.
Death from Above. Melee, standard, at-will, Poison. Shift 6 squares and make a Bite attack. A hit deals 1d6 extra damage and also knocks the target prone.
Prodigious Leap. Move, encounter. Shift 10 squares.
sections.Traits and skills: Spider climb. Athletics +10 (+20 when jumping). Stealth +11.
sections.Encounter checks:
T1 uses three spiders with ettercaps. They use tremorsense to detect approaches at the southeast door and alert the webspinner. If entry takes 3 or more rounds, the webspinner has time to warn the fang guards through the southwest door. If the party enters the southern chamber promptly, the two closest spiders attack.
T12 uses two spiders. They stay out of combat until attackers reach the battlement level. On hearing battle they climb around the tower exterior and attack with Death from Above.
T13 uses four spiders. On the ceiling in darkness they have total concealment. A light directed at the webs reduces that to concealment and characters can compare Perception with the spiders’ Stealth +11 to see them. They attack if intruders investigate the northeast corner or try to open the vault doors. They flank and leap after characters who break away.
T15 uses a trained spider clinging 10 ft. above the lookouts on the spire. Its tremorsense detects approaches the lookouts cannot see. It drops on the party and fights to the death.

name: Fire Beetles
otherStatistics: Level 1 Brute. Initiative +1. Fortitude 13, Reflex 12, Will 11. Bloodied 16. Perception +0. Resist 10 fire. Languages —.
appearance: Five dog-sized beetles with dark carapaces, dark orange patches and ember-bright eyes.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Scepter Tower of Spellgard, Adventure Book Two, p. 7. R2, Lookout.
sections.Printed ability modifiers: Str +2, Dex +1, Con +1, Int -5, Wis +0, Cha -1.
sections.Printed powers:
Bite. Melee basic, standard, at-will. +5 vs. AC. On a hit, deal 2d4 + 2 damage.
Fire Spray. Close, standard, recharge 5–6, Fire. Close blast 3. +4 vs. Reflex. On a hit, deal 3d6 fire damage.
sections.Encounter checks: Franco Darano’s five trained beetles occupy the second floor. DC 16 Perception notices the faint red glow from the stairs. The beetles provide bright, torchlike illumination on the second level. If they leave or die, daylight through the arrow slits gives dim illumination. They use Fire Spray against groups and flank lone targets for Bite. On attack Franco calls for help and the R1 wererats arrive in 5 rounds. The beetles fight to the death.

name: Gray Wolves
otherStatistics: Level 2 Skirmisher. Initiative +5. Fortitude 14, Reflex 14, Will 13. Bloodied 19. Perception +7, low-light vision. Languages —.
appearance: A pack of lean gray wolves with mottled coats, narrow flanks and low stalking postures.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Scepter Tower of Spellgard, Adventure Book Two, p. 11. R6, Kennel.
sections.Printed ability modifiers: Str +2, Dex +3, Con +3, Int -3, Wis +2, Cha +1.
sections.Printed powers: Bite. Melee basic, standard, at-will. +7 vs. AC. On a hit, deal 1d6 + 2 damage, or 2d6 + 2 against a prone target.
sections.Traits and skills: Combat Advantage. When the wolf hits a target it has combat advantage against, the target also falls prone.
sections.Encounter checks:
Five hungry gray wolves are chained to the south wall by 20-ft. leashes. They cannot leave the room. The leash squares between wolf and anchor are difficult terrain, and the wolves ignore each other’s leashes. The kennel is dark. The wolves leave wererats and goblins alone and prefer fresh meat to trail rations. Their howls put occupants of R7 and R8 on alert for 1 hour. They flank and pile onto prone targets.
The first time a wolf knocks a PC prone in a chain square, describe the chain looping around the PC’s leg as the PC gets up. This first incident has no mechanical effect. On the next such knockdown, an adjacent wolf can move through at least three squares adjacent to the prone PC, provoking opportunity attacks normally. The attacking wolf can do this if it still has a move action. The chain entangles the prone PC, who is grabbed by that wolf. Other wolves attack the PC normally.

name: Spitting Drake
otherStatistics: Level 3 Artillery. Initiative +5. Fortitude 14, Reflex 16, Will 14. Bloodied 19. Perception +3. Resist 10 acid. Languages —.
appearance: A wingless bronze drake with four clawed feet, an angular head, a plated spine and a long tapering tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Scepter Tower of Spellgard, Adventure Book Two, p. 8. R4, Bunkroom.
sections.Printed ability modifiers: Str +3, Dex +5, Con +3, Int -3, Wis +3, Cha +2.
sections.Printed powers:
Bite. Melee basic, standard, at-will. +6 vs. AC. On a hit, deal 1d6 + 2 damage.
Caustic Spit. Ranged, standard, at-will, Acid. Ranged 10 squares. +8 vs. Reflex. On a hit, deal 1d10 + 4 acid damage.
sections.Encounter checks: Two trained drakes join three human guards in the frontal defense of the bunkroom while a shadowhunter bat and Borlem Darano take their positions. The guards press the party while the drakes use Caustic Spit on the back ranks. The drakes fight to the death. Fighting alerts Kalmo at R5, who sends two gravehounds in round 4 and two more in round 5, then joins in round 6.

name: Dire Bear
otherStatistics: Level 11 Elite Brute. Initiative +8. Fortitude 25, Reflex 22, Will 23. Bloodied 138. Perception +9. Saving throws +2. 1 action point. No listed languages.
appearance: A massive tawny brown bear with a heavy shoulder hump, broad paws and small ivory projections along its upper back.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, King of the Trollhaunt Warrens, first printing, October 2008, Adventure Book Two, Encounter W4, Mound of Skulls, stat block p. 17 and encounter pp. 16–17.
sections.Printed powers:
Claw. Melee basic attack, standard, at-will. Reach 2. +15 vs. AC. Hit for 2d8 + 6 damage.
Maul. Melee, standard, at-will. Make two Claw attacks. If both hit the same target, make a secondary attack against it at +13 vs. AC. A hit grabs the target until escape.
Ursine Crush. Melee, standard, at-will. Deal 4d8 + 6 damage to a grabbed creature without an attack roll.
sections.Encounter: Norgg’s bear lies below the ledge and gnaws on bones. In combat it attacks the closest target, using Maul to establish a grab before Ursine Crush. Norgg and the bear stay in the chamber if the party flees.

name: Redspawn Firebelcher
otherStatistics: Level 12 Artillery. Initiative +7. Fortitude 25, Reflex 22, Will 21. Bloodied 48. Perception +6, low-light vision. Resist 20 fire. No listed languages.
appearance: A squat, wingless russet reptile with a broad jaw, heavy legs, spined back and long curved tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, King of the Trollhaunt Warrens, first printing, October 2008, Adventure Book Two, Encounter W7, The Foundry, stat block p. 25 and encounter pp. 24–25.
sections.Aura: Fire Within, Fire, aura 5. Allies inside the aura gain resist 10 fire.
sections.Printed powers:
Bite. Melee basic attack, standard, at-will, Fire. +16 vs. AC. Hit for 1d10 + 4 damage and ongoing 5 fire damage (save ends).
Fire Belch. Ranged, standard, at-will, Fire. Range 12. +15 vs. Reflex. Hit for 2d6 + 1 damage and ongoing 5 fire damage (save ends).
Fire Burst. Area, standard, recharge 5–6, Fire. Area burst 2 within 10. +15 vs. Reflex. Hit for 3d6 + 1 damage and ongoing 5 fire damage (save ends). On a miss, deal half damage and no ongoing fire damage.
sections.Encounter: The firebelcher starts out of sight below the escarpment. If battle alerts it, it rolls initiative and enters in round two. It fires from near the top of the steps. Thurk stays close enough to gain its aura’s protection. The firebelcher flees if it is bloodied and Thurk falls.

name: Wyverns
otherStatistics: Level 10 Skirmisher. Initiative +10. Fortitude 24, Reflex 20, Will 19. Bloodied 53. Perception +12, low-light vision. No listed languages. The encounter fields three wyverns worth 500 XP each.
appearance: Two studies of a brown, two-legged wyvern with leathery wings, a narrow head and a long tail ending in a curved stinger.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, King of the Trollhaunt Warrens, first printing, October 2008, Adventure Book Two, Encounter R3, Airborne Assault, stat block p. 42 and encounter pp. 42–43.
sections.Printed powers:
Bite. Melee basic attack, standard, at-will. Reach 2. +15 vs. AC. Hit for 1d8 + 7 damage.
Claws. Melee basic attack, standard, at-will. Only while flying. +15 vs. AC. Hit for 1d6 + 7 damage and knock the target prone.
Sting. Melee, standard, at-will, Poison. Reach 2. +15 vs. AC. Hit for 1d6 + 4 damage, then make a secondary attack against the same target at +13 vs. Fortitude. A secondary hit deals ongoing 10 poison damage (save ends).
Flyby Attack. Melee, standard, at-will. Fly up to 8 squares and make one melee basic attack at any point during the movement. It provokes no opportunity attacks while moving away from the target of that attack.
sections.Mount: Aerial Agility +2, at-will, Mount. While the wyvern is flying with a rider of level 10 or higher, that rider gains +2 to all defenses.
sections.Encounter: All three wyverns fly over the Old Troll Wall. They go after the adventurers once the adventurers attack. They use Claws from the air and land to help the other attackers if those allies are engaged in melee, alternating Bite and Sting. The troglodyte remounts a wyvern if its manticore is killed first.

name: Female Steeder
publication: Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.
appearance: A large tarantula-like steeder with a broad body and thick hairy legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters, Appendix C: Creatures, p. 62.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without an ability check.
Leap. If its speed is at least 30 ft., the steeder can spend all its movement on its turn to jump up to 90 ft. vertically or horizontally.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 12 Constitution save and takes 9 (2d8) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sticky Leg (recharges when no creatures are grappled by the steeder). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. On a hit, the target sticks to its leg and is grappled until it escapes (escape DC 12).
sections.Encounter ecology: Duergar train these larger steeders as mounts. They do not spin webs. Their legs secrete the adhesive used to climb and catch prey.

name: Male Steeder
publication: Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.
appearance: A pony-sized tarantula-like steeder with compact body and long, bristled legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters, Appendix C: Creatures, pp. 62–63.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without an ability check.
Leap. If its speed is at least 30 ft., the steeder can spend all its movement on its turn to jump up to 60 ft. vertically or horizontally.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 12 Constitution save and takes 4 (1d8) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sticky Leg (recharges when no creatures are grappled by the steeder). Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Small or Tiny creature. On a hit, the target sticks to its leg and is grappled until it escapes (escape DC 12).
sections.Encounter ecology: Duergar use these pony-sized steeders as beasts of burden. Their leg secretions allow climbing and capture.

name: Female Steeder
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.
appearance: A large tarantula-like steeder with a broad body and thick hairy legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, DDEX3-16 - Assault on Maerimydra, Monster/NPC Statistics appendix, p. 54.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without an ability check.
Leap. The steeder can use all its movement to jump up to 120 ft. vertically or horizontally.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 12 Constitution save and takes 9 (2d8) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sticky Leg (recharges when no creatures are grappled by the steeder). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. On a hit, the target sticks to its leg and is grappled until it escapes (escape DC 12).
sections.Encounter ecology: A quaggoth rider joins the fight on a female steeder, and the adventure also provides two female steeder mounts.

name: Spider King
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 14. No languages. The HP is fixed at 44 by the adventure.
appearance: A demonic mutation has given this giant spider two heads and raised its front into a vaguely humanoid posture.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Out of the Abyss, Chapter 4: Gracklstugh, p. 74.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without an ability check.
Web Sense. While touching a web, it knows the exact location of any other creature touching the same web.
Web Walker. It ignores movement restrictions caused by webs.
Two heads. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious.
Dire Den awareness. It senses intruders who enter its domain and cannot be surprised by them.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If the poison damage reduces it to 0 HP, it is stable and poisoned for 1 hour even after regaining HP. It is paralyzed while poisoned this way.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. A hit restrains the target in webbing. The target can use its action to make a DC 12 Strength check and break the web on a success. The web can also be attacked to destroy it. It has AC 10 and 5 HP, is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: It waits with two ordinary giant spiders. It blocks the chamber entrance while they approach along the walls or ceiling. They fight to the death and do not follow fleeing prey.

name: Young Bulette
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No listed skills, special senses, or languages.
appearance: A juvenile bulette with a low armored body, powerful forelimbs, and a broad toothed mouth.
habitats: Temple of the Elder Elemental Eye

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Princes of the Apocalypse, Chapter 5: Temple of the Elder Elemental Eye, p. 139.
sections.Traits: Charge. If it moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Bite on the same turn, the hit deals 9 (2d8) extra bludgeoning damage. A creature hit also makes a DC 15 Strength save or falls prone.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Three young bulettes occupy the north kennels. They sleep if Rorgrin is absent. A character sneaking past them makes a DC 11 Dexterity (Stealth) check. They awaken on a failed check or if attacked and hiss at strangers to alert Rorgrin.
sections.Printing note: Area G13 calls for the Rhinoceros statistics with Bite in place of Gore. The Beast type comes from that proxy. The adventure supplies no separate damage type, so Bite retains the proxy’s bludgeoning damage.

name: Golden Stag
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. No listed skills, special senses, or languages in the normal stag branch.
appearance: A tall stag with a coat that shines like spun gold and pale branching antlers that look plated with platinum.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Hoard of the Dragon Queen, Episode 4: On the Road, p. 35.
sections.Traits: Charge. If the stag moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Ram on the same turn, the hit deals 7 (2d6) extra damage. A creature hit must also succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Actions:
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. On a hit, deal 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: In the normal stag branch, the hunters can corner and fight the animal. In two other branches it speaks a prophecy or is discovered to be a cursed elf prince. The Beast profile uses the adventure’s Elk instructions.
sections.Printing note: The p. 35 encounter directs the DM to use Elk statistics. The publisher errata changes the older table label The Golden Hind to The Golden Stag. The Elk supplement gives no separate damage type for the additional Charge dice.

name: Giant Fly
otherStatistics: Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. No languages in the creature block. The block gives no XP or specific attack.
appearance: A dark horsefly with large compound eyes, short antennae, and veined wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Dungeon Master's Guide (2014), Chapter 7, Figurine of Wondrous Power, p. 169. https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/4831-figurine-of-wondrous-power-ebony-fly
sections.Figurine use: As an action, speak the command word. Throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 ft. It becomes a living Giant Fly if there is space and the destination is clear of creatures and objects. The fly can carry a rider and remains for up to 12 hours. The fly is friendly to you and your companions, understands your languages, and follows spoken commands. Without a command, the fly defends itself and takes no other actions. It returns to figurine form when time expires or it drops to 0 HP. The figurine can be used again after 2 days. It also reverts if you spend an action speaking the command word while touching it.

name: Giant Fly
otherStatistics: Initiative +1 (11). Proficiency bonus +2. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. No languages in the creature block.
appearance: A dark horsefly with large compound eyes, short antennae, and veined wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Dungeon Master's Guide (2024), Chapter 7, Figurine of Wondrous Power, p. 261. https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/9228613-figurine-of-wondrous-power-ebony-fly
sections.Figurine use: Take a Magic action. Throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 ft. It becomes a living Giant Fly if there is space and the destination is clear of creatures and objects. The fly can carry a rider and remains for up to 12 hours. The fly is friendly to you and your allies, understands your languages, and obeys your commands. It acts immediately after you on the same initiative count. Without a command, the fly defends itself and takes no other actions. It returns to figurine form when time expires or it drops to 0 HP. The figurine can be used again after 2 days. It also reverts if you take a Magic action to make it revert while touching it.

name: Wolf of the Overworld
otherStatistics: AC includes natural armor. Perception +5. Stealth +4. Passive Perception 15. Proficiency bonus +2. No languages or special senses.
appearance: A gray-furred wolf with a thick coat, pointed ears, and a bushy tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast with Mojang Studios, Monstrous Compendium Vol. 3: Minecraft Creatures, Wolf of the Overworld, p. 7.
sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The wolf has advantage on attack rolls against a creature within 5 ft. of one of its allies, provided that ally is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Encounter notes: Wild wolves usually ignore humanoids but their pack turns hostile if someone hurts a pack member. Adventurers can tame one by feeding and caring for it. Even tame wolves instinctively attack animated skeletons unless told to sit.

name: Hippocampus
publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
otherStatistics: Ability modifiers STR +4, DEX +1, CON +1, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -1. Fixed Perception 13. Fixed Stealth 11. Cold damage resistance. Darkvision 60 ft. No languages.
appearance: A blue-green creature with horse forequarters, coral-pink fins, and a curving fish tail.

sections.Printed source: Open Design LLC d/b/a Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, Monsters, pp. 305–306.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The hippocampus can breathe air and water.

Shared Breath. Its gills release extra air as bubbles along its neck and back. An air-breathing rider can use the bubbles for fresh air while the hippocampus is neither fighting nor traveling at a fast pace.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail Slap.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.

Tail Slap. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Rearing Kick. The hippocampus rears and kicks with its forelegs at one creature it can see within 5 ft. The target makes a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, the hippocampus chooses whether to knock it prone or push it up to 10 ft. away.

name: Orca
publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
otherStatistics: Ability modifiers STR +4, DEX +0, CON +1, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -2. AC includes natural armor. Fixed Perception 13. Fixed Stealth 10. Cold damage resistance. Keensense 120 ft. No languages.
appearance: A black-and-white orca with a tall dorsal fin, pale eye patches, and a broad fluked tail.

sections.Printed source: Open Design LLC d/b/a Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, Monsters, p. 365.
sections.Traits:
Echolocation. The orca loses use of its keensense while deafened.

Heightened Hearing. Its Perception is 18 when it relies on hearing.

Hold Breath. The orca can hold its breath for 30 minutes.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 14 (3d6 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Tail Slap. The orca slaps one creature it can see within 15 ft. The target makes a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, the target is pushed up to 15 ft. away and knocked prone. If it fails by 5 or more, it is also stunned through the end of its next turn.

name: Birdsquirrel
appearance: A tiny brown bird with clawed feet and a large, curling squirrel tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Adventure with Muk, Monsters, unnumbered sheet 30.
sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The birdsquirrel has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally of the birdsquirrel is within 5 ft. of that creature and the ally is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Attack +4. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Claws. Attack +4. On a hit, deal 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
sections.Ecology: Birdsquirrel is devoted to Muk. It may be a one-of-a-kind creation of the wizard Doonwaggle.

otherStatistics: Initiative -3.

name: Boontu Monkey
appearance: A tiny chestnut monkey with pale cheeks, gripping fingers and a curling tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Adventure with Muk, Monsters, unnumbered sheet 30.
sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The Boontu monkey has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally of the Boontu monkey is within 5 ft. of that creature and the ally is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Attack +1. On a hit, deal 1 (1d4 - 1) piercing damage.
sections.Ecology: These wary monkeys search constantly for food and leave the sacred golden nuts on their home tree alone. A local story says a dryad transformed thieves into the monkeys after catching them stealing her nuts.

otherStatistics: Initiative +2.

name: Two-Headed Plesiosaurus
appearance: A gray-blue marine reptile with two long necks, four broad flippers and a short tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Tortle Package, High Horn, pp. 18, 19.
sections.Traits:
Hold Breath. It can hold its breath for 1 hour.
Two heads. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned or knocked unconscious.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Use its action to make two Bite attacks, one per head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (3d6 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: It hunts around the High Horn shipwrecks at high tide and retreats to the northern strait as the tide falls.

otherStatistics: AC includes natural armor. Languages none.

name: Wolf
appearance: A gray-brown wolf with pointed ears, a pale muzzle and a thick tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, DDEX1-01 - Defiance in Phlan, Missions 2 and 5, Monster/NPC Statistics, pp. 15, 31.
sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. The wolf has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally of the wolf is within 5 ft. of that creature and the ally is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit this way falls prone on a failed DC 11 Strength save.
sections.Encounter:
Mission 2, area 2C. Three goblins guard two caged wolves. A goblin can unlock a cage as an action. For a weak party, remove one goblin and one wolf. For a strong party, replace one wolf with a worg. For a very strong party, replace both with uncaged worgs.
Mission 5, area 3B. The guard room has a large dog using these Wolf statistics. Add one wolf for a very strong party.

otherStatistics: AC includes natural armor. Languages none.

name: Clawfoot
publication: Eberron: Rising from the Last War
otherStatistics: Perception +3, Stealth +5. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A tall-human-sized bipedal dinosaur with sharp teeth, a stiff tail, and large sickle-shaped toe claws.

sections.Printed source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War, Chapter 6, Friends and Foes, Dinosaurs, p. 289. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/erftlw/friends-and-foes#Dinosaurs
sections.Traits:
Pack Tactics. The clawfoot has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally is within 5 ft. of that target and the ally is not incapacitated.
Pounce. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Claws on the same turn. It falls prone if it fails a DC 11 Strength save. The clawfoot can then Bite that target once as a bonus action if it is prone.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Clawfoots hunt larger prey, often in packs. Talenta halflings train these dinosaurs as war mounts.
sections.Source notes: Charisma is 6 (−2) in the printed block. The indexed summary gives 10.

name: Fastieth
publication: Eberron: Rising from the Last War
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. No languages.
appearance: A human-sized bipedal plant-eater with large eyes, strong hindlegs, and brightly patterned scales.

sections.Printed source: Eberron: Rising from the Last War, Chapter 6, Friends and Foes, Dinosaurs, p. 289. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/erftlw/friends-and-foes#Dinosaurs
sections.Traits: Quickness (Recharge 5–6). The fastieth can take Dodge as a bonus action.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Fastieths prefer to flee when threatened. Talenta halflings breed them for speed and favor even-tempered animals as riding mounts. A fastieth can carry a halfling with light gear but is too small for larger riders.
sections.Source notes: The p. 289 block prints Quickness under traits. It uses a bonus action and recharges on 5–6.

name: Two-Headed Crocodile
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +2, Stealth +2. Passive Perception 12. No languages.
appearance: A low, armored crocodile with two independent heads and one long tail.

sections.Printed source: Infernal Machine Rebuild, Appendix B, NPCs and Monsters, p. 89. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/imr/npcs-and-monsters
sections.Traits:
Hold Breath. The crocodile holds its breath for up to 15 minutes.
Two Heads. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious.
Wakeful. If one head falls asleep, the other stays awake.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one creature. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage and grapples the creature, escape DC 12. The captive is restrained while grappled. The head holding it cannot bite another target until the grapple ends.
sections.Encounter ecology: One crocodile accompanies the lizardfolk shaman in the Temple of Moloch guardroom. If guards in area 5 warn them about intruders, the guardroom group goes to area 1 to intercept them.
sections.Source notes: The appendix gives a standalone Large Beast block. The bite restriction applies to the head maintaining the grapple.

name: Chimeric Fox
publication: NERDS Restoring Harmony: A Voice in the Wilderness
otherStatistics: Perception +3, Stealth +5. Darkvision 60 ft. Proficiency bonus +2. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A small fox with pale fur that shifts to the tan of its surroundings.

sections.Printed source: NERDS Restoring Harmony: A Voice in the Wilderness, Adventure 2, Monster/NPC Statistics, p. 8.
sections.Traits:
Chimeric Creation. The fox’s coat changes color to match its surroundings, granting advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Keen Hearing. The fox has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on hearing.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one creature. A hit deals 1 piercing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: A skittish fox follows Red and Elowen on the trip to Lemondrop Ledges. If Red treats it kindly, it tags along and may bark to warn them or distract a foe.
sections.Source notes: The supplies a complete Tiny Beast block on unnumbered sheet 8. The NERDS encounter on sheet 5 describes the fox choosing to follow Red after kind treatment.

name: Panther
otherStatistics: Perception +4. Stealth +6. Passive Perception 14. No languages.
appearance: A low-set black cat with rounded ears, broad paws and a long tail. Faint spotting shows through its coat.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, DDEX1-08 - Tales Trees Tell, November 1, 2014 release, Appendix, Monster/NPC Statistics, p. 26.
sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use smell.
Pounce. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Claw on the same turn. The creature falls prone unless it passes a DC 12 Strength save. If the creature is prone, the panther can make a Bite attack against it as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: The adventure places the panthers in the Quivering Forest as a weaker-party adjustment to the displacer beast encounter. It calls for three panthers in that adjustment.
sections.Source notes: The appendix contains the complete Panther stat block. The printed adventure code is DDEX1-8. Its catalog name retains the roster’s DDEX1-08 spelling. The pounce attack requires the same-turn approach and Claw hit. The bonus-action Bite checks whether the target is prone.

name: Relic Sloth
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Proficiency bonus +2. Perception +3. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A hulking, shaggy gray-brown beast with a long neck, strong forelimbs and inward-curving sickle claws.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Strixhaven: A Curriculum of Chaos, first printing, November 2021, chapter 7, Friends and Foes, p. 210. https://online.anyflip.com/usqxr/xjis/files/large/4b4ebc7af65997f4196bafa5ebd13056.webp
sections.Actions: Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage and grapple the target (escape DC 15). The sloth can hold up to two targets at once.
sections.Reactions: Slow but Sturdy. When something would force the sloth out of its space or knock it prone, it can use its reaction to stay in place and upright.
sections.Encounter ecology: Lorehold mages use relic sloths to carry gear and artifacts. Their slow, deliberate movement suits unstable ruins, and their long foreclaws help them climb.
sections.Source notes: Slow but Sturdy is a reaction. Claws is one attack against one target, with a maximum of two simultaneous grapples.

name: Swarm of Maggots
otherStatistics: Blindsight 10 ft. Passive Perception 8. Proficiency bonus +2. Resist bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing. Immune to charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned. No languages.
appearance: A low heap of soft, pale segmented larvae with small tapered ends.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Van Richten’s Guide to Ravenloft, first printing, May 2021, chapter 5, Monsters of Ravenloft, Swarms, p. 247. https://online.anyflip.com/npkza/fwfi/files/mobile/248.webp
sections.Traits: Swarm. It and another creature can share space. It passes through any opening big enough for a Tiny maggot. It cannot recover HP or gain temporary HP.
sections.Actions:
Infestation. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. A hit deals 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) when the swarm has half its HP or less. A creature the swarm damages makes a DC 12 Constitution save or contracts a disease. At the end of each long rest, roll a d6 for the effect.
1–2. Blinded until the creature finishes a long rest.
3–4. Reduce its HP maximum by 5 (2d4). That reduction lasts until the disease ends. The creature dies if its maximum drops to 0.
5–6. Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls until it finishes its next long rest.
The disease ends when magic removes it or when the creature rolls the same result band on two consecutive long rests.
sections.Encounter ecology: The book presents these maggots as scavenging larvae whose numbers and aggression increase as sinister forces take hold.
sections.Source notes: The original stat block omits an alignment. It uses blindsight 10 ft. and grants swim speed 20 ft. Disease onset is a Constitution save after the swarm deals damage. Its symptom roll is made at the end of a long rest.

name: Swarm of Scarabs
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Tremorsense 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. Proficiency bonus +2. Resist bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing. Immune to charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned. No languages.
appearance: A clustered mass of dark oval scarab beetles with ridged wing cases and short legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Van Richten’s Guide to Ravenloft, first printing, May 2021, chapter 5, Monsters of Ravenloft, Swarms, p. 247. https://online.anyflip.com/npkza/fwfi/files/mobile/248.webp
sections.Traits:
Swarm. It and another creature can share space. It passes through any opening big enough for a Tiny scarab. It cannot recover HP or gain temporary HP.
Skeletonize. If it starts its turn in the same space as a dead creature of Large size or smaller, it destroys the corpse and leaves its equipment and bones or exoskeleton.
Spider Climb. It crosses difficult surfaces, including the underside of ceilings, without an ability check.
sections.Actions: Ravenous Bites. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. A hit deals 14 (4d6) piercing damage, or 7 (2d6) when the swarm has half its HP or less. If the target is a creature, the scarabs burrow into it and deal 3 (1d6) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. Any creature can use an action to remove or kill the scarabs with fire or a piercing weapon. The target takes 1 damage of the corresponding type. A creature the swarm’s piercing damage reduces to 0 HP dies.
sections.Encounter ecology: These scavenging beetles form predatory swarms where malign forces take hold. A swarm can overwhelm a corpse at the start of its turn.
sections.Source notes: The original stat block omits an alignment. It uses tremorsense 60 ft. and has separate walking, burrowing and climbing speeds. The printed attack gives no saving throw against its continuing damage. Any creature can spend an action to remove the scarabs.

name: Ebonclaw
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Perception +3. Stealth +6. Passive Perception 13. Languages: Common.
appearance: A powerful saber-toothed cat with a short tail and long upper canines.

sections.Printed source:
Turn of Fortune's Wheel, Ch. 8, Faunel, Razortooth Rock, p. 50. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/paitm/tofw/the-mosaic-mimir#TheThreePacks
Inherited rules from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 336, Saber-Toothed Tiger. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2014/miscellaneous-creatures
sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. Ebonclaw has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on smell.
Pounce. A Claw hit after moving at least 20 ft. straight toward the creature that turn forces a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure the target falls prone. Ebonclaw can use Bite once as a bonus action against the prone target.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Ebonclaw leads the sapient predators of Razortooth Rock. He is suspicious of strangers and loathes the Vile Hunt.
sections.Encounter procedure: Ebonclaw agrees to speak after a successful DC 16 Charisma (Intimidation or Persuasion) check or a gift of fresh yak meat.
sections.Source notes: The adventure changes alignment, Intelligence and Charisma to 12, and speech to Common. The indexed summary instead carries the base tiger’s Intelligence 3 and Charisma 8. The 2014 Monster Manual supplies the other combat numbers.

name: Ophelia
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Natural armor. Passive Perception 12. Languages: Common.
appearance: A sapient elephant with thick gray hide, an expressive trunk and long tusks.

sections.Printed source:
Turn of Fortune's Wheel, Ch. 8, Faunel, Heart Delta, p. 50. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/paitm/tofw/the-mosaic-mimir#TheThreePacks
Inherited rules from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 322, Elephant. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2014/miscellaneous-creatures
sections.Traits: Trampling Charge. A Gore hit after moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature that turn forces a DC 12 Strength save. On a failure the target falls prone. Ophelia can then Stomp that prone target once as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +8, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 19 (3d8 + 6) piercing damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +8, reach 5 ft. A hit on one prone creature deals 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Ophelia leads the sapient herbivores of Faunel and speaks to gathered animals in the Hollow.
sections.Source notes:
The adventure changes alignment, Intelligence to 10, Wisdom and Charisma to 14, and speech to Common. Its prose does not restate passive Perception. The displayed 12 follows the new Wisdom modifier with no Perception proficiency. The base elephant has passive Perception 10.
The 2023 adventure inherits the 2014-rules Elephant. The November 2018 Monster Manual errata supplies the +6 damage bonus already in force when the adventure appeared. The first 2014 printing used +5 for both.

name: Parvaz
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Perception +4. Passive Perception 14. Languages: Common.
appearance: A giant albatross with very long narrow wings, a pale body and an elongated hooked bill.

sections.Printed source:
Turn of Fortune's Wheel, Ch. 8, Faunel, Eagles’ Aerie, p. 51. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/paitm/tofw/the-mosaic-mimir#TheThreePacks
Inherited rules from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 324, Giant Eagle. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2014/miscellaneous-creatures
sections.Traits: Keen Sight. Parvaz has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Beak and one Talons attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Parvaz holds court among Faunel’s flying animals. He knows where the Vile Hunt camps.
sections.Encounter procedure: A successful DC 18 Charisma (Persuasion) check convinces Parvaz to share the camp’s location. The owl figurine or another suitable gift can secure his help if the check fails.
sections.Source notes:
The adventure specifies neutral alignment, Intelligence 16, Charisma 14, and spoken Common. The displayed language follows the adventure’s named entry. The base Giant Eagle has its own language listing.
The attack names follow the borrowed Giant Eagle rules. Parvaz’s appearance follows the adventure’s albatross description.

name: Whirlwyrm
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +3. Natural armor. Stealth +5. Passive Perception 10. No languages listed.
appearance: An enormous serpentine eel that can rise ten feet out of the sea to snap at prey.

sections.Printed source:
Turn of Fortune's Wheel, Ch. 9, Glorium, Whirlwyrm Attack, p. 52. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/paitm/tofw/the-mosaic-mimir#WhirlwyrmAttack
Inherited rules from the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 324, Giant Crocodile. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2014/miscellaneous-creatures
sections.Traits: Hold Breath. The inherited stat block allows the eel to hold its breath for 30 minutes.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8, reach 5 ft. A hit on one target deals 21 (3d10 + 5) piercing damage and grapples it (escape DC 16). That target is restrained during the grapple, and the eel cannot Bite another target until it ends.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +8, reach 10 ft., against a target the eel is not grappling. On a hit deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit also makes a DC 16 Strength save and falls prone on a failure.
sections.Encounter ecology: These giant eels attack boats near the Ysgard maelstrom. A lone specimen can also appear at sea on the route to Grakenok.
sections.Encounter procedure: During the first attack, a DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check detects the two eels. The eels surprise the travelers and sailors if nobody notices them. An eel dives and flees at 10 HP or fewer. The Courier moves away 40 ft. each round, and an eel uses all but 10 ft. of movement to keep up. The lone encounter on p. 54 instead allows a DC 10 group Dexterity (Stealth) check to pass unnoticed.
sections.Source notes: The ordinary Whirlwyrm uses the Giant Crocodile block. The adventure’s separate elder Whirlwyrm uses Behir and belongs to the Monstrosity category.

name: Spotted Lion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +2. Natural armor. Perception +5. Stealth +6. Darkvision 60 ft.. Passive Perception 15. No languages listed.
appearance: A lion about twice the size of a common lion, with dusky fur and charcoal speckles on its coat and mane.

sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, Ch. 6, Bestiary, p. 177. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/3731048-spotted-lion
sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The lion has advantage on attacks against a creature if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of the target.
sections.Actions: Rend. Melee weapon attack, +8, reach 10 ft. A hit on one target deals 15 (2d8 + 6) piercing damage. If the lion moved straight toward it at least 20 ft. immediately before the hit, the target makes a DC 16 Strength save and falls prone on a failure. When the target is prone, the lion can Rend that target again as a bonus action.
sections.Encounter ecology: Prides hunt giant elk and mammoths. Stone and cloud giants also keep the cats as hunting companions.
sections.Source notes: The prone target qualifies the bonus attack even when it was already prone. The movement clause gates the save.

name: Titanothere
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
otherStatistics: Proficiency bonus +3. Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No languages listed.
appearance: An enormous rhinoceros relative. This individual has rugged folded hide and a broad branching nasal horn structure.

sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, Ch. 6, Bestiary, p. 185. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/3731056-titanothere
sections.Traits: Beast of Burden. Treat the titanothere as one size larger to determine carrying capacity.
sections.Actions: Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +10, reach 10 ft. A hit on one target deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage. If the titanothere moved straight toward it at least 20 ft. immediately before the hit, add 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit this way makes a DC 18 Strength save and falls prone on a failure.
sections.Encounter ecology: Titanotheres travel in herds and are irritable. They have many horn patterns and hide textures, including hornless, plated, and shaggy forms.
sections.Source notes: The charge rider adds damage to any target. Only a creature makes the Strength save.

name: Bristled Moorbounder
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A muscular, tusked hunter with rows of long blade-shaped bristles along its back and sides.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Explorer's Guide to Wildemount, March 2020 first printing, Wildemount Bestiary, Moorbounders, p. 295. https://fliphtml5.com/DnD5E/Explorers-Guide-To-Wildemount/Explorers_Guide_To_Wildemount/296/
sections.Traits:

Standing Leap. The moorbounder can long jump up to 40 ft. or high jump up to 20 ft. from a standstill or after a run.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Blades attack and one Claws attack.
Blades. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 14 (4d4 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: The bristled offshoot hunts in the marshes and muddy foothills of Xhorhas. Its sharp hide makes it a poor mount.
sections.Source notes: Wildemount labels the attack Claws. The later Call of the Netherdeep sheet uses Claw for the same roll.

name: Moorbounder
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A sleek, broad-chested hunting cat with long ivory tusks, powerful hind legs, and large clawed paws.

name: Old Croaker
otherStatistics: Immune to cold damage. Darkvision 30 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Explorer's Guide to Wildemount, March 2020 first printing, Frozen Sick, C5 Old Croaker's Pool, p. 240. https://fliphtml5.com/DnD5E/Explorers-Guide-To-Wildemount/Explorers_Guide_To_Wildemount/241/
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Old Croaker breathes air and water.
Standing Leap. With or without a run, it can long jump 20 ft. or high jump 10 ft.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 5 (1d10) poison damage and grapples the target, escape DC 13. Until the grapple ends, that target is restrained and Old Croaker can bite only that target.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack on a grappled target of Medium size or smaller. A hit ends the grapple and swallows the target. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside attacks and effects, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of Old Croaker’s turns. Old Croaker holds one swallowed target at once. When Old Croaker dies, the creature is no longer restrained and can move 5 ft. to emerge prone.
sections.Encounter ecology: Old Croaker lurks under the freezing pool in Croaker Cave. Hulil trained it to ferry visitors across the pool one at a time.
sections.Encounter application: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check can persuade Old Croaker to leave the party alone and carry the characters across individually.
sections.Source notes: The encounter changes the Giant Toad on Monster Manual p. 329 by granting cold damage immunity. D&D Beyond publishes this encounter variant as its own sheet.

appearance: A large toad with a broad mouth, warty back, and heavy hind legs.

name: Koi Prawn
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Journeys through the Radiant Citadel, June 2022 first printing, Salted Legacy, Battle Prawn Challenge, pp. 25–26. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/jttrc/salted-legacy
sections.Traits:
Charge. Moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hitting it with Ram on the same turn adds 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit this way makes a DC 11 Strength save or falls prone.
Water Breathing. The prawn breathes only underwater.
sections.Actions: Ram. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Four eight-foot prawns occupy a pool-sized glass tank in the Dyn Singh Night Market. The prawns defend themselves if damaged. They have half cover from attackers outside the water. Sid stops the challenge immediately if a prawn reduces a character to 0 HP. The sous-chefs rescue wounded participants.
sections.Source notes: The encounter on p. 26 directs the DM to use the Giant Sea Horse from Monster Manual p. 328. The art on p. 25 depicts the prawn, with the single specimen here on plain parchment.

appearance: An eight-foot jagged prawn with a segmented violet shell, cyan bands, long blue-violet antennae, and a spiny pointed rostrum.

name: Rooster
otherStatistics: Perception +4, passive Perception 14. No languages.

sections.Source notes: Uses the Hawk on Monster Manual p. 330 with its flying speed removed by the adventure.

appearance: A squat rust-brown grub with no wings, overlapping segments, short legs under the forebody, and prominent jaws.

sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save or takes 10 (3d6) poison damage. If this poison damage brings the target to 0 HP, it is stable, poisoned for 1 hour even after healing, and paralyzed while poisoned by this attack.

otherStatistics: Natural armor. Blindsight 30 ft. No languages.

description: A male peafowl with a blue crested head, blue neck, and an eyespotted green train.
appearance: A male peafowl with a blue crested head, blue neck, and an eyespotted green train.

sections.Traits:
Keen Sight and Smell. The peacock has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight or smell.
Pack Tactics. The peacock has advantage on attacks against targets within 5 ft. of a non-incapacitated ally of the peacock.
sections.Actions: Beak. Melee weapon attack +2, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 2 (1d4) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: Outer City Denizens result 7 has 1d4 commoners herding 2d8 goats and one peacock. The encounter uses the Vulture statistics unchanged.

name: Traxigor
description: A small brown otter in a red cassock.
appearance: A small brown otter in a red cassock.

sections.Printed source: Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus, Getting to Avernus, Traxigor’s Tower, p. 50. Uses Archmage from Monster Manual (2014), p. 342.
sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. Traxigor has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Spellcasting: Traxigor is an 18th-level Intelligence spellcaster with save DC 17 and +9 to hit with spell attacks. He casts Disguise Self and Invisibility at will. The prepared spells use the Archmage list with Plane Shift replacing Teleport. Cantrips are Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, and Shocking Grasp. Level 1, four slots: Detect Magic, Identify, Mage Armor, Magic Missile. Level 2, three slots: Detect Thoughts, Mirror Image, Misty Step. Level 3, three slots: Counterspell, Fly, Lightning Bolt. Level 4, three slots: Banishment, Fire Shield, Stoneskin. Level 5, three slots: Cone of Cold, Scrying, Wall of Force. Level 6, one slot: Globe of Invulnerability. Level 7, one slot: Plane Shift. Level 8, one slot: Mind Blank. Level 9, one slot: Time Stop. The Archmage block calls for Mage Armor, Stoneskin and Mind Blank before combat.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter: Traxigor’s otter form was made permanent by Wish. His tuning fork is keyed to the Nine Hells. He needs to recover it to take the group to Elturel with Plane Shift.

otherStatistics: AC 15 with Mage Armor. Resistance to damage from spells, and to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage while Stoneskin is active. Languages are Common, Draconic, Dwarvish, Gnomish, Halfling, and Troglodyte.

name: Enormous Tentacle
description: A single long green tentacle that tapers to a curved point.
appearance: A single long green tentacle that tapers to a curved point.

sections.Printed source: Acquisitions Incorporated, The Orrery of the Wanderer, area 8 Tentacle, pp. 93–94. Uses Giant Constrictor Snake from Monster Manual (2014), p. 324.
sections.Actions: Constrict. Melee weapon attack +6 against one creature anywhere in the room. Hit for 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage and grapple the creature, escape DC 16. The target is restrained while grappled. The tentacle can hold only one creature with this attack. It loses the Giant Constrictor Snake’s Bite.
sections.Encounter: The creature on the far side senses arrivals through tremors in the room. Each character makes a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice the water ripple before the tentacle appears. A character who knows the room’s story or detects the local magic gets advantage. Failure leaves the character surprised. On a grapple the tentacle immediately pulls the target into sewage 3 ft. deep. If the grapple persists on the following round, it pulls the target underwater in the 10-ft. section. It then has three-quarters cover, and the target cannot breathe. An unconscious target grappled underwater is pulled through the planar rupture and devoured.
sections.Source notes: The block uses Beast from the explicit combat proxy. The adventure leaves the creature on the other side unidentified. The snake’s normal movement is inherited data. The encounter depicts the appendage reaching through the rift and attacking within this room.

otherStatistics: Proxy blindsight 10 ft. The encounter’s unquantified tremorsense detects arrivals in the room. No languages.

name: Onyx
classification: Huge beast relative to the shrunken party, unaligned
speed: 400 ft., climb 200 ft. relative to the shrunken party
description: A brown domestic cat with bright blue eyes.
appearance: A brown domestic cat with bright blue eyes.

sections.Printed source: Acquisitions Incorporated, The Orrery of the Wanderer, Onyx Ascendant, pp. 185–187. Uses Cat from Monster Manual (2014), p. 320.
sections.Traits: Keen Smell. Onyx has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell. She also has advantage on all ability checks and saving throws during the encounter. Any incoming damage is reduced to 0.
sections.Actions: Claws. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit for 11 (2d10) slashing damage. Onyx attacks a random eligible character on her turn.
sections.Encounter: At the end of each character’s turn, roll on the printed Cat Chase Complications table. A hit against AC 12 makes contact without lasting damage. An attack or effect that would deal at least 10 damage gives Onyx disadvantage on attack rolls through the end of her next turn. Spell-imposed conditions end automatically at the end of her next turn. To end the chase, all living characters must hide. A passive Perception of 15 spots the mouse hole within view of the fireplace. A character looking for a ground-level hiding place can attempt a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check with advantage from anywhere in the room.
sections.Source notes: The adventure treats the cat as Huge relative to the shrunken characters. It explicitly gives climb 200 ft. even though multiplying the standard Cat’s 30-ft. climb by 10 gives 300 ft. The hit points come from the Cat block. The chase rules prevent damage from reducing them.

name: Bhaal, Ravager
publication: Minsc and Boo's Journal of Villainy
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Saves Str +16, Dex +14, Cha +9. Skills Athletics +16, Perception +10, Stealth +14. Resists necrotic. Immune to acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to charmed, exhaustion, frightened, incapacitated, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, stunned, and unconscious. Darkvision 120 ft., truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 20. Abyssal, Common, Primordial, and Undercommon.
appearance: Bhaal's huge, spined Beast avatar has a biting maw, claws, and a spiked carapace.

sections.Printed source: Minsc and Boo's Journal of Villainy, chapter 3, Campaign Villains, p. 95.
sections.Traits: Avatar of Bhaal. At 0 HP, the form breaks apart. The Slayer returns within 24 hours, 2d6 miles from the place the Ravager fell. Cull the Weak. After Ravager melee damage leaves a creature at 20 HP or less, it must pass a DC 21 Constitution save or fall to 0 HP. Immutable Form. Effects cannot change its form. Legendary Resistance, three per day. The Ravager can turn a failed save into a success. Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against magic. Magic Weapons. Claw, Bite, and Spines are magical attacks. Spiked Hide. At the start of the Ravager’s turn, any creature grappling it or in its grip takes 16 (3d10) piercing damage.
sections.Actions: Multiattack. Use the referenced Fear aura if available, then make one Bite and two Claws, or make two Spines attacks. Claw. +16 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 22 (3d8 + 9) slashing plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. Bite. +16 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 25 (3d10 + 9) piercing plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. A Large or smaller creature damaged by Bite is grappled, escape DC 20. While the grapple remains, the Ravager has no other Bite attack. When either hit damages a creature, it makes a DC 21 Constitution save. Failure subtracts the damage taken from its HP maximum until Greater Restoration or comparable magic removes the reduction. It dies if that maximum falls to 0. Spines. +14 to hit at 60/120 ft., one target. Deals 17 (3d6 + 7) piercing damage. A failed DC 19 Constitution save stuns the target through the end of its next turn.
sections.Legendary Actions: The Ravager has three legendary actions. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions when its own turn starts. Detect. Make a Wisdom (Perception) check. Smash. Creatures in a 10-ft. cube originating from the Ravager make DC 20 Constitution saves. Failure deals 36 (8d8) thunder damage and pushes a target 5 ft. Success halves the damage and prevents the push. The sound carries 100 ft. Spiky Carapace, costs two actions. The Ravager extends its spines. A creature that starts its turn within 5 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save or takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage, half on a success.
sections.Source notes: The 2021 Multiattack refers to a Fear aura with no rules in the block. Spiky Carapace has no stated end time. The separate Slayer avatar on p. 93 is Humanoid.

name: Deep Spider

The target makes a DC 14 Constitution save against 18 (4d8) poison damage, half on success. A target knocked to 0 HP by the poison is stable and poisoned for one hour, including after healing. It is paralyzed while that poisoning lasts. Foreleg. +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 19 (4d6 + 5) slashing damage.

sections.Source notes: The ecology prose describes leaps and restraint by sprayed webs, while the stat block defines no separate Leap or Web action.
