sections.Source notes: The ecology prose describes leaps and restraint by sprayed webs, while the stat block defines no separate Leap or Web action.

name: Rothé
otherStatistics: Darkvision 30 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages. Proficiency bonus +2.
appearance: A stocky horned rothé with a shaggy cattle build.

sections.Printed source: Chains of Asmodeus, chapter 2, The Nine Hells, Shadow of a Tyrant, p. 48.
sections.Actions: Gore. +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing. Add 7 (2d6) piercing if the rothé moved at least 20 ft. straight toward the target immediately before the hit.
sections.Encounter ecology: Herds stand on the River Styx shore. Ayperobos infest and control some cattle in Shadow of a Tyrant. The page gives no separate rules for those individual cattle.
sections.Source notes: Rothé in this printing has the Cattle tag and an explicit proficiency bonus. The encounter supplies no change to the herd’s anatomy.

name: Giant Canary
otherStatistics: Passive Perception 10. The block lists no languages. Proficiency bonus +2.
appearance: A living canary large enough to ride, with a stout songbird beak and yellow feathers in this portrait.

sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, chapter 2, Dragon Magic, Gold Canary Figurine of Wondrous Power, pp. 23–24.
sections.Actions: Peck. +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Figurine rules: Speak the command word as an action and throw the figurine to an unoccupied space within 60 ft. With room for the animal to appear, the living canary stays for up to eight hours and can be ridden. It is friendly to the user and companions, understands the user’s languages, and follows spoken commands. Without commands it defends itself. It returns to its statuette form when the time expires, when reduced to 0 HP, or when the user touches it and spends an action to speak the command word again. The canary can next be called at dawn.
sections.Source notes: The Beast block belongs to the figurine’s canary option. Its adult gold dragon option uses a separate Monster Manual profile.

name: Szikzith
publication: NERDS Restoring Harmony: A Web of Lies
appearance: An awakened, rust-brown giant wolf spider with a rounded abdomen swollen from eating honey.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Restoring Harmony: A Web of Lies, unnumbered sheet 6. The lair is on sheet 5.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. Szikzith can traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without a check.
Web Sense. While touching a web she can pinpoint creatures touching that web.
Web Walker. Webbing places no limits on her movement.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +3, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage. The creature makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 7 (2d6) poison on failure or half on success. If that poison reduces the creature to 0 HP, it stabilizes and remains poisoned for 1 hour, even if it regains HP. It is paralyzed for as long as that bite keeps it poisoned.
sections.Encounter ecology: Szikzith senses disturbances along the approach to the Beehive Room. On a failed DC 13 Dexterity check she either waits in ambush or investigates. A successful check gives Yellow surprise. She bargains for honey and can be outwitted with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Deception) check.
sections.Source notes: The stat block lists no languages. The encounter has Szikzith bargain with Yellow and leaves the language unspecified.

otherStatistics: Proficiency Bonus +2. Skills Perception +3, Stealth +7. Blindsight 10 ft. and darkvision 60 ft. Languages none in the stat block.

name: Sled Dog
appearance: A sturdy northern sled dog with a black-and-white double coat, pale blue eyes, and a leather pulling harness.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, The Rise of Tiamat (October 2014), Episode 2, p. 27. Use Wolf from the October 2014 Online Supplement, p. 26.
sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. The dog has advantage on Perception checks that depend on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. The dog has advantage on an attack against a creature within 5 ft. of one of the dog’s allies that is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Encounter ecology: Twelve sled dogs detect visitors who walk up the obvious path beside the ice chasm. Their barking and growling alerts the village. The Ice Hunters also rely on dogsleds over snow and ice.
sections.Source notes: This printing specifies the Wolf rules for the sled dogs. The encounter gives no adjustments to that block.

otherStatistics: Natural armor. Skills Perception +3, Stealth +4. Languages none.

name: Giant Spider
publication: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
appearance: A massive spider with long jointed legs, a round abdomen, and prominent fangs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club (2025), Appendix B, CR 1 Giant Spider.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The spider crosses difficult surfaces and ceilings without a check.
Web Walker. Webs do not slow the spider, which can find any creature that touches the same web.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee attack roll +5, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Web (Recharge 5–6). One creature the spider can see within 60 ft. makes a DC 13 Dexterity save. Failure restrains it until the web breaks. The web has AC 10 and 5 HP. It is vulnerable to fire and immune to poison and psychic damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Itsy hides above the den in D5 and attacks when visitors open the secret door or touch the crystal spider. Bitsy attacks upon seeing visitors in the mirror den at S5.
sections.Source notes: This scope is the CR 1 Giant Spider used for Itsy and Bitsy. The official index also lists a separate CR 6 version.

otherStatistics: Initiative +3 (13). Proficiency Bonus +2. Skills Perception +4, Stealth +7. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages none.

name: Swarm of Infesting Insects
classification: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, unaligned
otherStatistics: Initiative +2 (12). Proficiency bonus +2. Blindsight 30 ft.. Passive Perception 8. No languages. No treasure.
appearance: Olive-green, segmented insect larvae with rust-red heads mingle with darker adults with translucent wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Ravenloft: The Horrors Within, chapter 5, Denizens of the Mists, Swarms of Insects, digital export sheets 400–401 of 444. https://www.scribd.com/document/1054815014/Ravenloft-The-Horrors-Within-Neat-and-Tidy-Edition-1
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned
sections.Traits: Swarm. The swarm and other creatures can share a space. It can move through openings that admit a Tiny creature. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.
sections.Actions: Infestation. Melee attack roll +4, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 12 (4d4 + 2) poison damage, or 7 (2d4 + 2) if the swarm is Bloodied. The target becomes Poisoned. If this poison is still active after 1 hour, the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save. A success ends the condition. On a failure, roll 1d6. On 1–2 the target becomes Blinded, on 3–4 its maximum HP drops by 5 (1d10), and on 5–6 it gains 1 Exhaustion level. The rolled effect ends when this poison ends.
sections.Encounter ecology: A hidden coffin at the Von Zarovich Sanctuary releases one infesting swarm alongside a Vampire Nosferatu. Both fight to the death.
sections.Source notes: The digital export numbers these sheets 400–401. A secondary index gives printed p. 271 for the pair. The physical folio was not available to verify. The initial attack applies Poisoned on a hit. The save takes place an hour later if that condition persists. The block gives no repeat interval.

classification: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, unaligned
otherStatistics: Initiative +2 (12). Proficiency bonus +2. Tremorsense 60 ft.. Passive Perception 11. No languages. No treasure.
appearance: Olive-green, segmented insect larvae with rust-red heads mingle with darker adults with translucent wings.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Ravenloft: The Horrors Within, chapter 5, Denizens of the Mists, Swarms of Insects, digital export sheets 400–401 of 444. https://www.scribd.com/document/1054815014/Ravenloft-The-Horrors-Within-Neat-and-Tidy-Edition-1

Swarm. The swarm and other creatures can share a space. It can move through openings that admit a Tiny creature. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.
sections.Actions: Ravenous Bites. Melee attack roll +4, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 20 (4d8 + 2) piercing damage, or 11 (2d8 + 2) if the swarm is Bloodied. The insects burrow into the target and Poison it for 1 minute. A spell or effect that restores the target’s HP ends the condition early. At the start of each turn while Poisoned this way, the target takes 4 (1d8) piercing damage. It dies if this ongoing damage reduces it to 0 HP.
sections.Encounter ecology: A roll of 4 on the Trial of Hearts Jungle Events table in Valachan brings four ravenous swarms.
sections.Source notes: The digital export numbers these sheets 400–401. A secondary index gives printed p. 271 for the pair. The physical folio was not available to verify. The bite gives no saving throw. Death at 0 HP is specific to the ongoing damage. The artwork shows winged adults, but neither profile lists a fly speed.

name: Pandarian Dragon Turtle
appearance: A large dragon turtle used as a mount. The existing portrait shows a broad armored shell and a horned head on plain parchment.
otherStatistics: Initiative +1 (11). Proficiency bonus +2. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

sections.Printed source: D&D: World of Warcraft, Chapter 3, Mounts and Vehicles. Digital stat block.
sections.Traits: Amphibious. The turtle breathes in air and underwater.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee attack roll, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by the bite is Grappled, escape DC 13.
sections.Source notes: The publisher’s contents page locates the block in Chapter 3. The public image of the digital block has no folio. The upstream catalog lists p. 104.
